entries.name: Alaska Child Support Services Division (CSSD/CSED)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide child support (and court-ordered spousal support processed through the state disbursement unit)
entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: Agency is in the Alaska Department of Revenue, 550 W 7th Ave, Suite 310, Anchorage AK 99501. Client (Obligor) Portal Guide PDF on the Information page explains making payments in the ACSESS client portal.

entries.name: Alaska Court System - fines, bail and minor offenses
entries.service_area_detail: State court system: traffic tickets, fines, court costs, restitution and payment plans (county/municipal courts may use their own portals)
entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: 'Search Cases / Payments' page; bail can be paid online: https://courts.alaska.gov/trialcourts/bail.htm.

entries.name: Alaska LIHEAP - Heating Assistance Program (HAP) (Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance)
entries.parent_company: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; administered by the State Division of Public Assistance (some tribal organizations run their own programs)
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior program; seniors apply with the same application. The new application is available after September 1, so older adults can apply early and be ready when benefits start Oct 1.
entries.notes: Two programs: LIHEAP for income up to 150% of federal poverty guidelines, and the state-funded Alaska Affordable Heating Program (AAHP) for income above 150% up to 225%. One benefit per season. Heating Assistance applications accepted Oct 1 - Apr 30 (September applications processed, paid from Oct 1); one-time payment credited to your heating fuel or electric vendor. Crisis Assistance: applications Sep 1 - Jun 30 for households out of heating fuel or within 48 hours of running out, or with heat/electric service disconnected or about to be. Apply online through the Alaska Connect Portal, in person, by mail, or by drop box at any Public Assistance office. Virtual Contact Center 1-800-478-7778 (Alaska Relay 711).

entries.name: Alaska Medicaid Estate Recovery (Department of Health)
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Official DPA Adult LTC manual section 507 Estate Recovery  describes OBRA-93 recovery for 55+ nursing facility/HCBS costs and the spouse/minor/disabled-child exemptions; no recovery-unit phone or payment address is published there. Use the contact on the claim notice.

entries.name: Alaska Regulatory Commission of Alaska (RCA) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; RCA-regulated electric, gas and other utilities
entries.senior_programs: If the utility has been told a household member is seriously ill, elderly, has a disability, or depends on life-support equipment, it must give at least 30 days' written notice before disconnection (instead of 15) - 3 AAC 52.450(c)(2). Tell the utility right away about such a household member.
entries.notes: Alaska has no winter or temperature-based shutoff moratorium. Disconnection requires at least 15 days' written notice and may be done only Monday 8 a.m. through Thursday 5 p.m.; never on a Friday or the day before a holiday (3 AAC 52.450). You can ask the utility for a deferred payment agreement, dispute the reason for disconnection, and pay only the undisputed amount while a dispute is investigated. Contact the utility first, then the RCA Consumer Protection section: 1-800-390-2782 or 907-276-6222 (Anchorage), TTY 907-276-4533, email rca.mail@alaska.gov or cp.mail@alaska.gov.

entries.name: Alaska Senior Benefits Program
entries.parent_company: Alaska Department of Health, Division of Public Assistance
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; Alaskans 65+ under income limits
entries.notes: Included so Alaska seniors searching for state Rx help find it.

entries.name: Alaska Weatherization Assistance Program (Alaska Housing Finance Corporation)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by regional weatherization service providers and housing authorities
entries.notes: Free weatherization for homeowners and renters who meet AHFC income limits. Check the income limits, then contact the weatherization service provider for your area (residents of homes owned by a regional housing authority contact that authority). Homes never weatherized before get higher priority. AHFC headquarters 907-338-6100 or 1-800-478-2432 (toll-free in Alaska).

entries.name: Alabama DHR Child Support Enforcement Division (payments)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide child support (and court-ordered spousal support processed through the state disbursement unit)
entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: Payment Information page lists ExpertPay (www.expertpay.com) and MoneyGram as payment methods; online payment information website mydhropi.alabama.gov shows payment history/arrearage balances. ExpertPay and MoneyGram; mydhropi.alabama.gov requires creating an account; 24-hour voice response 1-800-284-4347 gives payment and arrears balance.

entries.name: Alabama LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs)
entries.parent_company: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by regional community action agencies (ADECA does not take applications)
entries.senior_programs: Households with a member age 60+, a member with a documented disability, or a child under 18 are treated as vulnerable and get priority. Local agencies hold early application periods, including appointment days for older adults at senior centers. High-need households (elderly or disabled members) may get an extra $50 on their benefit.
entries.notes: Apply through the community action agency for your county; use ADECA's regional map/contact list to find it (ADECA itself does not schedule appointments or process applications). Income limit: household income at or below 150% of the federal poverty level, based on gross income for the month before you apply. Season typically runs: heating and winter crisis Oct 1 - Apr 30; cooling and summer crisis May 1 - Sep 30. Crisis assistance is for households facing a shutoff notice, disconnection, or no fuel; it is handled by the same local agency and is usually resolved within 48 hours (18 hours if life-threatening). Bring proof of income for every household member for the prior month, plus your energy bill.

entries.name: Alabama Medicaid Estate Recovery Unit
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Estate Notice Office (probate estates) (334) 242-4097/4098, estatenotice@medicaid.alabama.gov; Estate Recovery Unit estaterecovery@medicaid.alabama.gov. A Hardship Waiver Application is available. Estate Recovery Unit email estaterecovery@medicaid.alabama.gov; the page links a Hardship Waiver Application PDF. The Estate Recovery page links FAQs (English and Spanish) and the Hardship Waiver Application. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Alabama Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PSC-regulated electric, gas, water and telecom utilities (not most city utilities or co-ops)
entries.senior_programs: PSC General Rule 12(E) requires each utility to have tariff rules for customers who need special consideration because of age or handicap, or when life or health may be threatened by a shutoff. Ask your utility about its medical-certificate and senior protections (for example, winter protection plans for customers 65+) before the shutoff date.
entries.notes: No residential electric or natural gas shutoff for nonpayment on a day the National Weather Service forecasts 32 degrees F or below for your location (PSC General Rule 12(B)(5)). There is no date-based winter moratorium and no summer heat rule. Utilities must give at least 5 days' written notice before disconnecting; no shutoff after 3:30 p.m. before a day the utility office is closed. Each utility office must have someone who can extend payment deadlines and set up installment plans. Contact the utility first; if unresolved, call the PSC Consumer Services Section at 1-800-392-8050 or 334-242-5211 (Mon-Fri 8-5), use the online complaint form, or write to PO Box 304260, Montgomery, AL 36130.

entries.senior_programs: Priority goes to elderly people, people with disabilities, and families with children.
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency repairs (insulation, air sealing, heating/cooling fixes) chosen after an energy audit of the home. Income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Apply through your regional community action agency listed on the ADECA weatherization page; ADECA does not take applications. Homeowner/landlord must agree to the work recommended by the audit.

entries.name: Trinity Health PACE
entries.service_area_detail: 15 owned/managed PACE programs with 25 centers in 12 states (program names include Mercy LIFE, LIFE St. Joseph of the Pines, Saint Francis LIFE and Trinity Health PACE of Pensacola)

entries.senior_programs: PACE: typically no cost for people with Medicaid (or Medicare and Medicaid); people over Medicaid income/asset limits pay a flat monthly fee; people without Medicare or Medicaid can pay privately.
entries.notes: Added as one of the largest PACE operators (about-us page: 15 programs, 25 centers, 12 states, 3,000+ participants). The FAQ explains that payment depends on Medicare/Medicaid eligibility, over-limit participants pay a monthly fee, others may pay privately, and participants can be personally responsible for unauthorized out-of-program services. No online bill-pay page.

entries.name: Arkansas DHS Medicaid Estate Recovery (Third Party Liability Unit - Decedents' Estates)
entries.phone_customer_service: 501-682-1001 (DHS main line; no unit line published)
entries.mail_payment_address: Arkansas DHS, Third Party Liability Unit, Attention: Decedents' Estates, P.O. Box 1437, Slot S296, Little Rock, AR 72203-1437
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Still no estate recovery web page on humanservices.arkansas.gov (site search returned none). The official Arkansas Medical Services Policy Manual is published as Code of Arkansas Rules 20 CAR pt. 500 (webftp.blr.arkansas.gov PDF; version 9.1.2026). Section H-600 covers recovery from people 55+ who got nursing-facility, ICF/IID or HCBS waiver care, and from people of any age who were permanently institutionalized. There is no recovery while a spouse, a child under 21 or a blind/disabled child survives, when recovery would cause undue hardship, or when it is not cost-effective. Beneficiary-deed interests are exempt (Act 570 of 2021). Section H-730 (6/1/2025): the personal representative or distributee may request a hardship waiver within 35 days of the DHS notice by mailing a statement with supporting documents to the TPL Unit address. Factors include a sole income-producing asset, the heir becoming benefit-eligible, a home valued at 50% or less of the county average, and other compelling circumstances. Payment instructions come with the DHS notice of intent to recover. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Arkansas Judiciary - Pay Traffic Tickets

entries.name: Arkansas LIHEAP - Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Arkansas Energy Office)
entries.parent_company: Arkansas Department of Energy and Environment, Arkansas Energy Office (AEO)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide (all 75 counties); applications taken by local community-based organizations (CBOs), not by AEO
entries.senior_programs: Local agencies may start serving priority households (members who are elderly or disabled, or children under 6) up to 30 days before the regular heating and cooling seasons open, so older adults should call their CBO in early December and early June.
entries.notes: Apply through the community-based organization for your county (find it on the AEO CBO network map); AEO does not process applications and never charges a fee. Applications are first-come, first-served, typically January through April 30 (heating; opens the first Monday after New Year's) and July through September 30 (cooling; opens the first Monday after July 4). Crisis help (prevent disconnection, restore service, or deliver fuel when you are out) is available during both seasons through the same CBO. Income limit: 60% of state median income (150% of poverty for 8+ person households); see AEO's income eligibility chart. Bring ID, proof of household income, and your energy bill. AEO public inquiries: 1-888-233-0326 or 501-682-0744.

MyCase (mycase.ocse.arkansas.gov) takes card or eCheck as a one-time payment or on a recurring schedule and shows payment history; cancel/modify recurring payments in MyCase or call the Clearinghouse 1-866-428-8382.

entries.name: Arkansas Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; APSC-regulated electric, gas, telephone and larger water utilities
entries.senior_programs: Customers 65 or older or handicapped: utilities must identify them, contact them personally about a delinquency, and help connect them to social service agencies; gas or electric service cannot be cut off to them when 95 degrees F or higher is forecast in the next 24 hours. Medical certificate: a physician certifying a medical emergency can postpone shutoff up to 30 days (the utility provides the form; the doctor must return it within 7 days). Customers can name a third party (relative or caregiver) to receive shutoff notices.
entries.notes: Cold weather rule: no residential gas or electric shutoff when the forecast calls for 32 degrees F or lower at any time in the next 24 hours. Hot weather rule: no shutoff at 95 degrees F or higher forecast for customers 65+ or handicapped (and gas customers whose only gas use is air conditioning). Ask your gas utility about winter payment protections for low-income households (Nov-Mar). Utilities must give at least 5 days' written notice (3 more days if mailed); if a social service agency guarantees at least 25% of the overdue amount, shutoff can be delayed. If you dispute a bill and tell the utility, service should not be cut off during the complaint, but pay the undisputed part. Contact the utility first, then APSC Consumer Services: 1-800-482-1164 or 501-682-1718 (Mon-Fri 8-4:30), online contact form, or mail to P.O. Box 400, Little Rock, AR 72203-0400.

entries.name: Arkansas Weatherization Assistance Program (Arkansas Energy Office)
entries.parent_company: Arkansas Department of Energy and Environment, Arkansas Energy Office (AEO)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local community action agencies and nonprofits
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency improvements based on a computerized energy audit. Eligible if household income is at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines, or automatically if a member receives SSI or the household receives (or is eligible for) LIHEAP. Apply with the local provider for the county where the home is located. Bring household income documents, ID, and the last 12 months of utility bills.

entries.name: Dollar Energy Fund (utility hardship grants)

entries.notes: Hardship grants paid directly to a participating utility for limited-income customers. Steps: check with your utility that it partners with Dollar Energy Fund, then apply online at MyApp Connect or through a local community agency (Agency Finder: hardshiptools.org/AgencyFinder.aspx). Have your utility bill and proof of income for every household member. First come, first served while funds last. Utility assistance line 1-888-282-6816; office 412-431-2800.

Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: Official ALTCS Estate Recovery brochure DE-810 (rev 07/2026): AHCCCS Third Party Liability Office 602-345-1466; HMS Phoenix 602-954-8380, out-of-state toll-free 1-888-378-2836. Covers liens, statutory exemptions, undue-hardship waiver and partial reduction; grievances to AHCCCS Office of General Counsel, P.O. Box 6050, Mail Drop 15013, Phoenix, AZ 85002-5520 within 60 days. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Arizona Corporation Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; ACC-regulated utilities such as APS, TEP, UNS and regulated co-ops (not SRP or city utilities)
entries.senior_programs: No age-specific rule, but a utility may not shut off a customer unable to pay if a licensed medical practitioner documents, renewed every year, that shutoff would be especially dangerous to the health of someone in the home or that medically necessary equipment depends on the service (A.A.C. R14-2-211). Customers can name a third party (such as an adult child or caregiver) to receive delinquency and shutoff notices; the utility must notify them and give them at least 5 business days to act.
entries.notes: Summer heat protection: electric utilities must either stop shutoffs for nonpayment June 1 - October 15 or stop them on days forecast above 95 degrees F or at/below 32 degrees F (R14-2-211). APS, TEP and UNS Electric have chosen the June 1 - October 15 moratorium; regulated co-ops have their own tariffs. Bills still accrue during the moratorium, so keep paying what you can. Before shutting off a customer unable to pay, the utility must tell them about assistance agencies. Contact the utility first, then file a complaint online with the ACC or call Consumer Services: 1-800-222-7000 (in-state), 602-542-4251 (Phoenix), 520-628-6550 (Tucson).

entries.name: Arizona LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Arizona Department of Economic Security)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide (non-tribal); apply online with DES, with help from local Community Action Agencies; tribal nations run separate tribal LIHEAP programs
entries.senior_programs: Households with a member 60 or older (also disabled members, veterans, and children 6 and under) get extra points that raise priority and benefit amount. The DES Senior Utility Assistance Program (SUAP) lets eligible older adults recertify with a shorter application and guarantees the maximum benefit on the benefit chart; returning elderly participants can pre-register for priority.
entries.notes: Income limit: up to 60% of state median income (150% of poverty for households of 10+). Benefits: up to about $640 standard plus up to $500 crisis assistance once per 12 months. The state-funded Power AZ program uses the same application and extends help to households up to 100% of state median income. Assistance is year-round: heating season Nov 1 (Dec 1 in warmer counties) - Mar 31, cooling season Apr 1 - Oct 31 (Nov 30 in warmer counties). Apply online through the DES portal; a paper application is available for those who cannot apply online. Local Community Action Agencies (community navigators) help with applications. Questions or help applying: LIHEAP service line 1-866-494-1981. Have your utility bill, ID, and proof of income for all household members ready.

entries.name: Arizona Weatherization Assistance Program (Arizona Department of Housing)

entries.senior_programs: Elderly households (age 60+) are a priority group.
entries.notes: Free home energy repairs for households at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines, or anyone receiving SSI. Find your county's weatherization provider on the ADOH page (provider list by county) and contact them to apply. Bring proof of income for the prior year (pay stubs, Social Security statements).

entries.name: California DFPI PACE program administrator complaints
entries.parent_company: California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation
entries.service_area_detail: Licenses and regulates CA PACE administrators: Renew Financial (CaliforniaFIRST), PACE Funding Group (Home Run), FortiFi, Ygrene.
entries.senior_programs: California: before signing, the PACE administrator must do a recorded live oral confirmation call of key terms with the owner (no prerecorded calls) and verify ability to pay. Owners 65+ have 5 business days (not 3) to cancel a PACE contract signed on/after 1/1/2021. Report abuse to CA DFPI 866-275-2677.
entries.notes: File a PACE complaint online at dfpi.ca.gov/submit-a-complaint/, by phone 866-275-2677, email financialservices@dfpi.ca.gov, or mail DFPI Financial Services/California Financing Law, 320 W 4th St Ste 750, Los Angeles CA 90013. Paper PACE complaint forms (DFPI-801C) allow attaching documents. Free legal aid groups (e.g., Bet Tzedek, Bay Area Legal Aid, HERA, Public Counsel) help PACE victims. Financing is capped at 15% of home value up to $700,000.

entries.service_area_detail: Statewide California
entries.senior_programs: Seniors qualify through Medi-Cal, CalFresh, SSI, Section 8, veterans benefits, or income (from June 1, 2026: $24,600 for 1 person, $33,300 for 2).
entries.notes: Discount of up to $19/month on one home phone or cell phone line, up to $39 off connection, and exemption from some surcharges/taxes; pilot gives up to $20/month for standalone broadband or $30 for bundled. Apply by calling a participating phone company and asking for California LifeLine; you pay regular rates until approved, then get retroactive credit. Renew every year (renewal forms come in a pink envelope). LifeLine Call Center 1-866-272-0349 (Mon-Fri 7 a.m.-7 p.m. PT); Administrator 1-877-858-7463; complaints/appeals 1-800-649-7570. Combines with federal Lifeline.

entries.name: California LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) and Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP) (California Department of Community Services and Development)
entries.parent_company: California Department of Community Services and Development (CSD)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by local service providers (community action agencies and nonprofits) by city/county
entries.senior_programs: Because funding is limited, local providers give priority to particularly vulnerable households, which includes older adults and people with disabilities; tell the provider if anyone in the home is 60+, disabled, or uses medical equipment.
entries.notes: Three parts: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) one-time payment toward your utility bill; Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP) for households in crisis, such as a 24-48 hour disconnect notice, service already shut off, or a dangerous appliance; and LIHEAP Weatherization. Help is available year-round while funds last; some eligible households may not get a benefit in a given year. Income limit: 60% of state median income. Apply with the local service provider for your city or county (use CSD's Find Services in Your Area tool, choose Energy Bill Assistance) or call the CSD toll-free help line 1-866-675-6623 for where to apply. Bring a recent utility bill, ID, and proof of household income. Also ask your utility about CARE (about 30-35% off electric, 20% off gas) and Medical Baseline.

entries.name: California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; CPUC-regulated investor-owned utilities such as PG&E, SCE, SDG&E and SoCalGas (not city utilities like LADWP or SMUD)
entries.senior_programs: Customers 65 or older or dependent adults can sign up for third-party notification: a relative or caregiver gets past-due and shutoff notices (Public Utilities Code 779.1). If a licensed physician certifies that shutoff would be life-threatening and the customer cannot pay, the utility may not disconnect as long as the customer agrees to pay the balance over up to 12 months (PU Code 779). Utilities also have Medical Baseline and life-support/critical-care registration; sign up with your utility in advance.
entries.notes: No shutoff for nonpayment when the forecast is 32 degrees F or below, or 100 degrees F or above, within the next 72 hours (CPUC Decision 20-06-003). Utilities must give at least 19 days after the bill is mailed plus a 10-day delinquency notice, and must try to reach you by phone or in person at least 24 hours before shutoff (or post a 48-hour notice). You can ask to pay a past-due balance over time; service cannot be cut off while a bill dispute is being investigated or while you keep up with an approved payment plan. Call the utility first; if unresolved, call CPUC Consumer Affairs at 1-800-649-7570 or file an informal complaint online (no in-person complaints).

entries.name: California Weatherization Assistance Program (California Department of Community Services and Development)
entries.parent_company: California Department of Community Services and Development (CSD)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local service providers
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency upgrades and health-and-safety repairs for low-income households through LIHEAP Weatherization and the U.S. Department of Energy Weatherization Assistance Program (see CSD's DOE income guidelines). Use Find Services in Your Area to locate your provider and apply with them, or call 1-866-675-6623. CSD's Low-Income Weatherization Program (LIWP) separately offers no-cost solar and efficiency upgrades for farmworker and multifamily affordable housing.

Citations page: Administrative Review must be requested first to contest (attach photos/permits); pay by mail, in person at City Hall lobby (411 W. Ocean Blvd) or online via the Citation Processing Center search page; phone (562) 570-6822.

entries.name: City of Sacramento parking citations

Low Income Payment Plan: for California-registered vehicles; request an application at paymentplanparking@sandiego.gov or 1-619-744-1702; if approved, late fees and penalties are waived.

entries.name: Consumer Credit Counseling Foundation, Inc.
entries.service_area_detail: HQ Livermore, CA; UST-approved for: Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia and others
entries.phone_customer_service: Existing clients only 1-800-656-6207 (office 7am-5pm PT); new client inquiry 800-918-6709 / 800-359-1561; info@cccfusa.org

View DMP deposits/creditor disbursements in the client login; to change or stop the monthly deposit or cancel the DMP, call the existing-client line. Approved by the U.S. Trustee Program to give pre-bankruptcy credit counseling. Many UST-approved agencies only sell bankruptcy counseling/education courses and do not run monthly debt management plans - confirm before assuming a DMP exists. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general.

entries.name: LADOT Parking Citations (City of Los Angeles)

entries.notes: Parking ticket (no autopay; one-time payments). Pay online, by phone, app, mail or in person; Visa/Mastercard $2 processing fee. Contest a citation online. LA offers low-income and indigent payment plans/community service options (see LADOT). Late penalties accrue if payment is not received by the due date (CVC 40309).

entries.name: WelbeHealth PACE

entries.name: FortiFi Financial

entries.senior_programs: California: before signing, the PACE administrator must do a recorded live oral confirmation call of key terms with the owner (no prerecorded calls) and verify ability to pay. Owners 65+ have 5 business days (not 3) to cancel a PACE contract signed on/after 1/1/2021. Report abuse to CA DFPI 866-275-2677.
entries.notes: Paid as a line item on the county property tax bill. Payoff quotes and balances are handled by DTA: 800-969-4382 or poportal.com ($50 fee, credited if you prepay; about 5 business days). DTA email for CA assessments FortiFi@financedta.com; FL assessments info@FloridaPACE.gov. FortiFi: 858-345-2000 or 888-399-2819, info@fortifi.com, Mon-Fri 10am-6pm ET; 12770 High Bluff Dr Ste 260, San Diego CA 92130. Financing complaints by email to FortiFi compliance (include owner names, address, assessment number); about 30-day response. Installation problems go to the contractor.

entries.name: Renew Financial (CaliforniaFIRST)
entries.service_area_detail: CaliforniaFIRST residential PACE through CSCDA in California; Florida residential PACE through Florida Green Finance Authority.
entries.senior_programs: California: before signing, the PACE administrator must do a recorded live oral confirmation call of key terms with the owner (no prerecorded calls) and verify ability to pay. Owners 65+ have 5 business days (not 3) to cancel a PACE contract signed on/after 1/1/2021. Report abuse to CA DFPI 866-275-2677.
entries.notes: Assessment is billed on the county property tax bill (pay with taxes or via mortgage escrow). Payoff/prepayment: call 844-736-3934 (CA) or for Florida 844-589-7953 / prepayments@renewfinancial.com; online request form linked from CSCDA's PACE page (needs proof of ownership such as deed or closing papers; POA if a caregiver submits). Prepay in full or in $2,500 increments; no prepayment penalty, a processing fee may apply. PACE Hardship Program: for temporary hardship (medical illness, death, disaster, job loss) causing you to fall behind on property taxes or the tax/escrow part of the mortgage.

entries.name: Finance DTA (David Taussig & Associates) PACE Property Owner Portal
entries.service_area_detail: Third-party assessment administrator for HERO (CA/MO), FortiFi, PACE Funding/Home Run, Florida PACE Funding Agency and other PACE districts.
entries.notes: Payoff or paydown statements can only be requested through the Property Owner Portal (staff will walk callers through it). Free estimated balance online (not a payoff figure). Statements take up to 5 business days; a $50 calculation fee is charged and credited back if you prepay; extra payment-instruction requests cost $50 each. Payoff is paid by check or wire to the government agency, not through the portal. After full payment the lien is released within about 120 days; paid by June 30 means no PACE charge on the next fiscal year tax bill. Balance updates within 4 weeks of payment. Other phone seen for HERO: 949-955-1500.

entries.name: Willdan Financial Services (PACE payoff quotes)
entries.service_area_detail: Payoff servicer for Ygrene projects and legacy Show Me PACE residential assessments.
entries.notes: Full payoff quotes online at wfspayoffquotes.com (small upfront fee; about 2 business days). Partial payoff or questions: 866-807-6864, POSR@Willdan.com. Request at least 2 weeks before closing a sale or refinance.

entries.name: Home Run Financing (PACE Funding Group)

Customer service 844-USE-PACE (844-873-7223), info@homerunfinancing.com, 7 days 6:30am-8:30pm PT; bilingual line 800-231-6991. 750 University Ave Ste 140, Los Gatos CA 95032. For a payoff have the assessment ID, owner name/address and closing date ready.

entries.name: Renovate America HERO (legacy, in bankruptcy)

entries.notes: Renovate America no longer services HERO. California or Missouri HERO: Finance DTA 949-955-1500 / poportal.com. Florida HERO: Florida Development Finance Corp 888-338-3578 (prepayments at paymypace.com). Bankruptcy notice questions: RAIInquiries@Stretto.com. The HERO charge stays on the property tax bill until paid off.

entries.name: Collection Bureau of America (CBA)
entries.service_area_detail: Collector (Hayward, CA) for medical, utility and consumer accounts, mainly in California. CFPB complaints since 2023: 292.
entries.mail_payment_address: Collection Bureau of America, P.O. Box 5013, Hayward, CA 94540.
entries.notes: Scam check: never pay a caller you cannot verify - look up the collector's number yourself (not from the call/text), ask for the written validation notice, and compare with CFPB 'debt collector or scammer?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-can-i-tell-if-a-caller-is-a-debt-collector-or-a-scammer-en-1699/ and FTC 'Fake and abusive debt collectors' https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/fake-abusive-debt-collectors. Dispute/validation: under the FDCPA/Reg F you can dispute in writing within the 30-day validation period and the collector must pause collection until it sends verification (CFPB rights: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/debt-collection/answers/know-your-rights/ ). Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). Complaints: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/.

entries.name: DebtWave Credit Counseling
entries.service_area_detail: Escondido/San Diego, CA; nationwide by phone. NFCC member; UST-approved.
entries.notes: Login goes to a Client Support Software-hosted extranet. Call for deposit changes or cancellation. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/. Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. DMP FAQ says to cancel, contact DebtWave at (888) 686-4040 so they can review upcoming debits, payments in process, enrolled creditors and funds on the account; fees are a one-time set-up fee plus monthly service fee that vary by state.

entries.name: Colorado Family Support Registry (FSR)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide child support (and court-ordered spousal support processed through the state disbursement unit)
entries.mail_payment_address: Family Support Registry, P.O. Box 2171, Denver, CO 80201-2171
entries.payment_processor: SMART e-Pay (Systems & Methods Inc.) co.smartchildsupport.com; MoneyGram; payment kiosks
entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: Make a Payment page: online account, credit card site, Pay by Text (one-time or recurring card), Apple Pay/Google Pay/PayPal/Venmo, MoneyGram, free Recurring Automatic Withdrawal (RAW), and payment records requests. PayNearMe discontinued after 10/31/2024. SMART portal co.smartchildsupport.com (electronic payment free); Recurring Automatic Withdrawal (RAW) registration free in the online account; phone payments need a PIN and can be scheduled up to 30 days ahead; payment history in the online account or by email cdhs_fsrcustomerservice@state.co.us. RAW cancellation not described - call 800-374-6558.

entries.name: Colorado HCPF Medicaid Estate Recovery Program (HMS/Gainwell)
entries.parent_company: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy & Financing (administered by HMS/Gainwell)
entries.mail_payment_address: Colorado Recovery Unit, 333 W. Hampden Ave., Suite #425, Englewood, CO 80110
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: Local (303) 837-8293; email coestaterecovery@gainwelltechnologies.com; document portal submissions.hms.com. FAQ covers hardship waiver/compromise and heirs keeping property by paying the claim. No online pay page published. The debt is enforceable only after the client's death; heirs may ask the Department to waive or compromise recovery for hardship (Department's discretion). The Department may place a lien on property while the recipient is alive, which is paid when the property is sold. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Colorado Judicial Branch - Online Payments
entries.service_area_detail: State court system: traffic tickets, fines, court costs, restitution and payment plans (county/municipal courts may use their own portals)
entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: Colorado Judicial Online Payments (state courts; Denver County Court is separate).

entries.name: Colorado LIHEAP - Low-income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) (Colorado Department of Human Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications processed by county human services departments
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior LEAP window. Coloradans 65+ (or disabled, or surviving spouses 58+) with low income can also claim the state Property Tax/Rent/Heat Rebate (form 104PTC, Colorado Department of Revenue), which includes a heat-expense rebate of up to $192.
entries.notes: LEAP season runs Nov 1 - Apr 30 (2026-27 season: Nov 1, 2026 - Apr 30, 2027); applications accepted only in that window. Income limit: 60% of state median income (e.g., about $3,774/month gross for 1 person, $4,936 for 2 in 2026-27). Helps with heating bills (winter crisis help up to $1,000) and repair or replacement of a broken primary heating system such as a furnace or wood stove (not portable heaters); the Crisis Intervention Program for heating-system repair runs year-round. Apply online through Colorado PEAK starting Nov 1, or download/pick up a paper application and mail or email it to your county human services office. Use the LEAP checklist: answer every question, include proof of income and lawful-presence documents for household members born outside the U.S., and a recent utility bill. Heating emergency or help outside the season: 1-866-HEAT-HELP (1-866-432-8435). Energy Outreach Colorado also offers year-round emergency bill help through local agencies.

entries.name: Colorado Public Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies, Public Utilities Commission (PUC)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; PUC-regulated utilities such as Xcel Energy, Black Hills Energy and Atmos Energy (not municipal utilities or most electric co-ops)
entries.senior_programs: Medical certificate: a utility must postpone electric shutoff for 90 days from the date of a medical certificate from a Colorado-licensed physician or qualified health care practitioner stating that shutoff would aggravate or create a medical emergency for the customer or a permanent household member; usable once in any 12 months (4 CCR 723-3, Rule 3407). Use the 90 days to set up a payment plan.
entries.notes: No electric shutoff for nonpayment when the National Weather Service morning forecast predicts 32 degrees F or lower, or 95 degrees F or higher, in the next 24 hours (Rule 3407). Shutoffs only between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. Monday-Thursday (generally before noon), and not from noon the day before through 8 a.m. the day after a holiday or office closure. There is no date-based winter moratorium. Ask the utility for an installment payment plan. Contact the utility first, then PUC Consumer Assistance: 1-800-456-0858 (outside Denver) or 303-894-2070, email dora_puc_complaints@state.co.us, or the online complaint form linked from the For Consumers page.

entries.name: Colorado Weatherization Assistance Program (Colorado Energy Office)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by regional weatherization service providers; Energy Outreach Colorado handles multifamily buildings
entries.notes: Free energy-saving home improvements after a free home energy audit, for homeowners and renters (renters need the landlord's permission), including manufactured homes. Eligible by county income limits or by current enrollment in programs such as SNAP or LEAP. Apply online or through your local weatherization service provider; there may be a waiting list depending on funding. Owners of apartment buildings with 5+ units apply through Energy Outreach Colorado at 303-825-8750.

entries.service_area_detail: Denver (parking tickets / citations)

entries.notes: Parking ticket (no autopay; one-time payments). Pay a Parking Ticket page: look up by citation number, license plate or VIN; lost citations - call the Parking Violations Bureau at 1-866-280-9988 (phone agents can find it and take payment).

entries.name: InnovAge PACE
entries.service_area_detail: Largest US PACE operator
entries.senior_programs: PACE cost depends on eligibility (eligibility-and-cost page): no premium with Medicaid or Medicare+Medicaid; Medicare-only participants pay the Medicaid portion plus a monthly Part D premium; people with neither pay a self-pay rate.
entries.notes: Eligibility & Cost page: no premium with Medicaid; Medicare-only enrollees pay the Medicaid portion plus a Part D premium; others self-pay. Share-of-cost fees apply in some states. No public bill-pay page. The Eligibility & Cost page  lists 844-211-6178 and 866-535-9350.

entries.service_area_detail: Statewide child support (and court-ordered spousal support processed through the state disbursement unit)
entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: Child support payments can be made online at ct.smartchildsupport.com (SDU child support internet payment website).

entries.name: Connecticut Judicial Branch - Centralized Infractions Bureau
entries.service_area_detail: State court system: traffic tickets, fines, court costs, restitution and payment plans (county/municipal courts may use their own portals)
entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: Email TrafficTickets@jud.ct.gov.

entries.name: Connecticut LIHEAP - Connecticut Energy Assistance Program (CEAP) (Connecticut Department of Social Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by local Community Action Agencies (CAAs)
entries.senior_programs: Households with elderly (60+) or disabled members are eligible on the same income terms; a Disability Certification form is used where applicable. Households that receive SNAP, TFA or SSI may qualify on that basis. Approved CEAP households can also get utility hardship status, which brings winter shutoff protection (Nov 1 - May 1) and access to the Matching Payment Program.
entries.notes: 2026-27 season: applications open Sept 1, 2026; deadline May 31, 2027 (mail postmarked by that date). Benefits $355-$705 for the season depending on household size, income and heating source. Income limit is 60% of State Median Income (about $48,714/yr for 1 person, $63,703 for 2). Apply online through the CEAP client portal, or by phone, email, mail or in person through your local Community Action Agency; call 2-1-1 to find your agency. Documents: most recent electric bill, primary heating bill/fuel info, income proof (4 consecutive weeks of pay stubs from the last 3 months or employer letter), plus a Zero Income Affidavit or Disability Certification if applicable. Crisis help: households with deliverable fuel (oil, propane, kerosene) who are out of fuel or within a week of running out get expedited processing - eligibility within 24 hours and delivery authorized within 18 hours. Extra help may include crisis/safety-net fuel deliveries and heating equipment repair or replacement. Must reapply every year. DSS line 1-800-842-1132, Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm.

entries.name: Connecticut Medicaid Estate Recovery (DAS Collection Services, Recovery Unit)
entries.parent_company: Connecticut Department of Administrative Services (collects for DSS)
entries.mail_payment_address: Department of Administrative Services - Collection Services, PO Box 601, Manchester, CT 06045 (checks payable to State of Connecticut)
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Connecticut collects estate recovery for DSS programs, including Medicaid, through the DAS Collection Services Recovery Unit (OLR report 2019-R-0331). The official DAS Collection Services Contact page confirms Collections Recovery at 860-713-5400 (same as Billing). Delinquent Accounts/State Tax Intercept: 860-713-5460; fax 860-713-7407. It says to make checks payable to State of Connecticut and mail them with all correspondence to DAS Collection Services, PO Box 601, Manchester, CT 06045. Phone 860-713-5400. No online payment option is published. Make checks payable to State of Connecticut and mail to DAS Collection Services, PO Box 601, Manchester, CT 06045; no automatic payment option.

entries.name: Connecticut Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PURA-regulated electric, gas and water utilities
entries.senior_programs: No age-only rule; protection comes through hardship or medical status. Hardship status (on CEAP, SNAP, TANF, unemployment or other assistance, or income at or below 60% of State Median Income) blocks gas and electric shutoff for nonpayment Nov 1 - May 1. Medical protection: a household member with a serious illness or life-threatening condition, certified by a physician, is protected; it is renewed annually, covers the winter period for serious illness and all year for life-threatening conditions. Apply for hardship or medical status through your utility, not PURA.
entries.notes: Winter Protection Period: Nov 1 - May 1 for customers approved as financial hardship or medically protected (gas and electric). Matching Payment Program (for hardship customers) matches your payments and energy assistance toward past-due balances and gives year-round shutoff protection as long as you keep up the designated payments. Low-Income Discount Rate gives a monthly electric discount; auto-enrollment at 10% for some benefit recipients, call your utility for higher tiers. Before filing with PURA you must first try to resolve the issue with the utility. PURA Customer Affairs: 1-800-382-4586 (outside CT 860-827-2622; TDD 860-827-2837), Mon-Fri 8:30am-4:30pm, email pura.information@ct.gov, or online complaint form. Filing a complaint does not by itself stop a shutoff, so also call the utility right away.

entries.name: Connecticut Weatherization Assistance Program (Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection)
entries.parent_company: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; Community Renewal Team serves Hartford, Tolland, Middlesex, Windham and New London counties; Center for Eco Technology serves New Haven, Fairfield and Litchfield counties
entries.senior_programs: Priority is given to elderly residents, people with disabilities, families with children and high energy users.
entries.notes: Free home weatherization for households at or below 60% of State Median Income. Apply through the joint CEAP application at your local Community Action Agency (call 2-1-1 to find an intake site) and ask the intake worker to refer you to the weatherization provider, or email DEEP.Weatherization@ct.gov. Homes weatherized in the last 15 years, or listed for sale or in foreclosure, are not eligible. If you don't qualify, the utility-funded Home Energy Solutions program through Energize CT (1-877-947-3873 / 1-877-WISE-USE) is an alternative.

entries.name: Generation Power CT (formerly Operation Fuel) - utility, fuel and water grants
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide Connecticut
entries.notes: Grants up to $500 toward gas or electric bills (one energy grant per 12 months; separate fuel and water assistance). Applications open only in 3 windows: Sept 1-15, Dec 1-15 and Mar 1-15. Household income up to 75% of state median income. Need proof of gross income for the last 4 weeks for every member 21+, payment history showing at least 4 monthly payments in the last 12 months, and the latest past-due bill. Decisions come by email. Help applying at an Application Support Center. Phone 860-243-2345, Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-noon.

entries.name: DC DHCF Medicaid Estate Recovery (Third Party Liability Division)

entries.notes: DHCF fact sheet: Health Care Operations Administration, Third Party Liability Division (202) 698-2000; language line (202) 727-5355. Notice of Proposed Recovery arrives with Exemption and Undue Hardship Waiver applications that must be returned within 30 days. Estate recovery does not include Medicare Part A and B premiums, deductibles, coinsurance and copays for recent dates of service. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.notes: DC parking/photo tickets are paid to DC DMV, not the courts.

entries.name: District of Columbia LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (DC Department of Energy and Environment)
entries.parent_company: DC Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE)
entries.service_area_detail: District-wide; administered directly by DOEE (Utility Affordability Administration)
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window. LIHEAP approval also enrolls you in the Utility Discount Program (electric, gas and water discounts). A copy of the disconnection notice speeds emergency help. Call 311 or 202-737-4404 if you need help completing the paper application.
entries.notes: FY2027 applications open October 20, 2026. Regular assistance is a one-time grant of about $250-$1,800 based on household size, income, heating source and type of home; no repayment. Emergency assistance is for households whose service has been disconnected or whose heating oil is at 5% or less of tank capacity, with $250+ still owed after the regular benefit. Apply by calling 311 or 202-737-4404 (TTY 711), or mail the completed application and documents to DOEE, 1200 First Street NE, 5th Floor, Washington DC 20002. Documents: government-issued photo ID, recent Washington Gas, Pepco and DC Water bills, proof of current income for all household members, Social Security cards, and the disconnection notice for emergency help. Income limits are posted on the program page each year.

entries.name: District of Columbia Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia
entries.service_area_detail: District-wide; covers Pepco, Washington Gas, DC Water and other PSC-regulated utilities
entries.senior_programs: No age-based rule. Medical: a physician's certificate or notice from a public health official that disconnection would harm the health or safety of an occupant postpones shutoff for up to 21 days, provided the customer enters a deferred payment agreement (DPA); it can be renewed once for up to 21 more days (15 DCMR 311.1). Extreme-temperature protection applies to everyone and is especially important for seniors.
entries.notes: No seasonal moratorium; instead, electric and gas service cannot be disconnected on the day before or the day of a National Weather Service forecast of 95 F or above or 32 F or below, and if that forecast falls before a weekend or holiday, not during the weekend/holiday either (DC Code 34-1506.01 and 34-1671.06a). Utilities must mail disconnection notice at least 15 days ahead (15 DCMR 311.3) and generally may not disconnect on holidays or days the utility is closed. Service cannot be cut while a dispute filed with the PSC Office of Consumer Services is pending, as long as you pay the undisputed amount (15 DCMR 311.2). Being on a DPA you're keeping up with also prevents shutoff. File a complaint online at complaints.dcpsc.dc.gov, call the Office of Consumer Services at 202-626-5120, or visit 1325 G St NW, Suite 800 (Tue-Thu 10am-4pm). If informal resolution fails you can request a formal hearing and free representation from the Office of the People's Counsel.

entries.name: District of Columbia water bill assistance (Utility Discount Program - DC Water discount)
entries.parent_company: DC Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE)
entries.service_area_detail: District-wide; discounts applied to DC Water bills
entries.senior_programs: Seniors apply on the same income terms; LIHEAP approval also qualifies you for the discounts.
entries.notes: The Utility Discount Program gives eligible low-income DC residents discounts on electric (up to $475/yr; $300 without electric heat), gas (up to $276 in winter) and water/sewer (more than $962/yr) bills. FY26 income limits ranged from $91,800 for 1 person to $173,100 for 8. The utility account must be in the applicant's name. Applications reopen October 20, 2026; call 311 or 202-737-4404 (TTY 711), or mail the application with recent utility bills, photo ID, income proof for all earners, Social Security cards and any disconnection notice to DOEE, Attn: Utility Affordability Administration, 1200 First Street NE, 5th Floor, Washington DC 20002. Applications are available in six languages.

entries.name: District of Columbia Weatherization Assistance Program (DC Department of Energy and Environment)
entries.parent_company: DC Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE)
entries.service_area_detail: District-wide; DOEE assigns approved homes to nonprofit contractors
entries.senior_programs: Households with a member receiving SSI (or TANF) qualify regardless of the income table. The same application also covers the Emergency Mechanical Systems program, which replaces failed heating/cooling systems and water heaters.
entries.notes: Free weatherization for homeowners and renters with income below 60% of State Median Income ($61,841 for a 1-person household in FY26) or with a member on TANF or SSI. The home must not be in foreclosure, pending redevelopment or for sale. One application covers Weatherization, Emergency Mechanical Systems Replacement and Lead Reduction; apply online, by email to doee.dcwap@dc.gov, or by mail to DOEE Weatherization Assistance Program, 1200 First Street NE, 5th Floor, Washington DC 20002. Documents: signed LIHEAP application, photo ID, Social Security cards, income proof for each member, recent utility bills, recent bank statements, mortgage statement or deed, and homeowner's/renter's insurance. Weatherization openings may be delayed in some years; Emergency Mechanical Systems replacement has been open. Phone 202-299-3316, Mon-Fri 8:30am-2:30pm.

entries.name: Washington Gas home repair plans (HomeServe partner)
entries.parent_company: HomeServe USA Repair Management Corp. (Washington Gas partner program)
entries.payment_processor: HomeServe USA (in-house payment portal, card/ACH) - billed separately from the utility
entries.notes: Gas line $5.49/mo, exterior water line $5.99, water heater $12.99, exterior electric $5.99, interior electric $5.99. Enroll/cancel via HomeServe. SCAM/SALES WARNING: service-line and appliance plan offers often arrive as mailers styled like an official city or utility notice ('your water line is not covered'); they are optional, unregulated products. Unpaid plan charges cannot legally cause utility shut-off. Utility impostor calls demanding immediate payment by gift card/crypto/payment app are scams - call the number on the real bill. HomeServe payment portal: sign in with a HomeServe ID to make a one-time payment, change or remove the payment method, change billing frequency (Update Recurring Payment), see scheduled payments and view 1 year of payment history. HomeServe billing questions 1-855-336-2465.

entries.notes: Still no dedicated DMMA estate recovery unit page. The DMMA contact page  lists Medicaid Customer Relations, 302-571-4900 or 866-843-7212. Estate recovery rules are in the Delaware Social Services Manual, 16 Del. Code 20000-20500 "Estate Recovery and Liens" (text read on law.cornell.edu). Recovery is deferred while there is a surviving spouse or a blind/disabled child. Section 20500.5.3 allows an undue-hardship waiver for the period of hardship. Section 20500.7 sets a lien moratorium while a qualifying relative who lived in the home 24+ months still lives there. Payment instructions come on the claim letter.

entries.name: Delaware LIHEAP - Delaware Energy Assistance Program (DEAP) (Delaware Health and Social Services)
entries.parent_company: Delaware Health and Social Services, Division of State Service Centers
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications handled by Catholic Charities county offices
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window; seniors apply on the same terms. Catholic Charities asks anyone who needs an intake appointment to call early in the season. Utility-funded sharing programs administered by Catholic Charities (such as the Chesapeake Utilities Sharing Program) help elderly, disabled and fixed-income households.
entries.notes: Three parts: Winter Heating Assistance (heating season Oct 1 - Mar 31; 2026-27 applications accepted starting Aug 1, 2026 through Mar 31, 2027), Summer Cooling Assistance (typically applications Apr - mid-Aug), and Crisis Assistance (year-round, on top of the seasonal benefit). Crisis help requires a shut-off/disconnect notice, fuel tank at or below 10%, or past-due utility bills. Apply online through Catholic Charities or the DHSS ASSIST portal; first-time applicants and households of 10+ must make a phone appointment. Catholic Charities: New Castle 302-654-9295, Kent 302-674-1782, Sussex 302-856-6310. Documents: photo ID, Social Security cards for household members, proof of citizenship/qualified alien status, Delaware residency proof, income proof (pay stubs/award letters), current utility bills. Incomplete applications are not processed. Delaware 2-1-1 can also point you to emergency utility help.

entries.name: Delaware Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PSC-regulated electric, gas and water utilities
entries.senior_programs: No age-based rule; protection is medical. If any occupant is so ill that losing service would harm their health or recovery, and a licensed Delaware physician (or accredited Christian Science practitioner) certifies it to the utility, the utility may not disconnect (26 Del. C. 117(d); 26 Del. Admin. Code 3002). Weather-based rules protect everyone, including seniors.
entries.notes: Code 3002 (termination during heating and cooling seasons). Heating season Nov 15 - Mar 31: no shutoff for nonpayment on a day when the 8am temperature is 32 F or below. Cooling season Jun 1 - Sep 30: no shutoff on a day when the forecast heat index may reach 105 F or higher. Utilities must give at least 14 calendar days' written notice before shutoff, with steps to avoid it and payment-arrangement information. Before a shutoff: call the utility first, then the Division of the Public Advocate (302-241-2555, toll-free 1-888-607-2427, publicadvocate.delaware.gov/file-a-complaint) for help; formal complaints go to the PSC (302-736-7500, toll-free 1-800-282-8574) and must name the law, rule or order violated and the relief requested. Delaware Helpline for financial assistance: 1-800-464-4357.

entries.name: Delaware Weatherization Assistance Program (Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control)
entries.parent_company: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC), Division of Climate, Coastal and Energy
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by the Energy Coordinating Agency
entries.senior_programs: The waiting list is prioritized by need, the age of residents and special needs (such as disability).
entries.notes: Free weatherization (insulation, weather-stripping, heating/cooling upgrades, window and door work) for homeowners and renters; typical bill savings 30-50%. Income limits: $31,920/yr for 1 person, $66,000 for 4, $111,440 for 8. Call the Energy Coordinating Agency at 302-504-6111 (or email coletted@ecasys.org) to set an appointment and bring required documents. Approved households go on a waiting list; if not served within 12 months, you must reapply to confirm income. Other questions: DNREC 302-735-3480 or DNREC.WAP@delaware.gov.

entries.name: Florida LIHEAP - Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (FloridaCommerce)
entries.parent_company: Florida Department of Commerce (FloridaCommerce), Division of Community Development
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by local LIHEAP providers (community action agencies and local governments) in each county
entries.senior_programs: Emergency Home Energy Assistance for the Elderly Program (EHEAP): for low-income households with at least one person 60+ facing a home energy emergency; can pay electric, gas, propane and other fuels, deposits, reconnect and late fees, and may provide blankets, fans or emergency shelter. EHEAP is moving from the Department of Elder Affairs to FloridaCommerce; contact FloridaLIHEAP@Commerce.fl.gov or the Elder Helpline 1-800-963-5337 (1-800-96-ELDER) for your local provider. If power is off or about to be cut and a senior or person with a disability is at risk, call 9-1-1 for life-threatening emergencies or 2-1-1 for help.
entries.notes: Heating help Oct 1 - Mar 31, cooling help Apr 1 - Sep 30, crisis help year-round (crisis requires a final termination notice or similar emergency). Benefits typically $400-$1,350 for heating/cooling, up to $2,000 for crisis. Depending on county funds you may get help more than once a year, but not every month. Income limit 60% of State Median Income: $32,155/yr for 1 person, $42,049 for 2, $61,837 for 4. Gas or propane bills are covered only in winter and only if used for heating; LIHEAP cannot pay water, sewer or phone. Apply by calling your local LIHEAP provider (lines are busy - keep trying and check hours). Documents: most recent energy bill, final utility termination notice, proof of gross income for all household members, applicant photo ID, Social Security cards or numbers for all members, proof of citizenship or permanent residence. Payments go straight to the utility.

entries.name: Florida Medicaid Estate Recovery Program (AHCA / HMS)
entries.parent_company: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (administered by HMS/Gainwell)
entries.mail_payment_address: Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program, P.O. Box 12188, Tallahassee, FL 32317-2188
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: Contact page lists P.O. Box 12188 for 'Correspondence and Payments'; email flsubro@gainwelltechnologies.com; fax 844-845-8352. FAQ explains claim filed in probate, homestead protection, and Request for Hardship Waiver form (obtain by contacting the program). The personal representative or any heir may ask the Agency to waive all or part of the claim for hardship using the Request for Hardship Waiver form (get it from the program); losing an expected inheritance alone is not a hardship. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Florida Medically Needy (Share of Cost) program
entries.parent_company: Florida Department of Children and Families (DCF)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide
entries.senior_programs: Medically Needy 'share of cost' is a monthly spend-down: no payment to the state - the member submits proof of medical bills/insurance premiums until the share of cost is met, then Medicaid covers the rest of the month.
entries.notes: DCF 2024 Medically Needy brochure ('An Explanation of Share of Cost'): proof of medical expenses goes through the MyACCESS portal (MyACCESS.myflfamilies.com), fax, mail or in person, with name and case number. There is no state pay-in option; the bill is owed to providers. There is no bill from the state and nothing to pay online or by automatic payment: the spend-down is met each month by showing proof of medical bills and insurance premiums through MyACCESS, fax, mail or in person.

entries.name: Florida Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for investor-owned electric and gas utilities (and some private water/wastewater utilities); municipal utilities and electric co-ops are not PSC-regulated for rates and service
entries.senior_programs: Florida has no age-based or seasonal shutoff protection. Each electric utility must file a tariff procedure for customers whose service is medically essential (Fla. Admin. Code 25-6.105(11)); ask your utility to register a household member who relies on electric medical equipment. Customers can designate a third party (such as a family member) to receive a copy of any past-due notice.
entries.notes: No winter or summer moratorium and no temperature-based rule statewide. Code 25-6.105: utilities must give at least 5 working days' written notice, separate from the bill, before shutoff for nonpayment; no shutoff of residential service from noon Friday to 8am Monday or from noon the day before a holiday to 8am the next working day. If you disagree with a shutoff, contact the utility first, then the PSC Office of Consumer Assistance & Outreach: 1-800-342-3552, fax 1-800-511-0809, email contact@psc.state.fl.us, or the 24-hour online complaint form. The PSC handles improper termination, billing errors, deposits and high-bill complaints for investor-owned utilities (e.g., FPL, Duke Energy Florida, TECO); for city utilities or co-ops, contact the utility's own governing board.

entries.name: Florida Weatherization Assistance Program (FloridaCommerce)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by community action agencies, local governments and nonprofits by county
entries.senior_programs: Preference is given to elderly (60+) and disabled residents, families with children under 18 and households with high energy bills. Bring documentation of disability or elderly status.
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency repairs based on a home energy audit: air sealing, insulation, duct sealing, HVAC repair or replacement, water heater repair/replacement, refrigerator replacement, solar screens and reflective roof coating for manufactured homes. Income must be at or below 200% of poverty ($30,120/yr for 1 person, $40,880 for 2, $62,400 for 4). Apply through your county's local weatherization agency (list at FloridaJobs.org/WAPHelp). Documents: photo ID, proof of income for all household members, Social Security cards, recent utility bill, proof of homeownership or landlord authorization if renting, and proof of disability/elderly status or child in the home. Services depend on available funding.

entries.senior_programs: Hardship: DMP FAQ says clients under severe financial distress may have some set-up/monthly costs waived.
entries.notes: 'Portal Login' for DMP clients; separate Bankruptcy Login. Call for draft changes or cancellation. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/. Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. DMP FAQ (faq-debt-management-plan) covers fees; it does not describe stopping drafts, so call 800-920-2262 to change or cancel.

entries.name: Georgia LIHEAP - Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Georgia Department of Human Services, Division of Family and Children Services)
entries.parent_company: Georgia Department of Human Services, Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by local Community Action Agencies by county, first-come first-served
entries.senior_programs: Seniors 65+ and medically homebound applicants get a one-month head start: heating applications open to them on the first workday of December (general public: first workday of January) and cooling applications on the first workday of April (general public: first workday of May). Many utilities also offer senior discounts on the monthly service charge (for example Atlanta Gas Light's discount for customers 65+ with low household income); ask your utility.
entries.notes: Heating assistance: senior/homebound intake from the first workday of December, everyone else from the first workday of January; season typically runs until funds run out (as late as July 31). Cooling assistance: seniors/homebound from the first workday of April, others from the first workday of May. Winter and summer crisis assistance help households facing shutoff. Recent benefits: heating $400-$810, cooling $400-$500, winter crisis up to $810, summer crisis up to $500. Income limit 60% of State Median Income; you must be responsible for paying the home energy bill, and you're ineligible if your energy account has a credit of $1,000 or more. Apply through your county's Community Action Agency (provider map on the DFCS site) - funding is first-come, first-served, so apply as early as your window opens. Call your agency for its document list (typically ID, income proof and a recent energy bill). Free interpreter help is available.

entries.name: Georgia Medicaid Estate Recovery
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: First $25,000 of any estate waived; estates of $25,000 or less exempt. Heirs may seek undue-hardship waiver. The first $25,000 of any estate is waived for deaths on or after July 1, 2018; heirs can seek an undue-hardship waiver with clear and convincing evidence. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Georgia Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for PSC-regulated utilities (Georgia Power, Atlanta Gas Light, certificated gas marketers); EMCs and city utilities follow their own rules
entries.senior_programs: Medical: if a household member is seriously ill, notify the utility in writing and have a physician send a letter within 10 days confirming the illness, that disconnection would worsen it, and how long the illness is expected to last; the utility must then hold off on disconnection. No age-only protection in the rule, but cold- and heat-weather rules protect everyone.
entries.notes: Winter (Nov 15 - Mar 15): electric service cannot be disconnected when the forecast is below 32 F for the 24 hours starting 8am on the scheduled date; customers must agree in writing to pay the past-due balance in equal installments between Mar 15 and Oct 15 and keep current bills paid. Summer: no electric disconnection if a National Weather Service Heat Advisory or Excessive Heat Warning is in effect for the county before 8am on the scheduled date. Written disconnect notice at least 5 days before, plus a good-faith contact attempt at least 2 days before. If you face a shutoff, call the utility first, then the PSC Consumer Affairs line 1-800-282-5813  or file online through the PSC consumer portal; PSC, 244 Washington St SW, Atlanta, GA 30334.

entries.name: Georgia Weatherization Assistance Program (Georgia Environmental Finance Authority)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local Community Action Agencies
entries.senior_programs: Preference is given to the elderly, people with disabilities and families with children.
entries.notes: Free home energy audit and improvements (insulation, air sealing, heating/cooling upgrades, water-saving devices) for households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level; single-family homes, manufactured homes and multifamily buildings qualify, owners or renters. Apply through your local Community Action Agency (county list on the GEFA site).

entries.notes: Emergency help with electric, natural gas and water bills (and limited rent/prescriptions) for Georgia households in a financial crisis. Make an appointment with the Project SHARE partner agency in your county; bring proof of identity and residence and the utility bill. Eligibility is decided case by case. Questions: 1-800-25SHARE (1-800-257-4273) or your power company's customer service.

entries.name: Guam LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Guam Energy Office)
entries.parent_company: Guam Department of Public Health and Social Services (DPHSS); administered by the Guam Energy Office (GEO)
entries.service_area_detail: Island-wide; apply in person at the Guam Energy Office, Tamuning
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window is published. Households receiving SSI, SNAP or TANF may qualify automatically on income.
entries.notes: Applications are closed until the next funding year; the program reopens when new federal funds arrive (last season: Crisis Assistance Mar 16 - Aug 14, Cooling Assistance Credit Mar 16 - Mar 27). Crisis Assistance: one-time payment up to $1,000 to your Guam Power Authority (GPA) account if power is disconnected or you have a disconnection notice (notice required). Cooling Assistance Credit: $100 per month for up to 5 months on your GPA account, first come first served. Only one benefit per funding year. Eligibility: all household members U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens, and gross monthly income at or below 130% of poverty (e.g., $1,696 for 1 person, $2,292 for 2), or receipt of SNAP, TANF or SSI. Non-account-holders can apply with proof they pay the power bill (lease, self-attestation, authorization letter). Documents: photo ID, Social Security cards for all members, income proof (recent tax return, 2 recent pay stubs, employment verification, or SNAP/TANF/SSI statement), current GPA bill, GPA release form, LIHEAP questionnaire. Download the fillable application at energy.guam.gov or pick one up at 548 North Marine Corps Dr., Tamuning; submit in person Mon-Fri 9am-4pm (email submissions not accepted). Decision within about 15 business days. Email: LIHEAP@energy.guam.gov.

entries.name: Guam Office of the Attorney General Child Support Enforcement Division (CSED)
