entries.notes: Email childsupport@oagguam.org. Payments go through the local location or the channels above.

entries.name: Guam Public Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Regulates Guam Power Authority (GPA), Guam Waterworks Authority (GWA), telecom and other utilities
entries.senior_programs: No elderly- or medical-specific shutoff rule is published by the PUC. If power is cut off or a disconnection notice arrives, the Guam LIHEAP Crisis Assistance program (Guam Energy Office, 671-646-4361) can pay up to $1,000 toward the GPA bill when funds are available.
entries.notes: The PUC regulates rates and service rules for GPA (power) and GWA (water); there is no published winter or heat moratorium. Contact the utility first to dispute a bill or arrange payment; if unresolved, call or email the PUC (671-472-1907, info@guampuc.com) or write to Suite 807 DNA Bldg., 238 Archbishop Flores St., Hagåtña, Guam 96910. Utility rules, tariffs and dockets are posted under Rules & Procedures and the PUC Reference Center.

entries.name: Guam Weatherization Assistance Program (Guam Energy Office)
entries.service_area_detail: Island-wide; homeowners and renters (including Section 8)
entries.senior_programs: Priority is given to the elderly, people with disabilities, families with children, high energy users and households with a high energy burden.
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency upgrades for income-eligible households: refrigerator and/or air conditioner (room or mini-split) replacement, LED bulbs, low-flow shower heads and aerators, advanced power strips, smoke/CO detectors, weather-stripping. A home assessment is done first. Income must be under the program limit (based on area median income). Documents: photo ID, Social Security cards for all members, proof of all household income (pay stubs, Social Security checks, etc.), proof of ownership (deed, property tax, mortgage, insurance) or rental agreement. Download the WAP application packet from the GEO website or call 671-646-4361; email guamenergyoffice@gmail.com. GEO never charges a fee to apply; report anyone claiming to sell WAP equipment to GEO or the Attorney General consumer line 671-475-2720.

entries.name: Hawaii LIHEAP - Hawaii Home Energy Assistance Program (H-HEAP) (Hawaii Department of Human Services)
entries.parent_company: Hawaii Department of Human Services, Benefit, Employment and Support Services Division
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications accepted only by the Community Action Agency for each island (Honolulu Community Action Program, Maui Economic Opportunity, Hawaii County Economic Opportunity Council, Kauai Economic Opportunity)
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window; seniors and people with disabilities apply the same way, listing SSI, Social Security or disability income on the application. On Kauai, low-income seniors 60+ who own their homes may get a free refrigerator or electric water heater replacement through KIUC with the County of Kauai Agency on Elderly Affairs (808-241-4470).
entries.notes: Program year Oct 1 - Sep 30; a household can get only one type of H-HEAP payment per year (a one-time payment to the electric or gas company). Energy Crisis Intervention (ECI): for households with a disconnect notice or whose service has been cut; accepted year-round but monthly approvals are limited and fill quickly, so apply as soon as you get the notice (up to about $700). Energy Credit (EC): for heating/cooling bill help when not in crisis; applications accepted only June 1 - June 30 (benefits roughly $375-$1,400). Income limit 60% of State Median Income. Send the application and documents to your island's Community Action Agency, not to DHS offices. Agencies: Kauai Economic Opportunity 808-245-4077; Hawaii County Economic Opportunity Council 808-731-7009 option 1; Maui Economic Opportunity 808-249-2970; Honolulu Community Action Program district offices (e.g., 808-847-0804). Documents: Social Security numbers/cards, proof of all earned and unearned income (pay stubs, Social Security, SSI, unemployment), recent electric/gas bill and disconnect notice if any, and immigration documents for non-citizens.

entries.name: Hawaii Med-QUEST Medicaid Liens and Estate Recovery

Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: Official DHS 1168 brochure (Medicaid liens on home property): hardship waiver when the estate is the survivors' sole income-producing asset (family farm/business) etc.; questions to the Department of the Attorney General, Civil Recoveries Division at 586-1126 (Oahu, area code 808). Med-QUEST general line 1-800-316-8005. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Hawaii Public Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for regulated utilities (Hawaiian Electric, Hawaii Gas, Kauai Island Utility Cooperative, private water/wastewater companies)
entries.senior_programs: No age-based or weather-based shutoff rule in Hawaii. Hawaiian Electric customers who depend on life-support equipment at home, or have higher heating/cooling needs due to a medical condition, may qualify for reduced rates through its Life Support and Special Medical Needs programs; register with the utility so it knows about the medical need before any disconnection.
entries.notes: Hawaii has no winter or summer shutoff moratorium; disconnection procedures are set by each utility's PUC-approved tariff rules. If you get a disconnect notice: call the utility to ask for a payment arrangement, apply right away for H-HEAP Energy Crisis Intervention through your island's Community Action Agency, and if the problem isn't resolved contact the PUC. PUC consumer help: Oahu 808-586-2020; Hawaii District Office (Hilo) 808-289-5622; Kauai 808-274-3232; Maui 808-264-4438; Mon-Fri 7:45am-4:30pm, or use the PUC's online CDMS eServices customer assistance portal. The Division of Consumer Advocacy (consumeradvocate@dcca.hawaii.gov) also represents utility consumers.

entries.name: Iowa Judicial Branch - Pay a Fine or Court Debt
entries.service_area_detail: State court system: traffic tickets, fines, court costs, restitution and payment plans (county/municipal courts may use their own portals)
entries.senior_programs: Payment plans through the county clerk with no interest (private collectors may add up to 25%); unpaid fines can trigger license suspension and registration holds. Beware text-message 'unpaid fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: Scam alert page: https://www.iowacourts.gov/for-the-public/pay-a-fine/scam-alert/. Citations can take 10-14 days to appear; fines are due 30 days after assessment; paying online is a guilty plea.

entries.name: Iowa LIHEAP - Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Iowa Department of Health and Human Services)
entries.parent_company: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by local community action agencies in each county
entries.senior_programs: Households with a member 60 or older or a member with a disability can apply starting October 1; all other households start November 1. Being certified eligible for LIHEAP also protects against utility shutoff from November 1 through April 1.
entries.notes: Application period: Oct 1 - Apr 30 for elderly/disabled households, Nov 1 - Apr 30 for everyone else; first-come, first-served. Income limit 200% of federal poverty level (2025-26: 1 person $31,300; 2 people $42,300; 3 people $53,300; 4 people $64,300; add $11,000 per extra person); household must have an energy burden; renters and owners both eligible. Apply at your county's community action agency (locator at iowacommunityaction.org) or through the state online portal liheap-apply.hhs.iowa.gov. Apply BEFORE a shutoff and tell your utility you applied: certified LIHEAP households cannot be disconnected Nov 1 - Apr 1, but approval does not restore service already cut off. A weatherization application automatically creates a LIHEAP application. Help finding where to apply: dial 211. Community Action Agencies Unit: 515-776-8871.

entries.name: Iowa Medicaid Estate Recovery Program
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Hardship delay/waiver must be requested within 30 days of the estate recovery letter (household income under 200% FPL test). Program contact line (888) 513-5186 / (515) 246-9841. Online referral and probate notice forms hosted at iowa-estates.com (state contractor). Lien recovery page: https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery Families get a letter about repayment and have 30 days from receiving it to apply for a hardship delay or waiver (household income under 200% of poverty, resources of $10,000 or less). Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Iowa Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Iowa Utilities Commission (formerly Iowa Utilities Board)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; rate-regulated gas/electric (MidAmerican, Alliant, Black Hills) plus shutoff rules for co-ops and municipal utilities
entries.senior_programs: No age-based moratorium; protection comes from LIHEAP/weatherization eligibility (no shutoff Nov 1 - Apr 1 once certified eligible) and health certification: a doctor or public health official tells the utility shutoff would be an especial health danger, follows up in writing within 5 days, and service cannot be cut for 30 days. If already shut off, a medical statement within 14 days restores service for 30 days.
entries.notes: Winter: no shutoff Nov 1 - Apr 1 for households certified eligible for energy assistance or weatherization (apply before shutoff and notify the utility). Cold weather: no shutoff when the forecast is 20F or colder in the next 24 hours. Shutoffs only 6 a.m.-2 p.m. Mon-Fri, not nights, weekends or holidays; 12 days' written notice required, and from Nov 1 - Apr 1 the utility must try to reach you and post a door notice. First payment plan must spread past-due amounts over at least 12 months. Medical: 30-day postponement. Rules: 199 IAC chapters 19 (gas), 20 (electric), 21 (water/sewer), 27 (co-ops/municipals). Call the utility first, then the IUC Customer Service line 515-725-7300 or 1-877-565-4450 (8 a.m.-4:30 p.m. weekdays), email customer@iuc.iowa.gov, or use the online complaint form.

entries.name: Iowa Weatherization Assistance Program (Iowa Department of Health and Human Services)
entries.parent_company: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local community action agencies
entries.senior_programs: Program prioritizes elderly, disabled, and households with children.
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency improvements to lower heating and cooling costs for low-income households (income up to 200% of the federal poverty level). Apply at the community action agency in your county; applying for weatherization also starts a LIHEAP application. HHS general line: 1-800-972-2017.

SCAM/SALES WARNING: service-line and appliance plan offers often arrive as mailers styled like an official city or utility notice ('your water line is not covered'); they are optional, unregulated products. Unpaid plan charges cannot legally cause utility shut-off. Utility impostor calls demanding immediate payment by gift card/crypto/payment app are scams - call the number on the real bill. HomeServe payment portal: sign in with a HomeServe ID to make a one-time payment, change or remove the payment method, change billing frequency (Update Recurring Payment), see scheduled payments and view 1 year of payment history. HomeServe billing questions 1-855-336-2465.

Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.

entries.name: Idaho LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Idaho Department of Health and Welfare)
entries.parent_company: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by local Community Action Agencies (Nez Perce and Shoshone-Bannock Tribes take applications for tribal members)
entries.senior_programs: Households with an elderly or disabled member (or a child under 6) can apply for seasonal heating assistance starting in October; other households start in November. Funding is first-come, first-served, so applying early in October matters.
entries.notes: Two parts: Seasonal Heating Assistance (one payment toward heating bills per program year, Oct-Sep; applications typically open in October for priority households and November for everyone else, while funds last) and Crisis Heating Assistance (year-round, first-come first-served; for households with a shutoff notice, a disconnected utility, a past-due bill, or less than 48 hours of bulk fuel; aims to resolve within 48 hours; not available if you got crisis help in the past 12 months). Apply through your local Community Action Agency (in person, by phone, or by mailing/emailing/faxing the paper Application for Energy Assistance); the agency directory is the help link. Monthly income limits effective Oct 1, 2025: 1 person $2,736; 2 people $3,578; 3 people $4,420; 4 people $5,262; add $687.50 per extra person. Bring proof of identity, income, and your heating bill/expense. Past recipients must reapply each year. The statewide number is the Idaho CareLine (also reachable by dialing 211).

entries.name: Idaho Public Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric, gas, water and telephone utilities (Idaho Power, Avista, Rocky Mountain Power, Intermountain Gas, etc.)
entries.senior_programs: Winter protection: from December through March a gas or electric utility may not shut off (or threaten to shut off) a household that includes anyone 62 or older, a child 18 or under, or an infirm person, if the customer tells the utility they cannot pay in full. Such customers must be offered a Winter Payment Plan (half the normal level-pay amount each month); signing up before November 1 extends protection to November through March. Medical certificate: a written certificate from a licensed physician or public health official with medical training postpones shutoff 30 days; a second certificate can extend it if the illness or emergency continues.
entries.notes: Winter moratorium: Dec 1 - Mar 31 for households with elderly (62+), children, or infirm members who declare inability to pay (IDAPA 31.21.01.306); Winter Payment Plan started before Nov 1 protects Nov-Mar. Any unpaid balance must be paid or put on a new payment arrangement by March 1 (no plan) or April 1 (with plan), or service may be cut. Medical certificate postponement is 30 days (IDAPA 31.21.01.308). No summer heat rule. Before a shutoff, call the utility to ask for a payment arrangement, then call the PUC Consumer Assistance staff at 208-334-0369 or 1-800-432-0369, or use the online Consumer Complaint / Inquiry Form, for help with bills or disconnection. The PUC's FAQ lists local assistance resources by county.

entries.name: Idaho Weatherization Assistance Program (Idaho Department of Health and Welfare)
entries.parent_company: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local Community Action Agencies
entries.senior_programs: Priority goes to households with elderly or disabled members, families with children, and households with an emergency heating situation.
entries.notes: Free energy-saving home repairs (insulation, air sealing, heating system safety) for low-income households (generally up to 200% of the federal poverty level). Homeowners qualify; renters need written landlord permission. Funding is year-round, first-come first-served. Apply through your local Community Action Agency (directory in help link). Some utilities (Avista, Idaho Power, Rocky Mountain Power) also fund weatherization through the same agencies.

entries.name: Illinois Commerce Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric, gas, water, sewer and local telephone utilities (ComEd, Ameren, Nicor, Peoples Gas, etc.)
entries.senior_programs: No age-based moratorium, but key protections: a medical certificate from a licensed physician or local board of health stops disconnection for 60 days (a phone call from the doctor counts if a written certificate follows within 7 days); the customer then gets a medical payment arrangement. A new certificate is allowed once the balance is brought current or 12 months after the prior certification began. LIHEAP recipients who heat with gas or electricity cannot be disconnected Dec 1 - Mar 31, and large electric utilities cannot disconnect electric space-heating customers Dec 1 - Mar 31.
entries.notes: Cold weather: gas or electric heat cannot be shut off on any day when the National Weather Service forecasts 32F or below in the next 24 hours, or before a weekend/holiday forecast at 32F or below. Winter: Dec 1 - Mar 31 no disconnection for households that received LIHEAP (220 ILCS 5/8-206) or electric space-heating customers of large utilities. Hot weather: large utilities may not cut off service used for the only cooling on days forecast at 95F or above (or before a hot weekend/holiday). Medical certificate: 60 days (83 Ill. Adm. Code 280.130 and 280.160). No shutoffs on state holidays or after noon the day before. Before a shutoff, call your utility to ask for a payment arrangement, then call the ICC Consumer Services Division at 1-800-524-0795 (out of state 217-782-2024; TTY 888-261-4188) or file the online complaint form. You can ask the utility to send a copy of disconnection notices to a third party such as a family caregiver.

Box 19174, Springfield, IL 62794-9174. Hardship waiver application in 6 languages on the hardship page; can also be submitted via the HFS secure Information Portal. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Illinois HFS Medicaid Pay-in Spenddown
entries.parent_company: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; aged, blind or disabled Medicaid members with a spenddown
entries.senior_programs: Spenddown works like a monthly deductible; enrolled aged/blind/disabled members can pay the spenddown amount to the state to activate Medicaid for chosen months.
entries.notes: HFS 591SP brochure: after enrolling in Pay-in Spenddown, HFS mails a monthly Pay-in Spenddown Statement; return it to HFS Fiscal Operations with payment by money order, cashier's check, Visa or MasterCard (no personal checks). Payment is optional each month - pay only for months you need a medical card; can combine bills and a partial payment. DHS 'Pay-In Spenddown Facts' (HFS 3711H) explains enrollment (Form HFS 458SP-4 from the Health Benefits Hotline). There is no automatic payment option; each month you choose whether to pay, using the mailed Pay-in Spenddown Statement. Medical bills dated within the last six months can also be used to meet spenddown.

entries.name: Illinois Home Weatherization Assistance Program (Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity)

entries.senior_programs: Households receiving Social Security disability/SSI cash benefits or LIHEAP automatically meet income eligibility.
entries.notes: Free home weatherization (insulation, air sealing, furnace and safety work). Income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (about $31,920/year for 1 person, $66,000 for 4). Automatically eligible if the household gets LIHEAP, SSI/Title IV or XVI cash benefits, or HUD/USDA housing assistance. Apply online through DCEO's weatherization apply-online page or in person at your local community action agency. Help line 1-833-711-0374; email communityassist@illinois.gov.

entries.name: Illinois LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity)
entries.parent_company: Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications processed by local community action agencies (county agencies)
entries.senior_programs: Adults 60 and older, people with disabilities, families with children 5 and under, and households facing or already in disconnection can apply starting October 1; everyone else starts November 1. Homebound applicants can ask the local agency for a home visit.
entries.notes: Program year runs Oct 1, 2026 - Aug 13, 2027 or until funds run out. Apply online through the Help Illinois Families Request for Services form (helpillinoisfamilies.com), by calling the Help Illinois Families call center at 1-833-711-0374 for help with the form, or in person at your county's local agency. After you get an application ID (starts with 8) you can check status at liheap2025.ilenergyassistance.com/customerinquiry. Income limit (30-day gross income): 1 person $3,990; 2 people $5,410; 3 people $6,830; 4 people $8,250; 5 people $9,670. Bring: recent pay stubs or proof of fixed income (Social Security, VA, DHS), utility bills from the past 30 days, Social Security card or ITIN for household members, rental agreement if heat is included in rent, proof of TANF/SNAP/Medicaid if you have it. Crisis help: Reconnection Assistance if you are disconnected or will be within 7 days (call your county agency directly with the disconnect notice), and Furnace Assistance for homeowners without working heat; crisis help is provided within 48 hours of a complete application (18 hours when temperatures are below 32F). PIPP (Percentage of Income Payment Plan) for Ameren, ComEd, Nicor, Peoples/North Shore Gas customers lets you pay a share of income with a monthly benefit; new PIPP enrollment may be closed with only recertifications accepted. LIHEAP does not pay water or sewer bills.

Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. FAQ (https://www.familycredit.org/faq): monthly statement shows where the money went, online account shows status anytime; 2025 averages were $28/month fee and $39 one-time enrollment fee, both included in the monthly payment.

entries.name: Indiana LIHEAP - Energy Assistance Program (EAP) (Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority)
entries.parent_company: Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority (IHCDA)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications processed by Local Service Providers (community action agencies) by county
entries.senior_programs: Applying for EAP is what triggers Indiana's winter shutoff protection (Dec 1 - Mar 15), so older adults should apply as early as possible after Oct 1. Life-threatening heating emergencies with documented medical need must be addressed within 18 hours.
entries.notes: Program year 2027 applications open Oct 1, 2026 (8 a.m.) and close Apr 30, 2027 (5 p.m.). Apply online at eap.mylitt.com, or in person or by mail through your county's Local Service Provider (county map on the IHCDA EAP page). Income limit is 60% of state median income, measured over the last 3 months (about $8,389 for 1 person, $16,133 for a family of 4, per 3 months). Bring proof of income for the last 3 months, current utility bills/account statements, and a lease or tenant verification if utilities are included in rent. Crisis help: with a disconnect notice, a disconnection, or fuel at or below 25%, the provider must act within 48 hours (18 hours if life-threatening). Eligibility decisions can take up to 55 days and the utility may take 30 more days to post the benefit, so keep paying what you can. Questions: 317-232-7777, eap@ihcda.in.gov; IHCDA toll-free 1-800-872-0371; or dial 211 for local help. Township trustees also provide emergency utility help ('poor relief').

Email preferred for payment questions. Undue hardship waivers must be requested within 90 days of the claim date (877-267-0013 or EstateRecovery@fssa.in.gov). The program cannot accept prepayments while the Medicaid member is alive. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric, gas, water and sewer utilities; winter moratorium also covers municipal utilities and REMCs
entries.senior_programs: No age-based shutoff rule. Winter moratorium protects anyone who is eligible for and has applied for EAP (Dec 1 - Mar 15) once the household gives the utility written proof of the application. A medical statement from a licensed doctor or public health official postpones disconnection for 10 days.
entries.notes: Winter moratorium Dec 1 - Mar 15 for electric and natural gas service (investor-owned utilities, municipal utilities, and REMCs) for customers who applied for EAP at their local intake office and gave the utility written proof; does not cover water, sewer, phone or propane, and you must keep making payments. Medical statement: 10-day postponement. Utilities must offer a payment arrangement (required only once per 12 months). A 2026 state law (House Enrolled Act 1002) added a hot-weather protection tied to National Weather Service heat-index forecasts of 95F or higher; ask the utility or the IURC how it applies. Before a shutoff, contact the utility first, then the IURC Consumer Affairs Division at 1-800-851-4268 (Mon-Fri 8:15 a.m.-4:45 p.m. ET) or file online at iurc.portal.in.gov.

entries.name: Kansas Corporation Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric, natural gas and water utilities (Evergy, Kansas Gas Service, Atmos, Black Hills, etc.)
entries.senior_programs: If shutoff would be especially dangerous to the health of anyone in the home and the customer cannot pay in full, the utility must either allow reasonable installments or postpone disconnection at least 21 days; the KCC considers weather and the person's medical condition, age, or disability in deciding whether shutoff is especially dangerous.
entries.notes: Cold Weather Rule Nov 1 - Mar 31: no disconnection when the National Weather Service forecasts temperatures below 35F (or mid-30s or colder) within the next 48 hours. During the period any customer can keep or restore service by paying 1/12 of the overdue balance plus 1/12 of the current bill and any fees/deposits, then spreading the rest over 11 months, while paying for new usage. Utilities must give 10 days' written notice and try to reach you by phone or in person the day before. Health-danger rule: at least a 21-day postponement or an installment plan (KCC Billing Standards, Section IV.D). Applies to electric, gas and water utilities under KCC jurisdiction. Call the utility first, then the KCC Public Affairs and Consumer Protection office at 1-800-662-0027 or 785-271-3140, or file a complaint online through KCC-Connect (kcc-connect.kcc.ks.gov/s/file-a-complaint).

entries.name: Kansas LIHEAP - Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) (Kansas Department for Children and Families)
entries.parent_company: Kansas Department for Children and Families (DCF)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; administered directly by DCF (apply online or through local DCF Service Centers)
entries.senior_programs: Households where every member is 62 or older and income is only Social Security or KPERS may qualify for continuous eligibility for up to three years, so they do not have to fully reapply every year.
entries.notes: LIEAP is a once-a-year benefit for heating costs; there is no separate year-round crisis program. The application window is short and typically runs from about January 20 to March 31; check the DCF page for the next period's dates. Income limit: gross monthly income at or below 150% of the federal poverty level (1 person $1,995; 2 people $2,705; 3 people $3,415; 4 people $4,125; add $710 per extra person). Apply online through the DCF Self-Service Portal (cssp.kees.ks.gov), or get a paper application from a local DCF Service Center. Provide proof of all earned and unearned income, copies of all fuel/utility bills, proof of child support paid if any, and a rental or lease agreement if utilities are in the landlord's name. Questions: DCF Benefits Assistance 1-888-369-4777. For other emergency help, call 211 or 1-800-CHILDREN (1-800-244-5373); utility charity funds (Evergy Project DESERVE for people 65+ or with disabilities, Kansas Gas Service Share the Warmth, Atmos Sharing the Warmth) can also help.

entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by Community Action Kentucky member agencies and county outreach offices
entries.senior_programs: Households with a member who has a catastrophic illness may keep up to $4,000 in liquid assets instead of $2,000. A LIHEAP eligibility certificate (certificate of need) from the local agency gives a 30-day shutoff extension and winter reconnection rights with gas and electric utilities.
entries.notes: Components: Subsidy (heating help, typically November-December), Crisis (typically early January to mid/late March or until funds run out; requires a disconnect notice, past-due bill, or running out of fuel), and Summer Cooling only when extra funds are available. Income limit: at or below 130% of the federal poverty level; liquid assets up to $2,000. Crisis may require a co-payment for households at 75% of poverty or above. Apply through your county's community action agency (directory at capky.org/network; many offices offer online appointment scheduling or a dedicated LIHEAP phone line). Bring: recent utility bills with account numbers, proof of all household income (pay stubs, Social Security, disability, pension), any final termination notice, proof of address, Social Security numbers/cards for everyone in the household, and proof of citizenship or permanent residency. State toll-free line: 1-800-456-3452.

entries.name: Kentucky Medicaid Estate Recovery (DMS Third Party Liability Branch)
entries.parent_company: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services, Department for Medicaid Services
entries.mail_payment_address: Department for Medicaid Services, Division of Program Integrity, Third Party Liability Branch, 275 East Main Street, 6E-A, Frankfort, KY 40621
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: Official MAP-708 Estate Recovery fact sheet: after the member dies, contact the Third Party Liability Branch 502-564-4958 (while living: Eligibility Policy Branch 502-564-6890). Hardship (estate is only income source for remaining family) can stop recovery and may be appealed. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Kentucky Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric, gas, water and sewer utilities and rural electric cooperatives (not municipal utilities)
entries.senior_programs: No age-based or calendar moratorium. Medical certificate: shutoff is delayed 30 days if a physician, registered nurse or public health officer certifies in writing that it would aggravate a resident's debilitating illness or infirmity; the utility can refuse further extensions unless the certificate comes with an agreed partial payment plan. Customers with a medical certificate or certificate of need get partial payment plans based on ability to pay, with accounts current by October 15.
entries.notes: Winter (Nov 1 - Mar 31) protections under 807 KAR 5:006: (1) Certificate of need: if you get a termination notice between Nov 1 and Mar 31 and present a CHFS/community action agency certificate showing LIHEAP eligibility or income at or below 130% of poverty within the 10-day notice period, gas or electric shutoff is delayed 30 days, provided you make a payment you can afford and agree to a plan to be current by October 15. (2) Winter hardship reconnection: if already disconnected, the utility must reconnect Nov 1 - Mar 31 if you present a certificate of need (with a weatherization referral), pay 1/3 of the balance or $200, whichever is less, and agree to a payment plan. Medical certificate: 30 days (Section 15). No temperature-based rule. Call the utility first, then the PSC Consumer Services line 1-800-772-4636 (502-564-3940; TTD 1-800-648-6056), email psc.info@ky.gov, or file an online inquiry/complaint.

entries.name: Kentucky Weatherization Assistance Program (Kentucky Housing Corporation)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by community action agencies and other nonprofits
entries.notes: Free home energy retrofits for low-income households (generally up to 200% of the federal poverty level): insulation, sealing, duct repairs, and heating equipment replacement if needed; households often save up to $500 a year. Apply through your local community action agency (directory in help link). KHC: 502-564-7630 or 1-800-633-8896 (toll-free in KY), 8 a.m.-5 p.m. ET weekdays. Louisville/Jefferson County residents can also use Project WARM (502-636-9276); LG&E and KU customers can ask about the WeCare program, which prioritizes elderly and disabled households.

entries.service_area_detail: Louisville, KY parking citations

entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: Pay the parish clerk or city court.

entries.name: Louisiana DCFS Child Support Enforcement

entries.notes: Main page directs to LA CAFE online account for case details. Payments go through the local location or the channels above.

entries.name: Louisiana LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Louisiana Housing Corporation)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications and crisis appointments handled by local community action agencies in each parish
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior program on the state page; seniors apply through the same local parish agency. Some utility charity funds target elderly and disabled customers (e.g., Cleco Power of Sharing via the Louisiana Association of Councils on Aging, 1-800-622-6537; Entergy The Power to Care, 1-800-368-3749).
entries.notes: Helps pay heating or cooling bills, crisis (shutoff) bills, and can repair/replace heating or cooling equipment. Seasons: Heating Dec 15 - Mar 31; Cooling Apr 13 - Sep 30; Crisis year-round (Oct 1 - Sep 30). One LIHEAP benefit per season; funds are limited. Apply through the statewide LIHEAP online portal when it is open, or contact your local parish agency (directory in help link). Crisis help is never taken online; call the local agency for a crisis appointment. Income limit is 60% of state median income (2026: about $30,618/yr for 1 person, $40,039 for 2, $58,882 for 4). You must be responsible for the energy bill and have an active heating/cooling utility account. Bring: utility bills no older than 30 days; all pay stubs from the last 30 days; proof of Social Security, pension, retirement, disability or other unearned income; shutoff/disconnect notice (crisis only); proof of address (lease, deed, rent receipt); photo ID and Social Security cards for household members. LIHEAP is free; LHC and agencies never ask for passwords or bank/card numbers.

entries.notes: LDH Long-Term Care page, Medicaid Estate Recovery section: claim requests via the TPL Recovery Portal (lamedicaid.com) or email/fax (225) 342-1376; payment by personal check, money order or cashier's check payable to Louisiana Department of Health, mailed to the P.O. Box above (page shows ZIP 70802-3558 in one place and 70821-3558 in another). Claim accrues no interest. Waiver automatic when a child heir's family income is <=300% FPL; other hardship waivers on request; deferral while spouse survives. LTC contact line 1-800-230-0690.

entries.name: Louisiana Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric, gas, water and sewer utilities and all electric cooperatives (not city-owned utilities such as New Orleans' Entergy New Orleans or municipal systems)
entries.senior_programs: Louisiana has no age-based shutoff ban. Weather-based protections apply to everyone. If someone in the home depends on medical equipment, tell the utility and ask about its medical/critical-care listing, then call your Commissioner's office if a shutoff is threatened.
entries.notes: Weather rules (LPSC General Order): regulated utilities may not disconnect residential service for nonpayment when the temperature is forecast to be 32 F or below, or when the National Weather Service has issued a heat warning/advisory for the area. To complain, contact your elected Commissioner's district office (find it on the LPSC district map) by phone, email, mail or fax; give your name, address, parish, phone, the company name and a short statement of facts. Main office: 225-342-4999 or 1-800-256-2397, 602 N. Fifth St., 12th Floor, Baton Rouge, LA 70802. Municipal utilities are not regulated by the LPSC; complain to the city instead.

entries.name: Louisiana Weatherization Assistance Program (Louisiana Housing Corporation)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by regional community action agencies (provider map on the program page)
entries.senior_programs: Extra waiting-list points for elderly (60+), people with disabilities (SSI-standard), families with children 17 and under, and high energy users / high energy burden households.
entries.notes: Free home energy improvements such as insulation, air sealing, weather-stripping and duct sealing to cut heating and cooling bills. Income-based (generally up to 200% of the federal poverty level); service is not guaranteed and there is a waiting list. Apply through the weatherization provider for your parish/region (contacts and phone numbers listed on the program page).

entries.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric, gas and private water companies (Eversource, National Grid, Unitil, Liberty, Berkshire Gas, etc.); not municipal light plants or town water departments
entries.senior_programs: If all residents of the home are 65 or older, electric or gas service cannot be shut off without DPU permission. With financial hardship, service also cannot be shut off without DPU permission if someone in the home is seriously ill, there is an infant under 12 months, or all adults are 65+ and a minor child lives there. Private water companies cannot shut off water if everyone is 65+, someone is seriously ill, there is an infant, or all adults are 65+ with a minor child. Serious illness needs a doctor's note sent to the utility, which must be renewed periodically under the DPU rules.
entries.notes: Winter protection: Nov 15 - Mar 15, gas or electric service used for heat cannot be shut off for a household with financial hardship without DPU permission (rule: 220 CMR 25.00). If service is shut off and you qualify, call the utility first; they will ask for proof (doctor's note, birth certificate, or proof of income/hardship). If not restored, or if a shutoff is about to happen, call the DPU Consumer Division at 617-737-2836 or 1-877-886-5066, email DPUConsumer.Complaints@mass.gov, or file online. Town/city water: contact the municipality. Oil, propane and wood have no legal shutoff protections; contact the dealer and, if needed, the Attorney General's Consumer Hotline 617-727-8400. Apply for fuel assistance to get discount rates and help with bills.

entries.name: Massachusetts Good Neighbor Energy Fund (Salvation Army)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide Massachusetts; any heating source
entries.senior_programs: No age rule; for households (including retirees on fixed income) above LIHEAP limits but in a temporary crisis.
entries.notes: Emergency energy grant for Massachusetts residents in temporary financial hardship who do not qualify for state/federal fuel assistance. Household income must be between 60% and 80% of state median income (2025-26: single person about $53,586-$71,447). Apply through your local Salvation Army Corps Community Center: area codes 339, 351, 508, 617, 774, 781, 857, 978 call 1-800-334-3047; area code 413 call 1-800-262-1320. Bring a recent fuel bill or delivery ticket.

entries.name: Massachusetts LIHEAP - Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP / fuel assistance) (Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities)
entries.parent_company: Massachusetts Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications through local fuel assistance agencies (mostly community action agencies) by city/town
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window. Returning households get a renewal application in the mail each year and can renew online, in person or by mail. HEAP-eligible households automatically get utility discount rates on investor-owned electric and gas bills. Mass 211 answers questions 24/7 with translation.
entries.notes: Helps pay part of winter heating costs (oil, electricity, gas, propane, kerosene, wood, coal), Nov 1 - Apr 30; payments go directly to the heating vendor. Homeowners and renters (including heat-included-in-rent) can apply. Online applications open Oct 1 each year; apply online, in person, or by mail; first-time applicants need an intake appointment with the local agency. Must reapply every year. FY2027 income limit 60% of state median income: 1 person $53,585; 2 $70,073; 3 $86,561; 4 $103,049. Bring: photo ID, list of household members, heating company name and account number, lease or mortgage statement, proof of income for the 30 days before applying (wages, pension, Social Security). The same application covers HEARTWAP (emergency heating system repair/replacement) and Weatherization. Cold Relief Heatline 1-800-632-8175 finds your local agency. It is free; beware of anyone charging an application fee.

entries.notes: Free full-scale home energy efficiency work (average about $4,725 of measures): air sealing, attic/wall/floor insulation, pipe and duct insulation, limited energy-related repairs, plus a heating system evaluation and combustion safety testing. Eligible if HEAP-eligible (60% of state median income) or someone receives TAFDC or SSI. Homeowners and tenants (with landlord permission). The HEAP fuel assistance application is also the weatherization application; apply online from Oct 1 or at your local agency. Mass Save and municipal utility programs offer additional no-cost efficiency help.

Payment instructions are in the claim letter; no public online payment. Online applications only, Tuesdays and Wednesdays 9 a.m.-noon, with a daily cap. The grant does not cover the whole balance; you pay part.

entries.name: Maryland LIHEAP - Office of Home Energy Programs (MEAP, EUSP & Arrearage Retirement) (Maryland Department of Human Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; local OHEP offices in every county and Baltimore City
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window; the program is open year-round so seniors can apply any time. A physician certification form (DHS-FIA-810) is part of the application packet for households with medical needs. Benefits do not reduce Social Security, SNAP or other benefits. Proxy authorization form (DHS-FIA-811) lets a caregiver apply on someone's behalf.
entries.notes: One application covers: MEAP (heating bill help, paid to the fuel supplier/utility), EUSP (electric bill grant, once per July-June program year; budget billing optional), and Arrearage Retirement Assistance (up to $2,000 toward a past-due electric bill and up to $1,000 toward past-due gas; past-due balance must be $300+; once every five years). Year-round program; reapply each July-June year. You do not need a turn-off notice; apply early. With a turn-off notice, contact your local OHEP office; once an application is received, OHEP can request a 55-day hold on the account. Winter crisis help runs Nov 1 - Mar 31 (Crisis Season Declaration form DHS-FIA-805). Utility Service Protection Program (USPP) protects MEAP-eligible customers from heating-season turn-offs if they stay on even monthly budget billing. Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov, by phone 1-800-332-6347, by mail, drop box or in person at the local OHEP office. FY27 monthly income limits: 1 person $2,660; 2 $3,607; 3 $4,553; 4 $5,500. Bring: photo ID, proof of residency, Social Security cards for everyone, gross income for the last 30 days, recent utility bill and heating fuel bill, termination notice if any. Check status at myohepstatus.maryland.gov.

entries.name: Maryland Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates gas, electric, water and telephone utilities (BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, Potomac Edison, Washington Gas, SMECO, etc.)
entries.senior_programs: Serious illness / life support: notify the utility before the termination notice expires; a doctor, nurse practitioner or physician assistant may need to complete the Commission-approved certification form, which must reach the utility no later than the day before the scheduled shutoff. The utility then holds off for an additional 30 days, during which you must enter a payment agreement. No age-based ban, but the Nov-Mar affidavit rule protects occupants whose health or life would be threatened.
entries.notes: Winter (Nov 1 - Mar 31): a gas or electric utility may not shut off residential service for nonpayment unless it first files an affidavit with the PSC at least 24 hours ahead certifying the shutoff does not threaten the life or health of the occupants (valid 12 days after the last contact). Cold rule: no shutoff when the 6 a.m. forecast is 32 F or below. Heat rule: no electric (or gas used for cooling) shutoff when the 6 a.m. forecast is 95 F or above. With a termination notice: call the utility first to ask for an extension or payment plan, apply to OHEP (1-800-332-6347) and Fuel Fund of Maryland. PSC Consumer Affairs Division: 1-800-492-0474 (option 3, then 1) or 410-767-8028, Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-noon and 1-4 p.m.; TTY 1-800-201-7165. Complaints and extension/payment-arrangement requests can be filed online.

entries.name: Maryland Weatherization Assistance Program (Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development)
entries.parent_company: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local weatherization agencies
entries.senior_programs: Priority goes to people over 60, people with disabilities, households with children, and high energy users or high energy burden households.
entries.notes: Free home energy-saving improvements and health/safety repairs after a home inspection, for income-eligible homeowners and renters. Income limit is 60% of state median income (2026: about $48,085 for 1 person, $62,880 for 2, $92,470 for 4). Automatically income-eligible if you currently get OHEP energy assistance, SNAP, TANF, SSI or HUD housing assistance. Apply by contacting your local weatherization agency (list in help link); the agency checks eligibility and schedules an energy audit. OHEP energy assistance applicants are also referred to DHCD for weatherization and EmPOWER energy-efficiency programs.

entries.name: Constellation Home Services (formerly BGE HOME) service plans
entries.service_area_detail: Maryland (Baltimore), Pennsylvania, Texas, Georgia
entries.payment_processor: Constellation Home account platform (one-time guest payment, autopay, paperless)
entries.notes: HVAC, plumbing, water heater and electrical service plans. Payment page offers One-Time Payment as Guest, Enroll in AutoPay, and account login to view statements/contract details; paperless billing available. This bill is separate from a Constellation energy bill (pay that at constellation.com). Plans: https://www.constellationhome.com/md/home-service-plans. SCAM/SALES WARNING: service-line and appliance plan offers often arrive as mailers styled like an official city or utility notice ('your water line is not covered'); they are optional, unregulated products. Unpaid plan charges cannot legally cause utility shut-off. Utility impostor calls demanding immediate payment by gift card/crypto/payment app are scams - call the number on the real bill. Payment page also lists an automated pay-by-phone line (833-351-2609) and billing inquiries at 888-243-4663 (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm). AutoPay is managed (and stopped) in the new customer account platform.

entries.name: Maine LIHEAP - Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) (MaineHousing)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications through local Community Action Agencies (CAAs) or online
entries.senior_programs: No separate age-based window; apply as early as possible since funds run out. If income is over the limit, part of medical expenses may be deducted. Electric customers on oxygen pumps or ventilators 8+ hours a day may qualify for a utility Oxygen Pump/Ventilator Assistance Program through the CAA.
entries.notes: Helps homeowners and renters pay heating costs (fuel, emergency delivery, energy-related repairs and utility payments). 2026-27 HEAP applications open Aug 3, 2026 and run until funds are exhausted or May 29, 2027. Crisis: Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP) for an extremely low heating-fuel supply, Nov 1, 2026 - Apr 30, 2027; file a HEAP application first, then call your CAA. Apply online (MaineHousing online application), by phone, or in person by appointment with your local CAA (find by zip code). 2026-27 gross income limits: 1 person $38,070/yr; 2 $49,784; 3 $61,498; 4 $73,213. Bring: names, birth dates, Social Security numbers and proof of citizenship for everyone in the household; proof of gross income (Social Security, pension, wages, disability, etc.); recent full energy/utility bills showing usage; heating fuel type. HEAP-eligible electric customers can also get a bill credit through their utility's Low Income Assistance Program (LIAP), and HEAP applicants are automatically considered for Weatherization and the Central Heating Improvement Program (CHIP).

entries.name: Maine Public Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates electric transmission/distribution utilities (CMP, Versant), gas, water and telephone utilities
entries.senior_programs: Medical emergency (Chapter 815, Section 11): a utility may not disconnect when a doctor, PA or nurse practitioner certifies (orally or in writing) that lack of service would seriously harm someone in the home. Once you tell the utility a certification is coming, it must wait at least 3 business days; written confirmation may be required within 7 days. Protection lasts for the period certified or 30 days, whichever is less, and can be renewed twice in 12 months (3 certifications per home per year). If already disconnected, service must be restored by 5 p.m. the next day. Households at or below 150% of poverty or on HEAP or SSI can get a winter Special Payment Arrangement.
entries.notes: Winter Disconnection Period Nov 15 - Apr 15: electric and gas utilities cannot disconnect a residential customer without advance permission from the PUC's Consumer Assistance and Safety Division, and you get a chance to be heard. Contact the utility first to set up a payment arrangement; Special Payment Arrangements are offered Nov 1 - Mar 15. Heat rule: no disconnection while a National Weather Service Heat Advisory or Excessive Heat Warning is in effect for your area. Rule: MPUC Chapter 815 (Consumer Protection Standards). File complaints online, by phone, letter or fax; for an imminent shutoff call the Consumer Assistance Hotline 1-800-452-4699 or 207-287-1597 (Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-4 p.m.); TTY 1-800-437-1220. Keep paying undisputed amounts while a complaint is reviewed.

entries.name: Maine Weatherization Assistance Program (MaineHousing)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local Community Action Agencies
entries.senior_programs: No age-specific rules stated; applying for HEAP automatically considers the household for Weatherization and heating system repair/replacement (CHIP).
entries.notes: Free home energy assessment, then no-cost improvements such as air sealing, insulation, heating system efficiency work, ventilation, lighting and some appliance replacement. Serves income-eligible homeowners, renters (landlord must approve) and owners of 2-4 unit buildings; eligibility is usually based on HEAP participation. Contact your local Community Action Agency to apply and ask about wait times. Work may be postponed for structural, electrical, moisture/mold problems, homes for sale, or homes weatherized in the last 15 years.

entries.name: MaineCare Estate Recovery Unit
entries.parent_company: Maine DHHS Office of MaineCare Services
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Email EstateRecoveryUnitQuestion.OMS@maine.gov. Page describes hardship waiver eligibility and caregiver-related exemptions. MaineCare recovers only what it paid for covered services, not the whole estate; a Care Given Waiver and other waivers can reduce or waive a claim. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

SCAM/SALES WARNING: service-line and appliance plan offers often arrive as mailers styled like an official city or utility notice ('your water line is not covered'); they are optional, unregulated products. Unpaid plan charges cannot legally cause utility shut-off. Utility impostor calls demanding immediate payment by gift card/crypto/payment app are scams - call the number on the real bill. Oncourse FAQ re-read: pay by Visa/MasterCard, check or ACH, monthly or annual, or on the utility bill where offered; plans auto-renew yearly unless you opt out; cancel by phone (utility-billed charges can appear on 1-2 more utility bills). Refunds: full refund within 30 days of enrollment; monthly plans end at the end of the billing cycle with no refund; annual plans get a refund for the unused term. Existing customers 1-855-800-5195 (24/7), new customers 1-877-513-8520, customersupport@oncoursehome.com.

entries.name: Michigan LIHEAP - State Emergency Relief (SER), Home Heating Credit & MEAP (Michigan Department of Health and Human Services)
entries.parent_company: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; SER through MDHHS county offices / MI Bridges; Home Heating Credit through Michigan Department of Treasury; MEAP through local agencies reached via 2-1-1
entries.senior_programs: Seniors 65+ qualify for the utility Winter Protection Plan (Nov 1 - Mar 31) regardless of income and are not required to make set monthly payments during the heating season; ask your utility to enroll. AARP and the Accounting Aid Society can help seniors file the Home Heating Credit form.
entries.notes: (1) State Emergency Relief (SER): year-round crisis help when heat or electric service has been or will be shut off, or you need deliverable fuel (oil, propane) or an energy-related home repair; eligibility based on immediate need, income and assets. You pay a required share (e.g., heat: $40 for 1 person, $53 for 2; electric: $22 for 1, $29 for 2) and SER can cover the rest. One heat and one electric payment per Oct 1 - Sep 30 year; heating fuel maximum about $600-$900 depending on fuel; home repairs limited to $4,000 lifetime. Apply online through MI Bridges or at your county MDHHS office. (2) Home Heating Credit: file form MI-1040CR-7 with Michigan Treasury (no income tax return needed); forms available mid/late January, deadline September 30; past recipients get forms mailed. (3) Michigan Energy Assistance Program (MEAP): bill payment and self-sufficiency help through local agencies; call 2-1-1 or visit mi211.org to be connected. An SER payment also qualifies you for MEAP self-sufficiency services.

entries.name: Michigan Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; regulates investor-owned electric and gas utilities (DTE, Consumers Energy, SEMCO, UPPCO, I&M, etc.) and rural electric cooperatives; not most municipal utilities
entries.senior_programs: Winter Protection Plan (Nov 1 - Mar 31) for anyone 65 or older, anyone on MDHHS cash or food assistance or Medicaid, or households at or below 150% of poverty: no shutoff during the period; seniors do not have to make specific monthly payments, low-income customers pay 7% of the estimated annual bill monthly; balances are paid in installments April - November. Medical emergency (R 460.133): shutoff postponed or service restored for up to 21 days using the commission-approved medical certification form (3-day grace period to get it); up to 63 days per household member or 126 days per household per year. Critical care customers (R 460.130), where loss of service would be immediately life threatening, cannot be shut off for nonpayment; certify annually with the utility's approved form.
entries.notes: Contact your utility as soon as you know you cannot pay; do not wait for a shutoff notice. Enroll in the Winter Protection Plan through your utility. Rules: Consumer Standards and Billing Practices, R 460.101 - R 460.169. Informal complaints: online, by phone 1-800-292-9555, or by mail to MPSC Customer Assistance, P.O. Box 30221, Lansing, MI 48909; the utility has up to 10 business days to investigate. Formal complaints can follow if unresolved. Active-duty military customers can get 90-day shutoff protection. Call 2-1-1 for utility assistance referrals.

entries.name: Michigan water bill assistance (MDHHS Water Assistance Program)
entries.parent_company: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; administered by Community Action Agencies by county (call 2-1-1 if your county is not listed)
entries.senior_programs: Households on SSI qualify automatically, which covers many seniors and people with disabilities.
entries.notes: Helps low-income residential water/sewer account holders with metered service: restoring shut-off water or wastewater service, paying past-due bills, preventing arrears, and supporting affordability plans. Up to $3,000 per fiscal year. Eligible if under 200% of the federal poverty level or receiving FIP/TANF, SNAP, State Emergency Relief, SSI, Weatherization, or WIC. Funded through Sept 30, 2031 unless funds run out. Apply through the Community Action Agency for your county (contacts on the program page) or call 2-1-1.

entries.name: Michigan Weatherization Assistance Program (Michigan Department of Health and Human Services)

entries.senior_programs: Automatic eligibility for people receiving SSI or MDHHS cash assistance, which covers many low-income seniors and people with disabilities.
entries.notes: Free energy conservation work for low-income homeowners and renters: wall and attic insulation, foundation insulation, air leakage reduction, smoke detectors, dryer venting. Can cut heating costs by 20-25%. Income at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines. Contact your county's weatherization operator (map in help link) to apply.

entries.name: Minnesota LIHEAP - Energy Assistance Program (EAP) (Minnesota Department of Commerce)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; administered by about 30 local service providers (community action agencies, tribal governments, counties)
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window. Receiving energy assistance is the gateway to utility discounts (Xcel Energy PowerOn and Gas Affordability Program, Minnesota Power CARE, Minnesota Energy Resources Gas Affordability), which can lower bills for fixed-income seniors. Household income under 50% of state median also triggers Cold Weather Rule protection from heat shutoff.
entries.notes: Helps pay heating bills and provides crisis help for shutoff notices, disconnections, or running out of delivered fuel. Season typically runs Oct 1 - May 31 for regular help, with crisis help available roughly Oct - early July while funds last. Income limit: household income at or below 50% of state median income. Apply online through the state Energy Assistance application portal, request a mail application, or apply through your local service provider (find by county). Call 1-800-657-3710 to find your local provider. Bring proof of household income, recent energy bills, and any disconnect notice for crisis help. Must reapply each season.

entries.name: Minnesota Public Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections (Cold Weather Rule)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; PUC regulates investor-owned utilities (Xcel Energy, Minnesota Power, Otter Tail, CenterPoint, Minnesota Energy Resources, etc.). Cold Weather Rule also covers municipal utilities and electric co-ops.
entries.senior_programs: No age-based shutoff ban. Medical protection (Minn. Stat. 216B.098 subd. 5): the utility must continue or reconnect service where a medical emergency exists or life-sustaining electric medical equipment is in use, once it gets written certification (or phone certification followed by writing within 5 business days) from a doctor, physician assistant, or advanced practice registered nurse. A certification lasts up to six months; it can be renewed. Households at or below 50% of state median income (including anyone receiving energy assistance) cannot have their primary heat disconnected Oct 1 - Apr 30 if they keep up with a payment agreement.
entries.notes: Cold Weather Rule (Minn. Stat. 216B.096 for investor-owned utilities; 216B.097 for co-ops and municipals), Oct 1 - Apr 30: if household income is at or below 50% of state median, the utility must not disconnect, and must reconnect, primary heat service as long as you enter and keep a payment agreement based on your finances. Above that income, you still have a right to a payment agreement that considers your financial resources. Utilities must send a disconnection notice with your rights, a list of energy assistance providers, and an inability-to-pay form. During the cold weather period, disconnection cannot happen on a Friday, weekend, holiday, the day before a holiday, or when utility offices are closed. You can name a third party (such as an adult child) to get copies of disconnection notices. Every utility must offer budget billing and payment agreements for arrears (216B.098). Complaints: call the utility first, then the PUC Consumer Affairs Office at 651-296-0406 or 1-800-657-3782 (consumer.puc@state.mn.us). Co-op members can appeal to the co-op board; municipal utility customers go to the city. The Attorney General's office also helps: 651-296-3353 or 1-800-657-3787.

entries.name: Minnesota Weatherization Assistance Program (Minnesota Department of Commerce)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local weatherization providers (largely the same agencies as Energy Assistance)
entries.senior_programs: Weatherization programs nationally give priority to households with elderly or disabled members; ask your local provider about current waiting-list priority.
entries.notes: Free energy-saving improvements (insulation, air sealing, heating system checks and repairs) for income-eligible homeowners and renters. Income limit generally 50% of state median income (200% of poverty for very large households). Applying for Energy Assistance also refers you for weatherization; or contact your local weatherization provider directly.

'Access Your DMP Account' = fconline.lssmn.org; DMP Support Team can supply login info. Changing/stopping electronic payment or cancelling: call DMP Support Team. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/. Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent.

entries.name: Missouri LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (Missouri Department of Social Services, Family Support Division)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications processed through local LIHEAP contracted agencies (mostly community action agencies)
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior benefit, but low-income seniors/disabled people using LIHEAP should also register with their gas/electric utility as an 'elderly or disabled customer' (65+ or disabled) for extra Cold Weather Rule protections.
entries.notes: Energy Assistance: one-time payment toward heating or cooling costs for one fuel type, season typically runs October - May. Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP): helps when you have a disconnect notice with a specific date, service already shut off, propane/fuel oil tank under 20%, or prepaid/other fuel about to run out. Winter ECIP typically Nov - May (up to $800); Summer ECIP typically June - September (up to $300); funding-based. Contracted agencies may also provide blankets, heating/cooling repair, window air conditioners. Eligibility: responsible for home utility bills (renters included), Missouri resident, U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident, $3,000 or less in bank/retirement/investment accounts, income at or below the program limit (about 60% of state median income). How to apply: online form at formsportal.mo.gov (then upload documents), or print/mail/fax/drop off the paper application at your local contracted agency; call 855-FSD-INFO (1-855-373-4636) to have an application mailed. Typical documents: recent utility bills, proof of gross income (pay stubs, Social Security, pension, disability letters), shutoff notice if any, proof of address and household members, proof of citizenship/residency. Decisions take about 30 business days.

entries.notes: MO HealthNet Cost Recovery page: Estate Recovery Program; estate notice to MHD.COSTRECOVERY@dss.mo.gov or fax 573-526-1162; release letter issued only after the estate claim is paid. No claim if spouse, child under 21 or blind/disabled child survives. Also recovers nursing-home personal-fund balances. If the participant had no assets at death, nothing more is collected and living dependents are never asked to repay. Authorized representatives get a questionnaire about the estate claim. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Missouri Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers investor-owned electric, gas, water, sewer and steam utilities (not municipal utilities, rural electric cooperatives or public water/sewer districts)
entries.senior_programs: Registered elderly or disabled customer: a household member who is 65+, has a doctor's form saying gas/electric service is needed to maintain life or health, or has a federal disability award letter can register with the utility (renew each year by Oct 1) and gets extra notices before any winter shutoff. Low-income registered elderly/disabled customers (income under 150% of poverty, affidavit on file) on a Cold Weather Rule payment plan only need to pay at least 50% of the monthly bill or budget amount during Nov 1 - Mar 31 to stay connected. Medical: the utility must postpone a shutoff up to 21 days if it would aggravate an existing medical emergency of anyone living in the home; be ready to give reasonable proof (20 CSR 4240-13.050(10)).
entries.notes: Cold Weather Rule (20 CSR 4240-13.055), Nov 1 - Mar 31, for heat-related gas/electric service from investor-owned utilities: no shutoff on a day the National Weather Service forecasts the temperature to drop below 32 F in the next 24 hours. To keep service if you cannot pay in full: contact the utility, say you cannot pay in full, give income information, make the minimum payment and sign a payment agreement; a 12-month budget plan with initial payment no more than 12% of the total must be offered if you have not defaulted before. Utilities must mail notice 10 days before shutoff and try to contact you within 96 hours before. Hot Weather Law, June 1 - Sep 30: no shutoff of service used for cooling if the forecast for the next 72 hours is above 95 F or heat index above 105 F. Before shutoff: try the utility first, then call the PSC Consumer Services hotline 1-800-392-4211 (Relay Missouri 711) or email pscinfo@psc.mo.gov to file an informal complaint (online or with the Informal Complaint Form). Office of the Public Counsel (consumer advocate): 1-866-922-2959. Co-ops and city utilities are not covered by these rules.

Income-eligible homeowners qualify, and renters qualify with the landlord's permission (income limit typically 200% of the federal poverty level). Apply through the local weatherization agency for your county (list on the DNR Local Weatherization Agencies page). Division of Energy: 573-751-2254 or toll-free 1-855-522-2796.

entries.name: Mississippi LIHEAP - Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (Mississippi Department of Human Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide (all 82 counties); administered through local Community Action Agencies (CAAs)
entries.senior_programs: Households with an elderly or disabled member (or a child 5 or under) are 'vulnerable households' and get the greatest priority. After applying online, elderly/disabled applicants should get a CAA appointment within 30 business days (others within 45 days).
entries.notes: Helps with heating and cooling bills (natural gas, electricity, wood, propane/butane). Heating season typically runs Oct 1 - Apr 30, cooling May 1 - Sep 30; the Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP) for emergencies (e.g. shutoff notice) runs year-round while funds last. Income limit: at or below 60% of state median income; must have an energy bill due to a utility or landlord. How to apply: submit a pre-application on Access MS (www.access.ms.gov) and check 'Community Services'; you will get a letter with an appointment at your local Community Action Agency to finish the application in person. Bring photo ID for adults 18+, Social Security numbers for all household members, income proof (Social Security/SSI award letters, pay stubs within 30 days, etc.), proof of residence, and copies of energy bills (CAA staff can help get bill copies). Bills must be in the head of household's or spouse's name, or bring a landlord statement/lease. MDHS Community Services: 1-800-421-0762. Tip: if LIHEAP approves enough to cover your past-due balance within 30 days, the utility cannot cut off service once notified (PSC rule).

entries.name: Mississippi Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PSC-regulated electric, gas, water and telecom utilities (most municipal utilities and some co-ops are not regulated)
entries.senior_programs: Medical protection: a utility cannot disconnect for 60 days when a licensed doctor (Mississippi or adjoining state) certifies in writing that shutoff would create a life-threatening situation for anyone in the home (Service Rule 8.125(1)). Customers age 60+ who are the primary user and account holder can ask the utility to waive or refund the deposit (Service Rule 9.100(2)). Ratepayers may designate a third party (e.g. family member or caregiver) to receive shutoff notices (Service Rule 6).
entries.notes: Mid-winter rule (Service Rule 8.120): for December through March, electric/gas customers in extreme financial difficulty can avoid shutoff by giving the utility a copy of the latest bill and a signed hardship statement before the cutoff time, paying all bills rendered before Nov 11, and paying the levelized monthly amount during winter; after April 1 they pay 133% of the levelized amount until caught up. Weather rules: no electric or gas shutoff if an NWS freeze warning is in effect for the county at 8 a.m. on the shutoff day; no electric shutoff during an NWS Excessive Heat Warning (Service Rule 8.125(3)). No shutoffs on weekends/holidays unless the utility is open to take payment and restore service. At least 5 days' written notice required. No shutoff if LIHEAP has approved payment covering the past-due amount within 30 days. Try to resolve with the utility first, then file a complaint with the PSC online or call 601-961-5434; district toll-free lines: Northern 1-800-356-6428, Central 1-800-356-6430, Southern 1-800-356-6429.

entries.notes: Free home energy improvements: ceiling/wall/floor insulation, air sealing, furnace repair or replacement, duct improvements and energy education. Eligibility: household income within 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (owners and renters). Apply by submitting a pre-application on Access MS (mark 'Community Services'); the local Community Action Agency then schedules an in-person appointment. Runs year-round while funds last.

entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications handled by local Human Resource Development Council (HRDC) / community action eligibility offices and Tribal LIHEAP offices
entries.senior_programs: Approved applications are ranked into priority groups; special priority is given to older adults and people with disabilities. Households receiving SSI, SNAP or TANF may qualify automatically. LIHEAP-eligible households also qualify for weatherization and may get electric bill discounts (e.g. NorthWestern Energy discount for LIHEAP households).
entries.notes: Pays part of winter heating bills (natural gas, electric, propane, fuel oil, wood, coal) and may help with furnace emergencies. Apply during the heating season, Oct 1 - Apr 30, at the local eligibility office or Tribal LIHEAP office for your county (phone numbers on the Local Eligibility Offices page). Use the combined LIHEAP and Weatherization application: it can be filled out online but must be printed and mailed or delivered to the local office listed on its last page. Homeowners and renters may apply. Income limit: about 60% of state median income (e.g. about $36,120 for 1 person, $47,234 for 2 in the 2026-27 table); resource limit about $14,717 for 1 person, $22,515 for 2 (savings, checking, CDs, stocks, rental property). Benefit depends on fuel type, home type and number of bedrooms. For emergency heat help, ask the local office about crisis/furnace assistance and Energy Share of Montana (one-time emergency help, 1-800-777-7589). DPHHS Human and Community Services Division: 406-444-1788.

entries.name: Montana Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PSC-regulated utilities such as NorthWestern Energy, Montana-Dakota Utilities and Energy West (not rural co-ops, municipal utilities or propane vendors)
entries.senior_programs: Winter moratorium Nov 1 - Apr 1: the PSC will not approve a winter shutoff by a regulated utility if a household member is 62 or older, a household member is handicapped, the account holder receives public assistance, or income is at or below the federal poverty guideline. You must tell the utility BEFORE the shutoff that one of these applies and may need to provide documentation. Medical exception (ARM 38.5.1411): service may not be cut off if a licensed physician, PA, APRN or RN certifies in writing that loss of service would aggravate an existing medical condition threatening a permanent resident's health; the certificate is valid 180 days and can be renewed every six months. The customer must still negotiate a reasonable payment arrangement.
entries.notes: Winter moratorium runs Nov 1 - Apr 1: regulated utilities may still disconnect in winter, but only with prior PSC approval, and the PSC will not approve it for protected households (62+, handicapped member, public assistance recipient, or income at/below poverty). Having children in the home does not by itself prevent shutoff. Under a medical certificate, if arrears reach $500 or more the customer must keep a monthly plan (average bill plus 1/12 of the arrears); no medical-account disconnection proceedings for arrears under $500, and the PSC may intervene and set a different plan if you have applied for bill assistance. Co-ops and propane dealers set their own winter policies. If you cannot resolve it with the utility, contact PSC Consumer Assistance at 1-800-646-6150 or 406-444-6150, email pschelp@mt.gov, or submit the online Request for Consumer Assistance form.

entries.name: Montana Weatherization Assistance Program (Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services)
