entries.notes: Improves heating efficiency of the home (insulation, air sealing, furnace work) after an energy auditor visits to pick the most cost-effective measures. Homeowners and renters may apply; households that qualify for LIHEAP also qualify for weatherization and energy education. Income limit 200% of the federal poverty level (about $31,920 for 1 person, $43,280 for 2). Apply any time of year with the combined LIHEAP and Weatherization application through your local eligibility office or Tribal LIHEAP office.

entries.name: North Carolina LIHEAP - Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) and Crisis Intervention Program (CIP) (NC Department of Health and Human Services)
entries.parent_company: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS), Division of Social Services

entries.senior_programs: Early sign-up: households with a person 60 or older, or a disabled person receiving services through the NC Division of Aging and Adult Services, can apply for LIEAP Dec 1 - 31, a month before everyone else. Heating income limit is higher for these households (150% of poverty instead of 130%). For the Crisis Intervention Program, the resource limit is $4,500 for households with a member 60+ or disabled (vs. $3,000).
entries.notes: LIEAP is a one-time payment sent to your heating vendor. Season typically runs: Dec 1 - 31 for 60+/disabled households; Jan 1 - Mar 31 (or until funds run out) for all others. Apply online through ePASS (epass.nc.gov) or at your county DSS. Income limit is 130% of the federal poverty level (150% for households with someone 60+ or disabled); you must be responsible for your heating costs. Bring ID, proof of address, income, resources, and a copy of your heating bill. Crisis Intervention Program (CIP): year-round (Jul 1 - Jun 30, until funds run out) for households with no heat or cooling, or a disconnect notice for their primary heating/cooling, where someone's health is at risk; income up to 150% of poverty; apply at county DSS by mail, email, fax or drop-off with a copy of the bill showing the amount owed. entries.name: North Carolina Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: North Carolina Utilities Commission (NCUC) / Public Staff Consumer Services Division
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers NCUC-regulated electric and natural gas utilities (not most co-ops or city utilities)
entries.senior_programs: Winter protection (NCUC Rules R12-10 gas and R12-11 electric): for bills rendered Nov 1 - Mar 31, the utility cannot disconnect without the Commission's express approval if (a) someone in the household is 65 or older or handicapped, (b) the customer cannot pay in full or on a payment plan, and (c) the county DSS certifies the household is eligible for energy crisis assistance (even if funds have run out). Ask DSS for this certification and tell the utility before the shutoff date. You can also name a third party (such as a relative) to get copies of any shutoff notice.
entries.notes: Utilities must give at least 10 days' written notice before disconnecting, a supervisor must approve each disconnect, and the field representative must try to contact you at the home before cutting service (they may defer for death or illness or set up credit arrangements). The disconnect notice must tell you to call your local social services office for assistance. No temperature-based or summer heat rule at the state level. Talk to the utility first and ask for a supervisor; if unresolved, call the Public Staff Consumer Services Division at 1-866-380-9816 or 919-733-9277 (Mon-Fri 8-5) or email consumer.services@psncuc.gov; a formal complaint with the Commission is the last step.

entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications processed through the HHS Customer Support Center and human service zones; tribal LIHEAP programs serve members on reservations
entries.senior_programs: If you need help applying, a Community Options outreach worker can come to you and help with the LIHEAP application (call 1-800-823-2417). Approved households can also get help buying or repairing an air conditioner or cooling device through their Community Action agency.

Emergency (crisis) help: call the Customer Support Center (1-866-614-6005 or 701-328-1000, 711 TTY); if electricity is not your main heat, take your LIHEAP approval notice to your Community Action Partnership agency for Energy Share help with emergency electric costs. entries.name: North Dakota Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; rules cover investor-owned utilities (Xcel Energy, Montana-Dakota Utilities, Otter Tail Power, Great Plains Natural Gas, Dakota Natural Gas); co-ops and city utilities set their own policies
entries.senior_programs: Customers 65 or older or with a disability must get the 10-day disconnect notice delivered in person, not just mailed. You can postpone a disconnect for up to 30 days by telling the utility during the 10-day notice period that you are 65+, have a disability, or that dangerous health conditions exist (N.D. Admin. Code 69-09-02-05.1). Register ahead of time: each fall utilities mail a postcard asking whether anyone in the home is 65+, disabled, or has an emergency medical problem (such as dialysis or other life-sustaining equipment), and whether social services or a third party (like a family member) should be notified of any proposed disconnect; you can also call the utility for this form.
entries.notes: There is no winter moratorium or temperature rule in North Dakota; disconnection is allowed in winter if the notice rules are followed. Utilities must give 10 days' written notice, offer a payment plan for past-due bills, and cannot disconnect on Fridays, weekends, state holidays, the day before a holiday, or after noon on any day. You can pay the past-due amount to the utility worker before disconnection. Landlords who include utilities in rent must warn tenants 10 days ahead and tenants may open service in their own name. Contact the utility first; if unresolved, file an informal complaint by calling the PSC at 701-328-2400 (TTY 800-366-6888), emailing ndpsc@nd.gov, or by letter with your account number, bill copies and the relief you want; investigations usually take 2-4 weeks.

entries.name: Nebraska LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services)
entries.parent_company: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; administered directly by DHHS (ACCESSNebraska) with weatherization through DWEE
entries.senior_programs: Cooling assistance (June 1 - Aug 31) is available only to LIHEAP-eligible households with a member age 70 or older, a child under 6 on ADC, someone with a severe illness aggravated by heat (healthcare provider completes form IM-55, which DHHS provides on request), or who received a DHHS air conditioner in the past 4 years. Window air conditioner purchase help is tied to cooling eligibility.
entries.notes: Heating assistance: one payment per season to the utility; heating season Oct 1 - Mar 31. Cooling assistance: June 1 - Aug 31 (restricted to certain households, see senior programs). Crisis Assistance: year-round payments (including deposits and reconnect fees) when an unexpected medical/household expense, job or wage loss, loss of a wage earner, illness/injury or death caused inability to pay within the last 90 days. Furnace or central A/C repair/replacement up to $750. Income limit: at or below 150% of the federal poverty level (Oct 2026 - Sep 2027: $23,940 for 1 person, $32,460 for 2). Must be responsible for home energy bills and meet citizenship/residency rules. How to apply: online through iServe Nebraska, in person at a DHHS office, or by calling ACCESSNebraska (Lincoln 402-323-3900, Omaha 402-595-1258, elsewhere 1-800-383-4278). Households with an active Economic Assistance case can request LIHEAP without a new application. If you have or expect a shut-off notice from your heating provider, call 1-800-383-4278 right away. DHHS also issues automatic heating payments to some eligible households when federal funds arrive (a notice is mailed).

entries.name: Nebraska Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; PSC regulates investor-owned natural gas utilities (Black Hills Energy, NorthWestern Energy). Electricity in Nebraska is supplied by public power districts, co-ops and municipal utilities, which the PSC does not regulate; municipal gas utilities are also not covered.
entries.senior_programs: Medical protection under state law (Neb. Rev. Stat. 70-1606, applies to gas and electric utilities including public power and city utilities): disconnection must be postponed for at least 30 days if a licensed physician, physician assistant or APRN certifies that a household member has an existing illness or handicap that would cause an immediate, serious health hazard if service were cut. The certificate must be filed with the utility within 5 business days of receiving the shutoff notice; only one postponement is required per instance of nonpayment. Utilities must also offer a third-party notice option so a relative or caregiver is notified of any proposed shutoff (70-1607).
entries.notes: Cold weather rule (PSC-regulated natural gas utilities Black Hills Energy and NorthWestern Energy): Nov 1 - Mar 31, the utility cannot shut off service without allowing an extra 30 days to pay beyond the normal due date. There is no statewide temperature-based or summer heat moratorium. Shutoff notices must state your right to request a conference about a dispute before the disconnect date, and service cannot be cut while the conference is pending. If you cannot pay, contact the utility to arrange payment and apply for LIHEAP crisis help (1-800-383-4278). For complaints about a regulated natural gas utility, use the PSC Natural Gas Complaint Form or call 402-471-3101 / 1-800-526-0017 (Nebraska only). For public power or city utilities, contact the utility's board or the city.

entries.name: Nebraska Weatherization Assistance Program (Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment)
entries.parent_company: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide through eight local nonprofit/community action weatherization providers
entries.senior_programs: Preference is given to persons over 60, persons with disabilities and families with children under six. Households with someone receiving SSI or ADC are automatically income-eligible.
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency improvements after an energy audit (average about $7,500 in work). Income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Homeowners and renters (single-family, multi-family or mobile homes) can apply. Apply through the local weatherization provider for your area (links on the DWEE page; providers determine eligibility and schedule work). Funding is limited and waiting lists are common. Heating and Cooling Repair and Replacement Assistance (HCRRA, up to $5,000) is also handled by DWEE. DWEE energy office: 402-471-2186.

entries.name: Credit Advisors Foundation
entries.service_area_detail: Omaha, NE; nationwide by phone. NFCC member; UST-approved.
entries.notes: Client Login page on the members site. Call to change/stop deposits or cancel. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/. Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. Contact page (/about/contact) used for stop/cancel requests; info@creditadvisors.org.

entries.name: New Hampshire Department of Energy Consumer Services (utility complaints) - utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers regulated electric, natural gas, water, sewer and some telephone utilities (not municipal utilities, propane, heating oil, cable or cell service). Utility rules are set by the NH Public Utilities Commission (puc.nh.gov) and consumer complaints are handled by the Department of Energy Consumer Services Division.
entries.senior_programs: Winter period (Nov 15 - Mar 31): utilities must get Department of Energy approval before disconnecting a residential customer known to be 65 or older (En 1204.03(b)) - tell your utility your age. Medical emergency certification (En 1205.02): a physician, APRN, PA or mental health practitioner certifies a condition that would become dangerous if service is cut; with a payment arrangement on past-due balances it protects the account from shutoff. Each certificate lasts 90 days to one year as set by the provider and can be renewed an unlimited number of times. A phone call to the utility protects you at first if the written certification arrives within 15 days.
entries.notes: Winter period runs Nov 15 - Mar 31 (En 1202.20). During winter, an adult at the home must be notified in person or by phone 2 to 8 business days before shutoff; if the utility cannot reach anyone it must get Department approval. The Department will not approve a winter shutoff for a financial-hardship customer making good-faith payments; financial-hardship customers can choose a 12-month plan or pay 10% of the balance monthly over winter (provide hardship proof yearly). No winter shutoff for unpaid deposits. Arrears must exceed $450 (heating customers), $225 (electric non-heat) or $125 (gas non-heat) before a disconnect notice. If you have a social service appointment to review assistance eligibility, the utility must keep service on for 10 days after being notified. There is no temperature-based or summer heat moratorium. Contact your utility first; then call Consumer Services at 1-800-852-3793 (Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30), email consumerservices@energy.nh.gov, or write to Consumer Services, NH Department of Energy, 21 South Fruit Street, Suite 10, Concord NH 03301-2429. They mediate disputes and help set up payment plans but do not pay bills.

entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: Payments go through the local location or the channels above.

entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Recovers OAA/ANB/APTD cash assistance (always repaid) and Medicaid incl. MEAD received after 55; liens filed on homes of nursing-home residents after notice and hearing opportunity. Family/administrator may apply for hardship waiver. Email dhhs.estate.recoveries@dhhs.nh.gov; fax (603) 271-8135. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.

entries.name: New Hampshire LIHEAP - Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) (New Hampshire Department of Energy)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by five local Community Action Agencies (CAAs)
entries.senior_programs: Homebound applicants can call their local CAA to ask for a home interview, phone interview or mail-in application. Household vulnerability (e.g. elderly or disabled members) is one of the factors in eligibility and benefits. NH Adult and Aging Care: 1-866-634-9412.
entries.notes: Grant (not a loan) toward winter heating costs; benefits range about $100 - $2,177 (average about $1,045) based on income, energy costs, region and housing type. FAP can also help in a heating emergency by arranging an emergency fuel delivery, delaying a shutoff, or referring to other help; for no-heat emergencies call your local CAA. Season: heating benefits are for the winter heating season; winter crisis help typically runs Dec - Apr. Income limit: 60% of NH state median income (about $48,713 for 1 person, $63,702 for 2); homeowners and renters (including renters with heat in the rent) are eligible. How to apply: contact your local Community Action Agency for an appointment (Belknap/Merrimack 603-223-0043; Hillsborough/Rockingham CAPHR e.g. Manchester 603-647-4470; Southwestern Community Services Keene 603-352-7512; Strafford 603-435-2500 ext. 4001; Tri-County Carroll 603-323-7400, Coos 603-752-3248, Grafton 603-968-3560), or dial 211 / 1-866-444-4211 to find your agency. You can apply for Fuel Assistance, the Electric Assistance Program (monthly electric bill discount for Eversource, Liberty, Unitil and NHEC customers) and Weatherization at the same time. Neighbor Helping Neighbor (Eversource, Liberty, Unitil customers) and Project Care (NHEC) are last-resort funds through CAAs.

entries.name: New Hampshire Weatherization Assistance Program (New Hampshire Department of Energy)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local Community Action Agencies
entries.senior_programs: Serves low-income households most vulnerable to high energy costs; homebound applicants can ask the CAA for home, phone or mail-in application options.
entries.notes: Income limit: 60% of NH state median income (about $48,713 for 1 person, $63,702 for 2); homeowners and renters eligible. Apply through your local Community Action Agency; once income-eligible you are placed on a waiting list, then a certified energy auditor does a full home energy audit to decide which improvements qualify. Can be applied for together with Fuel Assistance and Electric Assistance. Questions: Weatherization@energy.nh.gov.

entries.name: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU), Division of Customer Assistance
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers BPU-regulated electric, gas, water and wastewater utilities
entries.senior_programs: Winter Termination Program (N.J.A.C. 14:3-3A.5): no shutoff of electric, gas, water or wastewater Nov 15 - Mar 15 for customers receiving Lifeline, LIHEAP, TANF, SSI, PAAD, General Assistance or USF, water-assistance applicants, or anyone who self-certifies they cannot pay due to unemployment, illness, medical expenses, or a recent death in the family; you must tell your utility you qualify. Medical emergency (N.J.A.C. 14:3-3A.2(i)): shutoff is barred for up to 90 days if a household member's medical emergency would be aggravated; the utility may require a written statement from a licensed medical professional and proof of inability to pay. The BPU can extend the 90 days for good cause if you request it in writing with an updated medical statement; service stays on while the request is reviewed.
entries.notes: Weather rules (N.J.A.C. 14:3-3A.2): no residential shutoff for nonpayment when the high is forecast at 32 F or below in the next 24 hours, or 90 F or above in the next 48 hours, for all customers. Shutoffs only 8 a.m.-4 p.m. Monday-Thursday, never on Fridays, weekends, state holidays or the day before a holiday. Once a year per utility you can request reconnection with proof of applying to USF, LIHEAP, PAGE or another assistance program, after a down payment of up to 25% of the balance. Call your utility first; if unresolved call the BPU Division of Customer Assistance at 1-800-624-0241 (out of state 609-341-9188) or file online. For an active shutoff, call rather than file online (online complaints are worked 9 a.m.-4 p.m. business days).

Case and payment history at caseinfo.njchildsupport.gov; no fee for check or money order by mail or at a local office. entries.name: New Jersey LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) and Universal Service Fund (USF) (New Jersey Department of Community Affairs)
entries.parent_company: New Jersey Department of Community Affairs (DCA), Division of Housing and Community Resources
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; apply online through DCAid or through the local community action agency for your county
entries.senior_programs: Applicants age 60+ or with a disability may apply and return the application by mail, or ask the county agency for a home visit. Separately, the state Lifeline Utility Assistance Program gives older adults and people with disabilities who meet PAAD eligibility rules or receive SSI a $225 yearly credit on electric/gas bills (or a $225 check for tenants whose utilities are in the rent); call 1-800-792-9745. Lifeline, LIHEAP, USF, SSI and PAAD recipients are protected from gas/electric/water shutoff Nov 15 - Mar 15 under the Winter Termination Program (tell your utility you qualify).
entries.notes: Applications are taken first come, first served Oct 1 through Jun 30 while funds last. Apply online at DCAid (dcaid.dca.nj.gov), or download and print the combined Home Energy/USF/Weatherization application and submit it to your county's community action agency. One application covers both LIHEAP (heating, medically necessary cooling, emergency fuel and heating-system repair/replacement) and the Universal Service Fund (USF), a monthly credit on gas/electric bills of up to $200. Income limit: gross income at or below 60% of state median income (about $51,273/yr for 1 person, $67,049 for 2 in FY2027). Must be responsible for heating/cooling costs; public-housing or rental-assistance tenants qualify for heating aid only if they pay heat directly. Medically necessary cooling benefit is $300. Emergency (crisis) help for past-due bills or no heat goes through the same local agency. Benefits for gas/electric are usually sent straight to the utility. Hotline 1-800-510-3102 (also Utilityhelp@nj211.org) to find your local agency. Bring proof of income for all household members and a recent utility/fuel bill.

entries.name: New Jersey Medicaid Estate Recovery
entries.parent_company: NJ Division of Medical Assistance & Health Services
entries.mail_payment_address: NJ DMAHS, Office of Legal and Regulatory Affairs, Attn: Estates, PO Box 712 - Mail Code #6, Trenton, NJ 08625
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Official DMAHS 'The NJ Medicaid Program and Estate Recovery - What You Should Know' PDF: estate recovery questions 609-588-2900; correspondence to the Office of Legal and Regulatory Affairs, Attn: Estates (address above). Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: New Jersey Weatherization Assistance Program (New Jersey Department of Community Affairs)
entries.parent_company: New Jersey Department of Community Affairs (DCA)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by county weatherization agencies
entries.senior_programs: The program specifically serves elderly, disabled and low-income residents. The combined LIHEAP/USF/Weatherization application lets energy-assistance applicants be referred for weatherization at the same time.
entries.notes: Free home energy repairs such as insulation, air sealing and heating-system repair or replacement for income-eligible homeowners and renters. Apply by contacting the weatherization agency that serves your county (contact list on the DCA page), or check the weatherization box on the LIHEAP/USF application. Low-income customers of PSE&G, JCP&L, Atlantic City Electric, NJ Natural Gas, Elizabethtown Gas, South Jersey Gas and Rockland Electric can also get free efficiency upgrades through the utility-funded Comfort Partners program (income up to 250% of poverty, or receiving LIHEAP, Lifeline, SSI, PAAD or similar).

entries.name: NJR Home Services Comfort Service Plans
entries.service_area_detail: Central/northern NJ (NJNG area)
entries.senior_programs: Discount on Comfort Service Plans for seniors over 62 and U.S. military veterans (call 877-466-3657).
entries.notes: Heating/cooling/water heater 'Comfort Service Plans' and generator maintenance plans; rates and sign-up form on site. SCAM/SALES WARNING: service-line and appliance plan offers often arrive as mailers styled like an official city or utility notice ('your water line is not covered'); they are optional, unregulated products. Unpaid plan charges cannot legally cause utility shut-off. Utility impostor calls demanding immediate payment by gift card/crypto/payment app are scams - call the number on the real bill. Plan page: contracts auto-renew for another year unless cancelled; a renewal letter is mailed 30-60 days before the renewal date; billed monthly (first bill includes the full year's sales tax). Contact NJRHSServiceAdvisor@NJResources.com.

entries.notes: Town WIPP portals are per-municipality. Largest: Brick Township Municipal Utilities Authority (NJ); Ridgewood Water (NJ); Jericho Water District (NY); Wayne Township Water & Sewer Utility (NJ); Wildwood Water Utility (City of Wildwood) (NJ); Evesham Municipal Utilities Authority (Evesham MUA) (NJ); Parsippany-Troy Hills Water & Sewer Utility (NJ); South Brunswick Township (NJ) Water Utility (NJ); Borough of Sayreville (NJ) Water & Sewer Department (NJ); info@edmundsgovtech.com, 888-336-6999; no public town directory, no resident autopay/e-bill help.

entries.name: New Mexico LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (New Mexico Health Care Authority)
entries.parent_company: New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA), Income Support Division (formerly Human Services Department)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; apply through YesNM online or at your local Income Support Division (ISD) office; some tribes and pueblos run their own LIHEAP
entries.senior_programs: Proof of disability is only needed if you do not already receive disability income. LIHEAP-eligible households (including seniors) cannot have gas or electric service shut off Nov 15 - Mar 15 if they have no past-due balance or stay current on a payment plan for amounts owed as of Nov 15, so applying before winter matters.
entries.notes: LIHEAP helps with heating and cooling costs and runs year-round. Apply online through the YesNM portal, or fill out the printable LIHEAP application (English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese) and turn it in at your nearest ISD office. Bring: ID for one adult, proof of household income for the last 30 days, proof of heating/cooling costs (a recent bill), immigration status if applicable. Crisis LIHEAP: ISD can act faster if your utility is disconnected, you have a disconnect notice (bring a copy), or you are almost out of wood, propane or other bulk fuel. After applying you are usually scheduled for an interview in about 10 days; a decision letter comes within 45 days, and you can request a Fair Hearing if denied. Income limit is about 150% of the federal poverty level.

entries.name: New Mexico Medicaid Estate Recovery Program (HCA / HMS)
entries.parent_company: New Mexico Health Care Authority, Medical Assistance Division (HMS/Gainwell vendor)
entries.mail_payment_address: NM Estates Program, P.O. Box 10530, Phoenix, AZ 85064
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: Official HCA estate recovery FAQ + Asset Identification form: forms/documents to NM Estates Program (address above), email nmestate@gainwelltechnologies.com or submissions.hms.com; toll-free 800-293-3973. Undue Hardship Waiver must be requested with documentation; heirs not personally liable. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: New Mexico Public Regulation Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (PRC), Consumer Relations Division
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PRC-regulated gas and electric utilities (rules in 17.5.410 NMAC)
entries.senior_programs: Seriously or chronically ill household member (17.5.410 NMAC): the utility will not disconnect if it receives, at least 2 days before the shutoff date, the utility's medical certification form completed by a licensed physician, physician assistant or nurse practitioner plus a financial certification form completed by an assistance agency; the certification is valid for 90 days from the doctor's signature. If already disconnected, service must be restored within 12 hours of receiving both forms. You still owe the bill. Utilities must keep records of households with disabled, elderly or other at-risk members they know about.
entries.notes: Winter moratorium (17.5.410.30 NMAC and NMSA 27-6-18.1): no gas or electric shutoff Nov 15 - Mar 15 for customers who qualify for LIHEAP, as long as they have no past-due balance or stay current on a settlement or installment plan for amounts owed as of Nov 15. To get this protection, apply for LIHEAP through HCA (1-800-283-4465). Utilities must send a 15-day written notice and a final contact at least 2 days before shutoff, and must offer installment agreements. If you dispute a bill, pay the undisputed part and the utility postpones shutoff until the dispute is resolved. If you cannot resolve a problem with the utility, call PRC Consumer Relations toll-free at 1-888-427-5772 or file an informal complaint online (complaints.nm-prc.org). No temperature-based or summer heat rule.

entries.name: New Mexico Weatherization Assistance Program - NM Energy$mart (Housing New Mexico | MFA)

entries.senior_programs: Priority goes to people over 60, people with disabilities, families with children, and high-energy-use homes. Households where someone receives disability income, SSI or TANF are automatically income-eligible.
entries.notes: Free weatherization (insulation, air sealing, heating-system and safety work) for owners and renters of houses and mobile homes. Otherwise income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (about $31,920 for 1 person, $43,280 for 2). Apply directly with the regional service provider, not Housing New Mexico: northern NM - Central New Mexico Housing Corp., 505-345-4949 or toll-free 855-345-4949; southern NM - Southwestern Regional Housing & Community Development Corp., Las Cruces, 575-523-1639; Navajo Nation - Red Feather Development Group, 928-440-5119. Renters need the landlord's signed consent.

entries.name: Nevada LIHEAP - Energy Assistance Program (EAP) (Nevada Division of Social Services)
entries.parent_company: Nevada Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Social Services
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; EAP offices in Carson City (north) and Las Vegas (south) plus community intake sites
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior benefit is listed; intake sites help with completing and mailing applications. Seniors with high out-of-pocket medical costs may qualify through the Crisis Intervention Component even if income is above 150% of poverty, since qualifying medical expenses are deducted.
entries.notes: Funded by federal LIHEAP plus Nevada's Universal Energy Charge. One annual benefit, usually paid directly to the energy provider; program year runs July 1 - June 30 and applications are taken year-round until funds run out. Income limit: gross monthly income at or below 150% of poverty (July 2026 - June 2027: $1,995/month for 1 person, $2,705 for 2). Must live in Nevada, meet citizenship rules and pay at least part of heating/cooling costs. Specialized programs: Fast-Track (expedited processing when energy service is about to be cut off and income dropped at least 15% in the last 2-5 months), Arrearage Payment (brings past-due heating/cooling bills current, once every five years when funded), and Crisis Intervention (chronic illness with out-of-pocket medical costs). How to apply: download the paper application (also vision-impaired and Spanish versions) or pick one up at an EAP office, Social Services office or intake site; return by mail, fax, DSS drop box/lobby, or email energyassistance@dss.nv.gov. Include proof of all household income for the last 30 days, ID for head of household, citizenship/legal status proof if born outside the U.S., recent heating/cooling bills, and a signed authorization if the bill is in someone else's name. Prior recipients can reapply about 11 months after their last benefit. EAP North (Carson City) 775-684-0730, EAP South (Las Vegas) 702-486-1404, toll-free 1-800-992-0900.

entries.name: Nevada Medicaid Estate Recovery
entries.parent_company: Nevada Office of the Inspector General / Division of Health Care Financing and Policy
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Nevada Office of the Medicaid Inspector General runs Medicaid Estate Recovery (MER); MER FAQ page has a State MER contact email (mer@dhcfp.nv.gov). DWSS form 6160-AF (Notification of Program Operation) states recovery may be waived, compromised or delayed for undue hardship and heirs get hardship application info at recovery. No phone published on the MER page. Recovery applies to recipients 55 or older or who were inpatients of a medical facility; the State may place a lien on the deceased recipient's property. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Nevada Public Utilities Commission (PUCN) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PUCN-regulated utilities such as NV Energy (Nevada Power and Sierra Pacific Power) and Southwest Gas
entries.senior_programs: Elderly or disabled households (tell the utility so it knows): the utility must notify an adult in the home at least 48 hours before shutoff, in person for electric service and in person or by phone for gas (NAC 704.390), and utilities must remind customers yearly that special assistance is available to elderly and disabled customers (NAC 704.385). They also get stronger extreme-temperature protection (see notes). Medical: shutoff is postponed 30 days when the utility gets a statement from a licensed physician, APRN or public health official that shutoff would be especially dangerous to a resident's health (advanced age and frailty can be considered), plus a customer statement that they cannot pay or can only pay in installments; the postponement can be extended another 30 days with a renewed certificate, and up to 90 days of installments must be allowed (NAC 704.370). No shutoff if someone in the home depends on a life-support device and is confined there (NAC 704.375).
entries.notes: Temperature-based shutoff ban (NAC 704.375): the utility must postpone a nonpayment shutoff when the National Weather Service forecasts extreme temperature in the next 24 hours. NV Energy north (Sierra Pacific): elderly/disabled 95 F or higher or 20 F or lower; others 105 F or higher or 15 F or lower. NV Energy south (Nevada Power): elderly/disabled in a pre-2000 mobile home 100 F or higher; other elderly/disabled 103 F or higher; others 105 F or higher; cold limits 20 F (elderly/disabled) and 15 F (others). Gas utilities: 105 F or higher or 15 F or lower for all customers. No shutoffs on weekends, holidays or the day before them; no shutoff for balances of $50 or less ($100 or less for smart-meter electric customers). To complain: contact the utility first, then the PUCN Consumer Complaint Resolution Division (most informal complaints handled in 3-5 business days): Northern Nevada 775-684-6100, Southern Nevada 702-486-2600, or use the online complaint form.

entries.name: Nevada Weatherization Assistance Program (Nevada Housing Division)
entries.parent_company: Nevada Department of Business and Industry, Housing Division
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide through three nonprofit agencies: Community Services Agency (Reno/northern counties), HELP of Southern Nevada (Las Vegas/Henderson), Rural Nevada Development Corporation (North Las Vegas and rural counties)
entries.notes: Free home energy upgrades for income-qualified homeowners and renters: air sealing, insulation, LED lighting, solar screens, weather-stripping, low-flow shower heads, and HVAC, refrigerator or water heater repair/replacement. Income limit: at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Landlords of eligible rental units may have to cover 50% of the cost. Steps: find the agency for your area, apply through that agency, then complete a home energy assessment before work is scheduled. Agencies: Community Services Agency (Carson City, Washoe, Churchill, Douglas, Lyon, Storey) 775-786-6023; HELP of Southern Nevada (Las Vegas, Henderson, southern rural Clark County) 702-795-0575.

entries.name: New York LIHEAP - Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) (NYS Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance)
entries.parent_company: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; administered by county departments of social services (HEAP Local District Contacts); NYC through HRA
entries.senior_programs: Households with a member age 60+, under 6, or permanently disabled get a $35 add-on to the Regular HEAP benefit. For Emergency HEAP, the resource limit is higher ($3,750 instead of $2,500) when a household member is 60+. Households with a member 60+ (or with a heat-sensitive medical condition) can qualify for the Cooling Assistance benefit (an air conditioner or fan installed, up to $800, or $1,000 for a wall-sleeve unit).
entries.notes: Season typically runs: Regular HEAP Nov - Apr (opens in early/mid November); Emergency HEAP Jan - Apr; Cooling Assistance spring - early summer; Heating Equipment Repair/Replacement and Clean and Tune open Oct 1 (both open now for 2026-27, homeowners only). One Regular benefit per season, paid to your heating vendor; base amounts $400 (gas/electric heat) to $900 (oil/kerosene/propane). Income: gross monthly income at or below HEAP limits (about 60% of state median income), or automatically eligible if receiving SNAP, Temporary Assistance or Code A SSI. Apply for Regular HEAP online at myBenefits.ny.gov (NYC: ACCESS HRA), in person at your HEAP Local District Contact, or by mailing the HEAP application (LDSS-3421). Emergency HEAP (heat or heat-related electric shut off or scheduled for shutoff, or less than 1/4 tank of oil/propane or 10 days of wood): call or visit your HEAP Local District Contact (NYC: 718-557-1399); not available online. Heating Equipment Repair up to $4,000 / replacement up to $8,000; Clean and Tune up to $500. Decision within 30 business days.

entries.mail_payment_address: NYS Office of the Medicaid Inspector General, Attention: OMIG Casualty & Estate Recovery Unit, 800 North Pearl Street, Albany, NY 12204 (correspondence only - not for payments)
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). entries.notes: OMIG runs NY Medicaid estate recovery with HMS. OMIG says do not send forms or payments to its Albany address; follow the notice received or contact HMS for submission instructions. Undue hardship: sole income-producing asset, or modest-value home (<=50% of county average) that is the heir's primary residence. NYC: HRA Division of Liens and Recovery (844) 449-3444, 375 Pearl St, 21st Fl, New York, NY 10038 (casualty liens; see LR-203 fact sheet). Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: New York State Department of Public Service (PSC) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: New York State Department of Public Service / Public Service Commission
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PSC-regulated electric, gas, steam and water utilities (HEFPA rules, 16 NYCRR Part 11)
entries.senior_programs: Elderly, blind or disabled (16 NYCRR 11.5(b)): if the customer is 62 or older, blind or disabled and everyone else in the home is 62+, 18 or under, blind or disabled, the utility must make a diligent effort to reach an adult in the home by phone or in person at least 72 hours before shutoff to work out a payment plan, and must contact social services if needed. Let your utility know you are in this group. Medical emergency (11.5(a)): no shutoff (or service restored) with a certificate from a doctor or local board of health; it lasts 30 days and can be renewed for 30 days (60 days for chronic conditions) with proof of inability to pay. Life-support equipment users get continued protection.
entries.notes: Cold weather period Nov 1 - Apr 15 (16 NYCRR 11.5(c)): before shutting off heat-related service, the utility must try to contact the household at least 72 hours ahead to check whether anyone's health or safety is at risk, and must refer at-risk households to social services; it cannot shut off customers unable to manage their own affairs if serious harm is likely. Call your utility first. Shutoff emergencies (final notice saying gas/electric will be cut in 48-72 hours): call the DPS shutoff hotline 1-800-342-3355 (Mon-Fri 7:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m.); do not use the online form. Other complaints: helpline 1-800-342-3377 (Mon-Fri 8:30 a.m.-4 p.m.) or the online complaint form. Relay users dial 711.

entries.name: Ohio Home Weatherization Assistance Program (HWAP) (Ohio Department of Job and Family Services)
entries.parent_company: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services (ODJFS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; services provided through local agencies in each county
entries.senior_programs: Priority is given to Ohioans over age 60, people with disabilities, households with children, and high energy use or burden households.
entries.notes: Free home inspection and energy-efficiency improvements. Income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (July 2026-June 2027: $31,920 for 1 person, $43,280 for 2); households that received SSI, TANF or HEAP (not Emergency HEAP) in the last 12 months are automatically income eligible, but you still must submit an application. Apply using the same Energy Assistance Application (online via OHID, by appointment, or by mail) through your local provider.

entries.name: Ohio LIHEAP - Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP) (Ohio Department of Job and Family Services)
entries.parent_company: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services (ODJFS); program moved from the Ohio Department of Development on April 6, 2026
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications handled by local Energy Assistance Providers (mostly community action agencies)
entries.senior_programs: Paper Energy Assistance Applications are available at local Area Agencies on Aging as well as local energy assistance providers, and you can apply by phone or in person by appointment (helpful for seniors without a computer; the online system does not work on phones or tablets). Ohioans 60+ or with disabilities also get priority for the Home Weatherization Assistance Program.
entries.notes: HEAP is a once-a-year payment applied directly to your utility or bulk-fuel bill; homeowners and renters qualify. Income limit: at or below 175% of the federal poverty level for households of up to 8 (July 2026-May 2027: $27,930/yr for 1 person, $37,870 for 2); larger households use 60% of state median income. Report gross income for the past 30 days (12 months preferred). Three ways to apply: online through the Energy Assistance Portal tile in your OHID account (PC browser only); by appointment in person or by phone with your local Energy Assistance Provider; or mail the signed application (JFS 00330) to your local provider. Processing can take up to 12 weeks. Bring: proof of income for every household member (SSI, SSDI, Social Security, pension, wages, etc.), recent utility bills, Social Security numbers and birth dates for all members, and proof of citizenship/legal residency. HEAP Winter Crisis Program (season typically runs Nov 1 - Mar 31): for households at or below 175% of poverty that are disconnected, threatened with disconnection, need to establish or transfer service, or have 25% or less bulk fuel; requires an appointment with your local provider (you can start online). Customers of PUCO-regulated utilities must join PIPP Plus or another payment plan for any remaining balance. A Summer Crisis Program helps with cooling in summer. PIPP Plus lets eligible customers (150% of poverty or less) pay a percentage of income toward gas/electric bills.

entries.notes: ODM may waive for undue hardship (Ohio Adm.Code 5160:1-2-07(H)); requests reviewed case by case. 14-day hold on lien releases for check/ACH payments. ODM may delay or waive recovery for undue hardship on survivors, reviewed case by case. Pay online through the Attorney General's Pay Online service (lien releases are held 14 days for check/ACH payments) or call 888-301-8885.

entries.name: Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PUCO-regulated electric and natural gas companies (Ohio Adm.Code 4901:1-18)
entries.senior_programs: Medical certification (Ohio Adm.Code 4901:1-18-06): a certificate from a licensed physician, physician assistant, clinical nurse specialist, certified nurse practitioner, certified nurse-midwife or local board of health physician stops a disconnection (or restores service) for 30 days if a household member's health would be endangered; it can be renewed two more times, 30 days each, up to 90 days per household in any 12 months. You must still set up a payment plan. Utilities advertise the medical certification program at the start of winter and summer. You can name a third party (e.g., an adult child) to receive copies of disconnect notices. There is no age-based shutoff ban in Ohio.
entries.notes: Winter (Nov 1 - Apr 15): before disconnecting, utilities must make an extra contact 10 days ahead (in person, by phone or hand-delivered notice) and tell you about energy assistance; they must offer a one-third payment plan in addition to the usual one-sixth and one-ninth plans. Each heating season the PUCO issues a Winter Reconnect Order that typically lets customers avoid or reverse a gas/electric shutoff once per season by paying the lesser of the amount owed or $175 (plus a reconnection fee capped around $36) and enrolling in a payment plan; HEAP Winter Crisis funds can cover the payment for income-eligible households. Every disconnect notice must be at least 14 days ahead. No temperature-based or summer heat moratorium. Call your utility first; if unresolved call the PUCO Call Center toll-free 1-800-686-7826 (8 a.m.-5 p.m. weekdays; 711 relay) or file an informal complaint online. The Ohio Consumers' Counsel (1-877-742-5622) also represents residential customers.

entries.name: Columbia Service Partners (Columbia Gas OH, VA, KY, MD, PA protection plans - Oncourse)
entries.parent_company: Oncourse Home Solutions, LLC (administered by American Water Resources)
entries.service_area_detail: Columbia Gas of Ohio, Virginia, Kentucky, Maryland and Pennsylvania service areas
entries.payment_processor: Oncourse Home Solutions (card/ACH/check) or partner utility bill where offered
entries.notes: Homeowner and renter plans (furnace/boiler, A/C, washer/dryer, refrigerator/range, electric lines, outside water & sewer lines; outside water+sewer about $5.99/mo). Not affiliated with Columbia Gas; not a regulated utility service. Utility pages: columbiagasva.com, columbiagasky.com, columbiagasmd.com /services/home-protection-plans. Cancel/refund per Oncourse FAQ. SCAM/SALES WARNING: service-line and appliance plan offers often arrive as mailers styled like an official city or utility notice ('your water line is not covered'); they are optional, unregulated products. Unpaid plan charges cannot legally cause utility shut-off. Utility impostor calls demanding immediate payment by gift card/crypto/payment app are scams - call the number on the real bill. Oncourse brands also include American Water Resources, NIPSCO Service Partners, Consumers Energy ASP and former Pivotal Home Solutions. Oncourse FAQ re-read: pay by Visa/MasterCard, check or ACH, monthly or annual, or on the utility bill where offered; plans auto-renew yearly unless you opt out; cancel by phone (utility-billed charges can appear on 1-2 more utility bills). Refunds: full refund within 30 days of enrollment; monthly plans end at the end of the billing cycle with no refund; annual plans get a refund for the unused term. Existing customers 1-855-800-5195 (24/7), new customers 1-877-513-8520, customersupport@oncoursehome.com.

entries.name: Oklahoma Corporation Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers OCC-regulated electric and gas utilities (e.g., OG&E, PSO, ONG); city utilities and most co-op/municipal matters are not covered
entries.senior_programs: Customers 65 or older or with a permanent disability that limits ability to pay can register in writing with their utility; when a shutoff notice comes, the OCC Consumer Services Division can ask the utility to delay disconnection 5 more business days (OAC 165:35-21-11). Life-threatening medical condition: ask the utility for a Life-Threatening Certificate/medical waiver form; it suspends electric disconnection for 30 days, and a doctor's verification returned within 30 days can add 30 more days (60 total). The customer still owes the bill.
entries.notes: No date-based winter moratorium. Weather rule (OAC 165:35-21-10): no electric shutoff for heating customers when the National Weather Service forecasts below 32 F in the next 24 hours, and no shutoff for cooling customers when the heat index is forecast or reaches 101 F or higher that day. Utilities must offer a 20-day delay while you seek government or charity aid, and payment plans. Contact the utility first; if unresolved call OCC Consumer Services 8:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m. weekdays: 1-800-522-8154 (outside OKC metro) or 405-521-2331 (OKC metro), email CS@occ.ok.gov, or file a Public Utility complaint online (form link at bottom of the complaint page).

entries.name: Oklahoma LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (Oklahoma Human Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; apply online at OKDHSLive.org during open enrollment or through local OKDHS county offices
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior application window. Life-threatening energy crisis help is available year-round for households with a member who needs lifesaving medical equipment or during extreme temperatures; call 405-522-5050 and choose the energy assistance option (a note from a licensed health care professional may be requested). Native Nation citizens may apply through OKDHS or a tribal program, but not both.
entries.notes: Three components, each open only during an enrollment period and closing when funds run out: Winter Heating (opened early January in 2026), Energy Crisis Assistance Program/ECAP (opened mid-April in 2026), and Summer Cooling (opened mid-July in 2026, closed mid-July). Check OKDHSLive.org; a red 'Apply for Energy Assistance' banner shows when enrollment is open. Income limit about 130% of the federal poverty level; heating benefit roughly $40-$500, cooling $150-$650, crisis up to $750. Must be responsible for paying the home energy bill and be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident; everyone on the same meter applies together; one payment per household per component. Apply online at OKDHSLive.org; upload proof using the 'Fast Pass Verification Upload' button or bring it to any OKDHS office. Mail: OKDHS LIHEAP, P.O. Box 25352, Oklahoma City, OK 73125. Email LIHEAP2@okdhs.org.

entries.notes: Energy assistance is available year-round while county funds last; you do not need a shutoff notice or past-due bill to apply. Income limit: at or below 60% of Oregon median income (gross income, by household size); must have documented energy costs; renters and owners eligible. Benefit is a one-time pledge paid directly to the utility (roughly $250-$750 for heating; crisis help up to about $1,000), and can take 2-3 billing cycles to post, so keep paying and ask your utility for a payment plan, telling them you have an energy-assistance appointment. entries.name: Oregon Public Utility Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PUC-regulated utilities (Pacific Power, PGE, Idaho Power, NW Natural, Avista, Cascade Natural Gas, some water companies); municipal and public utilities are not covered
entries.senior_programs: Emergency Medical Certificate: if someone in the household is under a doctor's care and needs electric or gas service (for example oxygen or refrigerated insulin), a qualified medical professional sends the certificate to the utility; it prevents immediate disconnection and lets you set up a more lenient payment plan or renegotiate one when hardship is shown. Certificates are time-limited (generally up to 6 months) and can be renewed. Disconnection can still happen if the plan is not kept. Medical certificate customers and income-qualified discount customers shut off just before a heat or air-quality event can ask for reconnection within 7 days. Does not apply to water utilities.
entries.notes: Severe weather moratoriums (energy utilities): no disconnection for nonpayment when the forecast is below 32 F (November-March), during a National Weather Service heat advisory, extreme heat watch or warning, or when the Air Quality Index is 100 or more (including wildfire smoke); utilities cannot disconnect until 48 hours after a heat event ends or 24 hours after AQI conditions end. If you were cut off within 72 hours before such an event, ask the utility to reconnect; reconnection fees cannot be required up front. Notice rules: electric and gas must send a 20-day notice and a 5-day notice and try to contact you on the shutoff day. Utilities must offer time-payment arrangements (typically 12 months). Call the utility first; if no satisfactory payment plan, call PUC Consumer Services at 503-378-6600 or 1-800-522-2404 (TTY 711), email puc.consumer@puc.oregon.gov (best), or file online at puc.oregon.gov/complaint.

entries.name: Pennsylvania LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (Pennsylvania Department of Human Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; apply online through COMPASS, by paper application, or at your County Assistance Office
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior-only window; older adults apply in the same season. You do not need to be on public assistance or have an unpaid heating bill, and renters and owners both qualify. Hearing-impaired callers can use 711.
entries.notes: The 2026-2027 LIHEAP season is scheduled to open November 2, 2026 (the season typically runs early November into April). Cash grant of $200-$1,000 paid directly to your utility or fuel dealer, based on household size, income and fuel type; it does not have to be repaid. Income limit is 150% of the federal poverty level (see the income table on the DHS page). Crisis grants are for heating emergencies: broken heating equipment or leaking lines, no fuel or less than a 15-day supply, main or secondary heat source shut off, or a utility termination notice for shutoff within 60 days. If you have not gotten a regular grant this season, apply for LIHEAP to be considered for crisis; if you already got one, call your County Assistance Office to report the emergency. Apply online at COMPASS (www.compass.state.pa.us) and check status at trackmybenefits.pa.gov. LIHEAP Hotline 1-866-857-7095.

entries.name: Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers PUC-regulated electric, natural gas, water, wastewater and steam utilities (not most municipal utilities or electric co-ops)
entries.senior_programs: Medical certificate: service will not be shut off (and can be restored) if a licensed physician, physician assistant or nurse practitioner certifies that someone in the home is seriously ill and termination would harm them. The initial certificate lasts up to 30 days, with renewals/extensions of up to 60 more days; you must keep paying current bills while it is in place. Third-party notification: designate a relative, friend or neighbor to receive copies of late and termination notices (they are not responsible for the bill) - useful for seniors who are away or need help with notices.
entries.notes: Winter moratorium December 1 - March 31: gas and electric utilities cannot terminate heat-related service without PUC approval for households at or below 250% of the federal poverty level (households above that income can be shut off). Rest of year, the utility must send a 10-day termination notice and attempt contact at least 3 days before shutoff (two phone tries, a home visit, or electronic contact if you agreed); a notice is valid for 60 days. During the moratorium, service is restored within 24 hours after you pay and meet conditions. Utilities must offer at least one payment arrangement and explain Customer Assistance Programs (CAPs). Contact the utility first; if unresolved, call the PUC Bureau of Consumer Services at 1-800-692-7380 (best for shutoff/termination cases) or file an informal complaint online. Rules: Title 66 Chapter 14 and 52 Pa.

entries.name: Puerto Rico Energy Bureau (Negociado de Energía, NEPR) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Junta Reglamentadora de Servicio Público de Puerto Rico
entries.service_area_detail: Regulates LUMA/PREPA and other electric service companies island-wide
entries.senior_programs: No elderly-specific shutoff protection is set out in the NEPR bill-review and suspension regulation. Households with a medical need for fans or air conditioning can use the ADSEF Energy Crisis program (bring a medical certificate) when facing shutoff.
entries.notes: You have 30 days from the bill date to pay, object to or request an investigation of a bill with the electric company (LUMA). To object, pay the average of your undisputed bills from the prior 6 months; service cannot be suspended over the disputed amount while the objection is pending. The company must answer within 30 days (investigation up to 60 days). You may ask the company to reconsider within 20 days of its decision, then request review by the Energy Bureau within 30 days of the final decision. Before shutoff the company must send a written warning at least 10 days ahead with the exact date. Service may never be cut on a Friday, Saturday, Sunday, holiday or the workday before a holiday. No seasonal or temperature-based moratorium. File with NEPR Secretaría: World Plaza Bldg., 268 Ave. Muñoz Rivera, Suite 202, San Juan; email nepr@jrsp.pr.gov. A separate regulation covers bills issued during emergencies when power was out (Law 143-2018).

entries.name: Puerto Rico LIHEAP - Programa de Subsidio y Crisis de Energía (ADSEF, Departamento de la Familia)
entries.parent_company: Puerto Rico Departamento de la Familia - Administración de Desarrollo Socioeconómico de la Familia (ADSEF)
entries.service_area_detail: Island-wide; apply at the local ADSEF office nearest your home
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window is published; benefits go first to the lowest-income households that spend a high share of income on electricity or fuel. The Crisis subprogram accepts a medical certificate when a household member needs fans or air conditioning for a health condition.
entries.notes: Federal LIHEAP in Puerto Rico has two parts: the Energy Subsidy (Subsidio de Energía, once a year) and the Energy Crisis subprogram (Crisis de Energía) for households facing an electric shutoff or lack of fuel. TANF households get the subsidy automatically and do not need to apply; others below the program's poverty-level income limit apply in person (head of household or spouse) at the nearest local ADSEF office. Each year when funds arrive the Departamento de la Familia announces the application period by press, radio and TV; applications are typically taken spring through September 30. You must go through the Subsidy first; Crisis is granted after the Subsidy. Bring: original Social Security card, pay stubs/employer letter/income certificate, and your latest electric bill (or last gas/kerosene receipt). For Crisis also bring the past-due suspension notice (aviso de suspensión) from the electric company, a certification of disconnection if service is already off, and a medical certificate if fans/AC are needed for health reasons. Crisis recipients must show how the benefit was used within 5 calendar days of payment. Civil-rights/discrimination complaints: 787-289-8009 (toll-free), ADSEF, P.O. Box 8000, San Juan, PR 00910-8000.

entries.name: Puerto Rico Weatherization Assistance Program - Programa de Climatización de Hogares (DDEC Programa de Política Pública Energética)
entries.parent_company: Puerto Rico Departamento de Desarrollo Económico y Comercio (DDEC) - Programa de Política Pública Energética (PPPE)
entries.service_area_detail: Island-wide; applications open during periods announced by DDEC
entries.senior_programs: Priority is given to families with dependent children up to age 19, elderly people and people with disabilities who also have high energy use.
entries.notes: Free home energy-efficiency upgrades (DOE WAP; 'Tu Casa Eficiente') for low-income homeowners or renters (with owner permission) who are responsible for the electric bill. Possible replacements: LED bulbs, refrigerators, air conditioners (up to 3), shower heads, electric water heaters to solar heaters, outlets, dryer vent kits. Income below 200% of poverty, or a household that received TANF, PAN (nutrition assistance) or LIHEAP in the past 12 months. Households on a flat-rate electric tariff are not eligible. Applicant must be 18+, U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Apply online through the link on the DDEC page during the application dates announced in DDEC public notices and newspapers. Documents: income proof (pay stubs, Social Security letter, tax returns), Social Security card copy, photo ID, proof of residence (lease, deed), and electric bill. Process: intake, eligibility, energy audit, installation, final inspection. Email: energia@ddec.pr.gov.

entries.name: Rhode Island Good Neighbor Energy Fund (United Way of Rhode Island)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide Rhode Island; applications through local Community Action (CAP) agencies
entries.notes: For Rhode Islanders in a temporary crisis who cannot pay a current energy bill and do not qualify for state/federal aid (income above LIHEAP limit and at or below 300% of poverty; 2025-26 limit about $46,950 for 1 person, $63,450 for 2). Paid directly to the company. Apply at a CAP agency; dial 2-1-1 to find yours. Bring photo ID, proof of income, household members, and current heating bill. Repeat help in a following year needs proof of extenuating hardship.

entries.name: Rhode Island LIHEAP - Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (Rhode Island Department of Human Services)
entries.parent_company: Rhode Island Department of Human Services (DHS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken by local Community Action Program (CAP) agencies
entries.senior_programs: CAP agencies will arrange for older adults and people with disabilities to apply at a convenient intake site. Households that got heating assistance last year are usually mailed renewal forms by their CAP agency, so keep your address current with the agency. LIHEAP recipients and all-62+ households also get winter shutoff protection from regulated gas and electric utilities.
entries.notes: Heating season applications typically open October 1 (most years taken September through May). Two parts: Heating Assistance (a grant paid to your utility or fuel dealer; roughly $50-$861) and Crisis Assistance (help when heat is shut off for nonpayment of a regulated bill, you cannot pay for delivered fuel, or the heating system fails and cannot be repaired; up to about $1,500). Income at or below 60% of Rhode Island median income; you do not need to be on public assistance or have an unpaid bill; renters and owners qualify. New applicants should apply in person at their local CAP agency, or apply online through the DHS client self-intake portal (requires verifying your email within 30 minutes). You can appeal a denial. Last-resort help: Good Neighbor Energy Fund (Salvation Army/United Way, up to $300 once per season for households over LIHEAP income limits), 401-421-0956.

entries.name: Rhode Island Medicaid Liens and Estate Recovery (EOHHS)
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Rhode Island regulation 210-RICR-10-00-4 covers Medicaid liens, recovery, discharge of liens and undue-hardship applications. EOHHS initiates estate recoveries on notice of a member's death. EOHHS main office 3 West Road, Cranston, RI 02920.

entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.

entries.name: Rhode Island Public Utilities Commission / Division of Public Utilities and Carriers - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Rhode Island Public Utilities Commission and Division of Public Utilities and Carriers
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers regulated electric, gas and water utilities (e.g., Rhode Island Energy); complaints handled by the Division's Consumer Section
entries.senior_programs: Households where all adults are 62 or older (including a single adult 62+) or where any resident is handicapped can register with the utility on its form (account number, address, names, birth dates; utility may ask for proof of age or a disability affidavit). The utility then cannot terminate without applying to the Division, which investigates whether proper notice was given and fair payment arrangements were offered. These households can also name a third person to receive copies of shutoff notices (that person is not liable for the bill). Serious illness: no disconnection while a resident is seriously ill as certified by a licensed physician (may start by phone; written certificate within 7 days); termination date must be at least 3 weeks after the written certificate, and you can ask the Division for an extension if the illness lasts longer.
entries.notes: Winter moratorium November 1 - May 1 (810-RICR-10-00-1): gas and electric utilities cannot shut off Protected Status Customers - elderly or handicapped, LIHEAP recipients, people receiving unemployment, the seriously ill, or households with a child under 2 and financial hardship. For other customers, no winter shutoff of primary heat unless the overdue balance is over $500 (over $200 if not the heat source). Summer: no residential shutoff for nonpayment on days with a National Weather Service heat advisory or excessive heat warning. Shutoffs cannot happen on Fridays, weekends, holidays or the day before a holiday. Call the utility first; if no satisfactory arrangement, call the Division of Public Utilities and Carriers Consumer Section at 401-780-9700 - service will not be cut off while a Division review is pending.

entries.name: South Carolina LIHEAP - Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) (South Carolina Office of Economic Opportunity)
entries.parent_company: South Carolina Office of Economic Opportunity (OEO), Department of Administration
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications taken only by county Community Action Agencies
entries.senior_programs: No statewide senior-only window; local Community Action Agencies set their own intake schedules and may set limits on how often a household is served. Ask the county agency about home-visit or phone intake if you cannot travel.
entries.notes: Heating help typically runs October through April, cooling April through September, and crisis help year-round while funds last (benefits roughly $200-$850 heating, $200-$775 cooling, up to $1,000 crisis). Income limit: 60% of state median income (about $31,993/year for 1 person, $41,837 for 2). Bring: proof of U.S. citizenship or qualified immigrant status for everyone in the household; government-issued ID showing South Carolina residence; gross income for the last 30 days for all household members 18+; and a current need such as an energy bill due (bill must be in an adult household member's name). LIHEAP does not pay water or sewer bills and is not meant to cover the full bill. Apply by contacting the Community Action Agency for your county (select your county on the OEO Find Help page).

entries.name: South Carolina Public Service Commission / Office of Regulatory Staff - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: South Carolina Public Service Commission (PSC) and Office of Regulatory Staff (ORS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers investor-owned electric, natural gas, water and wastewater utilities (e.g., Duke Energy, Dominion Energy SC); most electric co-ops and city-owned utilities are not covered
entries.senior_programs: Special needs accounts: a customer qualifies if a licensed health care provider (doctor, PA, nurse practitioner or APRN) certifies on the utility's form that losing electric service would be dangerous to the health of someone in the household, or certifies that the customer has Alzheimer's disease or dementia; utilities must follow special written termination procedures for these accounts (S.C. Code 58-27-2510 et seq.). December-March medical certificate (Reg. 103-352): no electric or gas termination if, at least 3 days before shutoff (or to the crew at the door), you give the utility a physician-signed certificate that loss of service would be especially dangerous to health, signed by you stating you cannot pay by installments; it lasts 30 days and can be renewed up to 3 more times. Ask your utility about third-party notification so a relative is told before a shutoff.
entries.notes: No fixed winter moratorium date; each electric utility must have written procedures that stop shutoffs during extremely cold or hot weather (standards set by the utility and filed with ORS). Electric service cannot be cut for nonpayment until 25 days after the billing date. Utilities must offer installment plans to customers with satisfactory payment history and refer others to social service agencies. Call the utility first; if unresolved, contact ORS Consumer Services at 1-800-922-1531 (or use its online complaint form) for an informal complaint before filing a formal complaint with the PSC (a formal complaint means a hearing).

entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency improvements for South Carolina residents who need help with home energy costs and meet the income limit (200% of the federal poverty level; see income table on the page). Apply through the Community Action Agency serving your county; if denied, you can request a fair hearing with the agency and then appeal in writing to OEO.

entries.name: South Dakota LIHEAP - Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) and Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP) (South Dakota Department of Social Services)
entries.parent_company: South Dakota Department of Social Services (DSS), Office of Energy Assistance
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications processed centrally by the DSS Office of Energy Assistance in Pierre (apply online, by mail, or email)
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior window; seniors apply with the same application. If you cannot complete it alone, call 1-800-233-8503 for help or ask at a local DSS office. Emergency calls outside office hours can leave a message with name, phone, and the emergency.
entries.notes: Helps pay home heating costs; payment goes directly to the energy supplier. Benefit is based on household size, income, heating type and cost, and location. Income limits are based on gross income for the 3 months before you apply (2025-26: $7,825 for 1 person, $10,575 for 2). Send: the application signed by every household member 18+; proof of all household income from the prior 3 calendar months (check stubs, award letters, tax return; self-employed send last year's full tax return); and proof of heating costs (recent bill or fill ticket, supplier statement, or landlord statement if heat is in rent). Apply online or print the application; scan, email (DSSHeat@state.sd.us) or mail proofs to SD DSS Office of Energy Assistance, 700 Governors Drive, Pierre, SD 57501. Processed within 60 days; check status at 1-800-233-8503 option 1. Crisis help (ECIP, April 1 - March 31): if income-eligible and you have a disconnect notice for your main heat, are on cash-on-delivery or refused delivery with under 20% in the tank, or face eviction for unpaid heat in rent, call 1-800-233-8503 or email the disconnect notice to DSSHeat@state.sd.us. Office hours 8 a.m.-5 p.m. CT weekdays.

entries.name: South Dakota Public Utilities Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; covers investor-owned electric, natural gas and telephone providers (e.g., Xcel, Black Hills, NorthWestern, MidAmerican); co-ops and municipal utilities generally not covered
entries.senior_programs: No age-based shutoff protection in South Dakota rules. Medical emergency (ARSD 20:10:20:11): the utility must postpone disconnection for 30 days from the date of a physician's certificate, or a notice from a public health or social services official, stating that disconnection would aggravate an existing medical emergency of the customer, a family member, or another permanent resident; limited to a single 30-day period.
entries.notes: Winter rule (ARSD 20:10:20:10): from November 1 to March 31 a regulated utility must add 30 extra days to the normal disconnection notice period and tell you before the normal shutoff date that you have 30 more days. There is no full winter moratorium or temperature rule. Contact the utility first; if unresolved, contact PUC Consumer Affairs at 605-773-3201 or 1-800-332-1782, email PUCConsumerInfo@state.sd.us, use the online informal complaint form, or mail SD PUC, 500 E. Capitol Ave., Pierre, SD 57501. Have your account number and say whether you are facing disconnection.

entries.notes: One-time help with heating and cooling bills, paid directly to the utility or fuel supplier (not to the applicant). Applications are taken online through THDA's SmartSimple portal; the season typically opens November 1 (heating Oct-Apr, cooling May-Sep, crisis help year-round while funds last). Benefits range from about $174 to $750 depending on energy burden; crisis help up to $750. Income limit: at or below 60% of State Median Income (see THDA income chart). If you need help applying, call the local LIHEAP agency for your county (contact list linked). Supporting forms are on THDA's LIHEAP forms page. THDA general line: 800-228-THDA (800-228-8432).

entries.name: Tennessee Public Utility Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for privately owned (investor-owned) electric, gas, water/wastewater and telecom companies; TVA power distributors, municipal utilities and co-ops are not regulated by TPUC
entries.senior_programs: Tennessee has no statewide age-based or medical-certificate shutoff rule for all utilities; each regulated utility's disconnection procedures (including extreme weather) must be approved by TPUC. Ask your utility directly about medical or elderly hardship options and payment arrangements.
entries.notes: No statewide winter or summer shutoff moratorium. Disconnection procedures in extreme weather are set by each utility and approved by TPUC. TPUC's Consumer Services Division mediates complaints against privately owned utilities (e.g., Piedmont Natural Gas, Atmos, Tennessee-American Water); file online or call 1-800-342-8359 or 615-741-2904 (email contact.tpuc@tn.gov). If your utility is a city utility, TVA distributor or electric co-op, contact that utility's board instead. 1220-04-04 (electric) and 1220-04-05 (gas). Before a shutoff, ask for a payment arrangement and apply for LIHEAP crisis help.

entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.
