entries.name: Texas Lifeline (telephone discount)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide Texas
entries.senior_programs: Qualify by income at or below 150% of poverty (1 person $23,940; 2 people $32,460) or receiving Medicaid, LIHEAP, SNAP, SSI, federal public housing, TANF and others.
entries.notes: Reduces the basic monthly phone rate by up to $12.75; does not cover extras like caller ID or voicemail. A Link-Up installation reduction may also be available. Apply by calling the Low Income Discount Administrator toll-free 1-866-454-8387 or download the application from the PUCT page. Find a Lifeline provider at cnm.universalservice.org. For help with an overdue phone bill, ask the provider about deferred payment plans or dial 2-1-1.

entries.name: Texas LIHEAP - Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (CEAP) (Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs)
entries.parent_company: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; administered through local subrecipient agencies covering all 254 counties
entries.senior_programs: Households with vulnerable members (including elderly and people with disabilities) receive priority status in benefit determination under 10 TAC 6.309. Income limit is the same for all ages.
entries.notes: CEAP is Texas's LIHEAP utility bill program; it runs year-round (no fixed season) while funds last and covers heating, cooling and crisis help (crisis up to about $1,800). Income limit: 150% of Federal Poverty Guidelines (2026: about $23,940/yr for 1 person, $32,460 for 2). Apply through the local agency for your city or county: use the 'Help for Texans' search on the TDHCA site and choose 'Utility Bill Payment Help'. Bring proof of income for all adults 18+, ID, and a recent utility bill. Payments go to the utility or fuel vendor.

entries.name: Texas Medicaid Estate Recovery Program (MERP)
entries.parent_company: Texas HHSC; administered by contractor Stellarware Corporation (from Sept 1, 2026)
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Case questions: Stellarware 800-641-9356 or Contact@TXMERP.com; program email merp@hhs.texas.gov. Undue hardship includes family business/farm and homestead under $150,000 with low-income heirs (Form 5006). Home maintenance and pre-nursing-home care costs can reduce the claim. After clearance letter, estate reps call TMHP Third Party Resources 800-846-7307. Request a hardship waiver with Form 5006, Application for Hardship Waiver. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Texas Office of the Attorney General Child Support Division
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide child support (and court-ordered spousal support processed through the state disbursement unit)
entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: How to Pay pages: online/phone, mail, cash (TouchPay kiosk locator https://csapps.oag.texas.gov/locations/kiosks), bank autodraft.

entries.name: Texas Public Utility Commission (PUCT) - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for retail electric providers in competitive areas, regulated electric utilities, local telephone, and many water/sewer utilities; municipal utilities and electric co-ops set their own disconnection rules; natural gas complaints go to the Railroad Commission of Texas
entries.senior_programs: Critical-care and chronic-condition protection: have your doctor complete the PUCT 'Application for Chronic Condition or Critical Care Residential Customer Status' and send it to your electric utility; registered customers get outage notices and added disconnection protections. If a resident would become seriously ill or more seriously ill from a shutoff, the provider cannot disconnect if you set up a deferred payment plan and the attending physician sends a written statement; this exemption lasts 63 days and can be requested again after the plan is fulfilled. No age-based (elderly-only) shutoff rule.
entries.notes: Weather protection (16 TAC 25.29): no disconnection for nonpayment during an extreme weather emergency - when the temperature is forecast at or below 32 F, or a heat advisory is in effect or was in effect in the prior two days; ask for a deferred payment plan for bills due during the emergency. Providers must send a written disconnection notice with at least 10 days before shutoff, and cannot disconnect if an energy assistance agency notifies them by the final due date that it is paying. First call your electric provider; if unresolved, file a complaint online or call 1-888-782-8477 (Austin 512-936-7120, TTY 1-800-735-2989). These rules do not apply to city-owned utilities or electric co-ops; contact them directly.

entries.notes: Free energy audit and installation of weatherization measures (air sealing, insulation, repair or replacement of inefficient equipment) plus energy education. Income limit: 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines for DOE-funded weatherization (150% for LIHEAP-funded). entries.notes: Plans billed monthly on the TXU bill: Tech Protect $15.95, Surge Protect Max $8.95, Plumbing Protect Ultra $9.95, MyHome Appliances Protect $18.95, A/C & Heat Protect $24.95, MyHome Systems Protect $33.95, MyHome Protect Ultra $43.95. entries.name: Accredited Debt Relief
entries.parent_company: Beyond Finance, LLC (Accredited Debt Relief is a Beyond Finance brand; private, for-profit)
entries.service_area_detail: Debt settlement/consolidation marketer; mailing P.O. Box 660442, Dallas, TX 75266-0442; not available in all states. Fees 15%-25% of enrolled debt.
entries.phone_customer_service: 1-800-497-1965 (client Support Team; Mon-Fri 8am-11pm, Sat-Sun 8am-10pm ET); corporate 800-282-7186
entries.mail_payment_address: Accredited Debt Relief, P.O. Box 660442, Dallas, TX 75266-0442 (general mailing address)
entries.payment_processor: independent third-party dedicated-account provider ($9.00 set-up + $9.75/month per FAQ; provider not named)
entries.senior_programs: Has a 'Seniors on Fixed Incomes' page in site navigation; no fee waivers.
entries.notes: Clients monitor progress via a personal client dashboard / mobile app with direct messaging (customer-service page) FAQ: 'every client program requires a dedicated account owned and controlled by the client and operated by an independent third-party provider'. Company says it never asks for payment upfront and won't message via Facebook - beware impostors. Change deposit/cancel by calling 800-497-1965. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/, and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general. ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint. Customer-service page re-read: clients reach support by phone 800-497-1965, mobile-app messaging or email 365 days a year; app gives 24/7 progress visibility.

entries.parent_company: Beyond Finance, LLC (private, for-profit debt settlement; also operates Accredited Debt Relief)
entries.service_area_detail: Debt settlement company (Houston, TX area); mailing P.O. Box 660442, Dallas, TX 75266-0442; not available in all states. Fees typically 15%-25% of enrolled debt.
entries.phone_customer_service: 1-800-282-7186 (Mon-Fri 7am-9pm CT, Sat-Sun 8:30am-5pm CT; live chat 24/7); fax 888-495-4207; new clients 800-495-4069
entries.mail_payment_address: Beyond Finance, P.O. Box 660442, Dallas, TX 75266-0442 (mailing address)
entries.payment_processor: third-party Dedicated Account provider (client-owned; provider not named on public pages)
entries.notes: Existing clients: 'Log into your Client Dashboard' (activation at beyondfinance.com/registration/new) or the Beyond Finance app. Contact page lists separate email boxes for Client Success, general documents, legal documents and complaints. FAQ: single monthly deposit into a Dedicated Account 'that you control... You own the account and the money in it'; fees only after an offer you approve and payments begin. To change the deposit or cancel, contact Client Success by phone or chat. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/, and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general. ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint. One monthly deposit into a Dedicated Account; Client Dashboard login at /registration/new and the Beyond Finance app (live chat).

Claims: https://carguardclaims.com/. customersupport@carguardadmin.com; fax (877) 683-9200. Cancellation/refund per contract; payments are usually made to the seller or its payment-plan company. SCAM WARNING: 'final notice - your vehicle warranty is expiring' robocalls and postcards are the classic senior-targeted pitch (FTC); sellers are usually not your dealer or manufacturer. Never give card or bank details to an unsolicited caller; check the contract administrator, cancellation/refund terms and 30-day free look before paying. Complaints: ReportFraud.ftc.gov or your state attorney general. Vehicle service contracts are often financed through third-party installment billers.

entries.notes: Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. entries.name: Council Law Group
entries.service_area_detail: Debt settlement company; not available in all states.
entries.notes: ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/, and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general.

entries.notes: Client login uses debtfreeportal.com. ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/, and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general.

Fees (https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-payment-fees-are-calculated-and-activating-free-payments/): ACH $2.99 or $3.99 may apply, cards typically 3-3.5% of the amount; free when paying from a linked bank account in the doxo Wallet; doxoPLUS $5.99/month (cancel: https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-can-i-cancel-my-doxoplus-subscription/). Scheduled payments can be edited/cancelled only before processing starts; after that ask the biller for a credit/refund. Support 1-855-791-9986, chat, Mon-Fri 5am-5pm PT (https://www.doxo.com/w/about/contact/). Some billers (e.g., National Grid) list doxo as a paperless/delivery option. Largest: National Grid (Massachusetts Electric Company) (MA); Intermountain Gas Company (ID); Mountaineer Gas Company (WV); Minnesota Power (MN); Montana-Dakota Utilities Co. (ND|SD|MT|WY); Suburban Water Systems (Nexus Water Group) (CA); Lower Bucks County Joint Municipal Authority (LBCJMA) (PA); Middleborough Gas & Electric Department (MG&E) (MA); Superior Water, Light & Power (SWL&P) (WI) Other useful doxo help: cancel doxoPLUS https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-can-i-cancel-my-doxoplus-subscription/; close doxo account https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-do-i-cancel-my-doxo-account/; disconnect a provider https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-do-i-disconnect-from-a-provider/; contact https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-can-i-contact-doxo-customer-service/; doxo biller directory FAQ https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/what-billers-can-i-pay-through-doxos-bill-pay-platform/; doxo's response to FTC https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/are-the-ftc-allegations-against-doxo-true/. Stipulated Order for Permanent Injunction and Monetary Judgment filed Aug 17, 2026; doxo to pay $2.1 million. Added: track a payment's delivery (Bills > biller > View Activity History; email receipt shows withdrawal and expected delivery dates) https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-do-i-track-delivery-of-my-payment-with-doxo/; cancel doxoPLUS subscription (doxoPLUS Subscription page > Manage Subscription > Cancel; access continues to end of cycle) https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-can-i-cancel-my-doxoplus-subscription/; close account https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/how-do-i-cancel-my-doxo-account/; which billers can be paid https://www.doxo.com/w/user-support/what-billers-can-i-pay-through-doxos-bill-pay-platform/. entries.name: EPPS (Electronic Payment Provider Services) - debt settlement dedicated accounts
entries.notes: Dedicated-account/payment processor used by some debt settlement and student-loan document-prep companies. Contact your debt relief company for the EPPS account statement and to stop drafts. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/, and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general. 'EPP' is also used generically for any electronic payment provider holding a dedicated account.

entries.service_area_detail: Large collector (Jacksonville, FL) for telecom/wireless, cable/satellite and utility creditors (e.g., AT&T, Comcast, DirecTV, DISH per third-party sources). CFPB complaints since 2023 (listed as 'ERC'): 589.
entries.mail_payment_address: Payments: ERC, P.O. Box 23870, Jacksonville, FL 32241-3870. Correspondence/disputes: ERC, P.O. Box 57610, Jacksonville, FL 32241.
entries.payment_processor: in-house Self-Service Portal (ssp.ercbpo.com); also Western Union Quick Collect (code city Domino, FL), PayNearMe and bank wire
entries.notes: ERC now publishes consumer help on ercglobalcx.com (Enhanced Resource Centers) The 'How to Make a Payment' FAQ  explains the Self-Service Portal at http://ssp.ercbpo.com (log in with the ERC reference/file number) with 'Pay Total Amount Due' or 'one time or multiple payments' (a payment schedule), plus mail, Western Union, PayNearMe and wire options. Disputes: online contact form or (800) 383-5979 per https://ercglobalcx.com/faqs/how-to-dispute-a-debt/; to stop a scheduled payment, call the same number. ERC is affiliated with TrueAccord. Scam check: never pay a caller you cannot verify - look up the collector's number yourself (not from the call/text), ask for the written validation notice, and compare with CFPB 'debt collector or scammer?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-can-i-tell-if-a-caller-is-a-debt-collector-or-a-scammer-en-1699/ and FTC 'Fake and abusive debt collectors' https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/fake-abusive-debt-collectors. Dispute/validation: under the FDCPA/Reg F you can dispute in writing within the 30-day validation period and the collector must pause collection until it sends verification (CFPB rights: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/debt-collection/answers/know-your-rights/ ). Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). Complaints: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/.

entries.name: EverBright, LLC
entries.service_area_detail: Solar lease/PPA/loan provider; EIA-861 rows IL/OH ~3,500, TX ~2,300, MD/NJ, CO
entries.notes: Once the system is in service you get an email invitation to register for MyEverBright (myeverbright.com), where you see the balance, make payments, check agreement, billing and payment details and chat with Homeowner Support (877-425-5201, Mon-Fri 9am-9pm ET, support@myeverbright.com). Selling your home (goeverbright.com/home-transfers): contact EverBright billing services at least 45 days before closing (everbright@youronlineaccount.com or (833) 353-0583). Retail installment/EverOwn customers can pay off the balance or transfer to a buyer who meets EverBright's credit criteria; PPA and lease customers can transfer to a qualifying buyer or ask about purchase options. The solar lease/PPA/loan bill is separate from the utility bill - you still get a (smaller) utility bill for delivery charges and grid power. Missing solar payments does not shut off electricity but can lead to late fees, collections and, for loans, a UCC-1 fixture filing on the equipment. A lease or PPA usually runs 20-25 years; when selling the home the options are transferring the contract to the buyer (buyer must qualify), prepaying/buying out, or as the contract allows. Watch for annual price escalators and loss of autopay discounts.

Scam check: never pay a caller you cannot verify - look up the collector's number yourself (not from the call/text), ask for the written validation notice, and compare with CFPB 'debt collector or scammer?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-can-i-tell-if-a-caller-is-a-debt-collector-or-a-scammer-en-1699/ and FTC 'Fake and abusive debt collectors' https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/fake-abusive-debt-collectors. Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). entries.notes: Consumer Help Hub FAQ: view account details and statements at client.forthpay.com or by calling 877-800-5577; to change payment date or amount, contact your debt relief service provider (DRSP) first because changes can affect pending settlements; banking-information updates go through your DRSP or FORTH (877-800-5577, clients@setforth.com). FORTH does not process ACH on bank holidays (schedule on the help hub). Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. entries.notes: ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/, and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general.

entries.name: InCharge Debt Solutions
entries.service_area_detail: Nationwide by phone/online; HQ 5750 Major Blvd, Suite 300, Orlando, FL 32819. NFCC member; UST-approved (as InCharge, personalfinanceeducation.com for bankruptcy courses).
entries.phone_customer_service: 1-888-734-6229 (Client Experience Specialist, existing accounts; Mon-Fri 8am-6pm ET); new counseling 1-800-565-8953
entries.senior_programs: Senior guidance article: https://www.incharge.org/debt-relief/financial-help-senior-citizens/; debt consolidation for seniors https://www.incharge.org/debt-relief/debt-consolidation/seniors/. DMP fees average $34/month plus one-time set-up fee averaging $52, varying by state.
entries.notes: Client Portal (my.incharge.org) - DMP page says clients 'can go online to review payments, update balances and track progress 24/7'. Deposit changes and stopping a draft: call Client Experience 888-734-6229. Cancel article: 'You can cancel anytime, for any reason. At InCharge Debt Solutions, you can cancel the debt management program with a phone call, email, fax or letter'; individual accounts can be removed by calling customer support. Bankruptcy course login is separate. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/. Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. A DMP is voluntary and can usually be cancelled or an account removed at any time by phone, email, fax or letter; creditors usually end concessions. Page lists (800) 565-8953 to discuss before cancelling.

entries.name: KUBRA (EZ-PAY / EZ-PAY+)
entries.service_area_detail: Bill presentment (iDoxs), payments (EZ-PAY), outage maps and notifications for large utilities, government and insurers in US/Canada
entries.notes: KUBRA does not take payments on its own site; pay via your service provider's EZ-PAY link. A guest one-time payment needs only your account number; payments show almost instantly with a confirmation number. For problems, contact the service provider. Support page (https://www.kubra.com/support) says contact your biller first, then KUBRA Consumer Support portal https://consumersupport.kubra.com/csp (JS-rendered). EZ-PAY+ (https://www.kubra.com/products-and-services/billing-and-payments/kubra-ez-pay) lets payers schedule, cancel and review payment history in the biller-branded wallet; supports card, ACH, PIN-less debit, Apple/Google Pay, cash at retail, natural-language IVR. No public biller directory. Platform does not hold the consumer's account; the biller owns bill view, autopay and history. Direct the senior to the biller's own portal. Largest: Xcel Energy - Colorado (Public Service Company of Colorado) (CO); Xcel Energy (Northern States Power Co - Minnesota) (MN|ND|SD); Eversource (Massachusetts) - NSTAR Electric (incl. former Western Massachusetts Electric) (MA); Xcel Energy - Colorado (Public Service Company of Colorado) (CO); Eversource (Connecticut) - formerly Connecticut Light & Power (CL&P) (CT); Washington Gas (DC|MD|VA); CPS Energy (TX); Tampa Electric (TECO) (FL); Xcel Energy (Northern States Power); gas (MN|ND|WI|MI); one-time payments need only the account number; biller sees the payment almost instantly, sometimes next business day; for problems, contact your service provider first, then the KUBRA Support Portal. No consumer phone is published. Pay through the service provider's site; OTP = guest one-time payment the provider authorized; payments usually visible immediately or within hours (sometimes next business day). KUBRA Support Portal https://consumersupport.kubra.com/csp?id=kubra_csp_index. No consumer phone published.

entries.name: Level Debt
entries.service_area_detail: Debt settlement company; not available in all states.
entries.notes: ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. entries.notes: For delinquent property taxes, ask the county tax office about senior/over-65 tax deferral or exemption programs before paying collection penalties. Social Security/SSI/VA benefits are generally protected from garnishment by private collectors (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-a-debt-collector-take-my-social-security-or-va-benefits-en-1157/ ). Complaints: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/.

entries.notes: 'My Account' portal (login.nationaldebtrelief.com) plus portal chat/Apple Messages for Business (Mon-Sat 8am-9pm ET). Fee charged to the Dedicated Account only after a settlement and at least one settlement payment; 'you can cancel anytime without any penalties or fees other than any fees earned associated with prior settled debts'. To change the monthly deposit or stop drafts, call the Client Success Team. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/, FTC https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/, and your state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general. ACDR-accredited member (https://acdr.org/member-list); ACDR also takes complaints about members at https://acdr.org/file-a-complaint. Contact page re-read: voice support Mon-Fri 9am-9pm, Sat 9am-6pm ET at 888-660-7427; portal chat and Apple Messages Mon-Sat 8am-9pm ET; success@nationaldebtrelief.com; My Account portal login.nationaldebtrelief.com.

A lease or PPA usually runs 20-25 years; when selling the home the options are transferring the contract to the buyer (buyer must qualify), prepaying/buying out, or as the contract allows. entries.notes: Manage/cancel through Allstate Protection Plans portal. SCAM WARNING: fake 'your protection plan / Geek Squad / Norton / Amazon renewal' emails and texts with an invoice and phone number are a top senior-targeted scam; real providers never ask you to call to 'cancel an auto-renewal' and then request remote access or gift cards. Debt-settlement safeguards (FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule): a for-profit debt relief company may not collect fees until it has settled at least one debt and you have made a payment under that settlement; money saved in the dedicated account is yours, and you can withdraw from the program at any time and get the account balance back (minus earned fees) within 7 business days. Settlement programs usually stop paying creditors while you save, so accounts become delinquent, may be sued, and forgiven amounts over $600 may be reported as taxable income. FTC guide: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-get-out-debt; CFPB: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-debt-relief-program-and-how-do-i-know-if-i-should-use-one-en-1457/. entries.name: Utah Division of Public Utilities / Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Utah Department of Commerce, Division of Public Utilities
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for utilities regulated by the Utah Public Service Commission (e.g., Rocky Mountain Power, Enbridge Gas); municipal utilities and most co-ops are not covered
entries.senior_programs: Medical protection: if you give the utility a physician's statement that a medical emergency exists in the home, service continues for 30 days or the time stated by the doctor, whichever is less; you may petition the Public Service Commission for more time. Tell the utility if anyone uses life-support equipment (oxygen, dialysis, respirator). Winter moratorium applicants who are 60+ or disabled must also have applied for utility help through the American Red Cross.
entries.notes: Winter moratorium (Utah Admin. Code R746-200): eligible households cannot be shut off by PSC-regulated utilities between November 15 and March 15 if they have a termination notice, have applied for HEAT, make a payment plan and pay in good faith, and meet one of: HEAT income-eligible, a recent medical or other emergency, job loss, or a 50% income drop. Apply for the moratorium through your local HEAT office. Utilities must give 10 days' written notice before shutoff (7 for telephone) and, October 1 - March 31, must make personal contact before disconnecting. If you have a problem, call the utility first; if unresolved, contact the Division of Public Utilities at 801-530-7622 or toll-free 1-800-874-0904, or file a complaint online.

entries.name: Utah LIHEAP - Home Energy Assistance Target (HEAT) Program (Utah Department of Workforce Services)
entries.parent_company: Utah Department of Workforce Services, Housing and Community Development
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications processed by eight local HEAT offices (associations of governments and community action agencies)
entries.senior_programs: Early application: households with an elderly member (60+), a disabled member, or a child under 6 can apply starting October 1; the general public starts November 1. Applicants 60+ or disabled seeking winter shutoff protection must also apply for utility help through the American Red Cross.
entries.notes: Program year runs October 1 - September 30 or until federal funds run out. Apply online (HEAT online application) or contact your local HEAT office to schedule an appointment; you can also mail, email or fax a paper application with documents to the local office. Income limit: at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level; household must pay home energy costs. Bring/send: copies of power and heat bills, proof of all household income for the month before you apply, proof of medical expenses/child support paid, and proof of disability if applicable. Crisis help: if you are in danger of shutoff, contact your local HEAT office for crisis assistance (available year-round). HEAT recipients can also ask about Rocky Mountain Power's HELP bill credit, Enbridge Gas's energy assistance credit, and a Weatherization referral. 1-866-205-4357 is the state line if you have a problem with the HEAT program.

entries.notes: ORS initiates recovery after death and may record liens on real property. Contact via ORS. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: Easy Ways to Pay page: MyChildSupport, TouchPay, military MyPay allotment, kiosk locations. Kiosk locations at /empowering-families/easy-ways-to-pay/kiosk-payment-locations/. No autopay instructions published.

entries.name: Virginia Judicial System - pay traffic tickets and court costs
entries.service_area_detail: State court system: traffic tickets, fines, court costs, restitution and payment plans (county/municipal courts may use their own portals)
entries.senior_programs: Each court has payment-plan policies for fines and costs (see Payment Plan Policies page). Beware text-message 'unpaid fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: General District Court payments: https://eapps.courts.state.va.us/gdcourts/landing.do?landing=landing; Circuit Court: https://eapps.courts.state.va.us/fmsOnline/#/searchHome. Circuit https://eapps.courts.state.va.us/fmsOnline/#/searchHome, General District https://eapps.courts.state.va.us/gdcourts/landing.do?landing=landing, J&DR https://eapps.courts.state.va.us/fmsOnline/#/searchHome?fips=000J; statewide case lookup (OCIS) shows amounts; questions go to the local court.

entries.name: Virginia LIHEAP - Energy Assistance Program (EAP) (Virginia Department of Social Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications through CommonHelp, the Enterprise Customer Service Center, or local departments of social services
entries.senior_programs: Cooling Assistance is only for households that include a vulnerable person: age 60+, living with a disability, or a child under 6. Fan Care (free fans for income-eligible people 60+ in Dominion Energy areas) is available through local Area Agencies on Aging (Virginia Department for Aging 1-800-552-3402).
entries.notes: Income limit for Fuel, Crisis and Cooling: gross monthly income at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level, and the household must have a heating or cooling expense. Fuel Assistance (heating costs): apply from the 2nd Tuesday of October to the 2nd Friday of November; eligibility notices are sent in late December. Crisis Assistance (no heat, cut-off notice, unsafe equipment): November 1 - March 15 for equipment repair/replacement and security deposits; January - March 15 for fuel and utility bills. Cooling Assistance: June 15 - August 17 (window AC units, AC/heat pump repair, electric bills or deposits). Apply online through CommonHelp, by phone at 855-635-4370 (Mon-Fri 7 AM-6 PM), with a paper application, or through your local department of social services. Dominion Energy and Appalachian Power customers who get EAP may qualify for the Percentage of Income Payment Program (PIPP), which caps electric bills as a share of income.

entries.name: Virginia Medicaid Estate Recovery (DMAS)
entries.parent_company: Virginia Department of Medical Assistance Services (DMAS)
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: DMAS Estate Recovery Fact Sheet (8/2022): claim filed against the estate; heirs who want to keep the home may contact DMAS to arrange other repayment options; undue-hardship waiver of all or part of claim, appeal within 30 days of denial. Fact sheet directs questions to the local department of social services; no direct unit phone published in it. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Virginia State Corporation Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC), Division of Public Utility Regulation
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for investor-owned electric and gas utilities, electric cooperatives, and regulated water/wastewater utilities; city-owned utilities are not covered
entries.senior_programs: Serious medical condition protection (20VAC5-330): tell the utility orally or in writing that you or a household member has a serious medical condition and termination is delayed 15 calendar days; with a Serious Medical Condition Certification Form (signed by a physician or nurse practitioner) on file, you can request an additional delay of at least 30 calendar days beyond the notice date. The utility may ask for a new form yearly or when the stated condition period ends. No age-based rule, but the temperature rules protect everyone.
entries.notes: Temperature rules (Va. Code 56-245.1:3): electric utilities cannot disconnect residential customers for nonpayment when the forecast low is 32 F or below, or the forecast is 92 F or above, within 24 hours after the scheduled shutoff; gas utilities cannot disconnect when the forecast low is 32 F or below; water/wastewater not when 92 F or above. No nonpayment disconnections on Fridays, weekends, state holidays, or the day before a state holiday. If facing disconnection, call the SCC immediately: 1-800-552-7945 or 804-371-9611, or file an online complaint (electric, gas, water or telephone). The SCC cannot help with propane/oil dealers or municipal utilities.

entries.name: Virginia Weatherization Assistance Program (Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development)
entries.parent_company: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local nonprofit providers by county/city
entries.senior_programs: Elderly and disabled households receive priority under federal weatherization rules; contact the local provider to be placed on its list.
entries.notes: Free home energy improvements: health and safety checks (carbon monoxide testing, smoke/CO alarms), air sealing, insulation, ventilation fans, duct repair, and repair or replacement of unsafe or inefficient heating and cooling systems. Income limits are posted by DHCD (generally 60% of State Median Income). Contact the local provider for the area WHERE THE HOME IS LOCATED to apply (provider listing by county).

entries.name: U.S. Virgin Islands LIHEAP - Energy Assistance (Department of Human Services, Division of Family Assistance)
entries.parent_company: U.S. Virgin Islands Department of Human Services
entries.service_area_detail: Territory-wide; DHS offices on St. Thomas, St. Croix and St. John
entries.senior_programs: DHS Division of Family Assistance also runs Aid for the Aged (OAA) and Aid to the Disabled cash programs; the Division of Senior Citizen Affairs serves residents 60+.
entries.notes: Energy Assistance (federal LIHEAP) is offered through the DHS Division of Family Assistance along with SNAP, TANF and aid for aged, blind and disabled residents. Program details and application periods are not posted online; call or visit a DHS office to ask about energy assistance and current funding: St. Thomas 340-774-0930, St. Croix (3012 Golden Rock, Christiansted) 340-718-2980, St. John (Cruz Bay) 340-776-6334.

entries.name: U.S. Virgin Islands Public Services Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: U.S. Virgin Islands Public Services Commission
entries.service_area_detail: Regulates WAPA electric and potable water, telephone, cable TV and ferry service
entries.senior_programs: No elderly- or medical-certificate shutoff protection is published by the PSC; ask WAPA directly about medical holds and payment arrangements, and file a PSC complaint if not resolved.
entries.notes: Complaint process: first contact the utility (e.g., WAPA). If not resolved within 30 days, contact the PSC; it is handled as an informal complaint. Send current and past bills and supporting documents within 5 business days of filing. PSC staff file the complaint with the utility, which must report its findings within 15 business days; PSC staff then work with both sides on a resolution. Download the complaint form from the PSC site and email it to psc.info@psc.vi.gov. Offices: St. Thomas, 1003 Estate Ross Ste 4 (340-776-1291); St. Croix, Estate Carlton Ste 1 & 2, Frederiksted (340-778-6010). No seasonal or temperature-based shutoff moratorium is published.

entries.name: U.S. Virgin Islands Weatherization Assistance Program (Virgin Islands Energy Office)
entries.service_area_detail: Territory-wide; offices on St. Thomas and St. Croix; owners and renters
entries.senior_programs: Applications are scored; points are added for household members in their sixties or older, disabled members, children under 5, energy bills over 20% of income and unusually high energy needs.
entries.notes: Free replacement of inefficient appliances and fixtures (ENERGY STAR refrigerator, air conditioner, water heater and timer, LED bulbs, low-flow shower heads and aerators, other approved items), worth $9,000+ if eligible. Household income must be below 200% of poverty (2026: $39,900 for 1 person, $54,100 for 2). Applications are typically accepted starting March 1. Submit copies (not originals) of proof of income, proof of ownership or occupancy, tax records and utility bills; incomplete applications are delayed. Application, eligibility flyer and priority item list are on the WAP page. Offices: St. Thomas, 8000 Nisky Center Ste 208 (340-714-8436); St. Croix, #2 Estate Carlton Ste 3, Frederiksted (340-713-8436). Email info@eo.vi.gov.

entries.senior_programs: Request an extension of time to pay (minimum $30 partial payment per complaint, max $100/month) using the Request for Extension of Time to Pay form. Beware text-message 'unpaid fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: Page says pay Judicial Bureau fines online via the Public Portal (Make Payments) within 21 days; overdue judgments go to collection agency AllianceOne; criminal fines by phone 802-652-1900. In person at 55 Railroad Row, White River Junction; email VJB@vtcourts.gov.

entries.name: Vermont LIHEAP - Seasonal Fuel Assistance and Crisis Fuel Assistance (Vermont Department for Children and Families)
entries.parent_company: Vermont Agency of Human Services, Department for Children and Families (DCF), Economic Services Division
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; seasonal fuel applications through DCF (online, mail or district offices); crisis fuel through local Community Action Agencies
entries.senior_programs: Crisis Fuel: if you are elderly or disabled and cannot apply in person, your Community Action Agency may take the application by phone. After-hours weekend/holiday 'out of fuel' help (1-866-331-7741, 8:30 AM-4 PM) is for households with a member 60+, under 6, or receiving federal disability. Statewide Senior Helpline: 1-800-642-5119.
entries.notes: Seasonal Fuel Assistance helps pay part of home heating bills for owners and renters (including heat included in rent). Income limit: 185% of the Federal Poverty Level. Prior-year recipients get an annual review form; new applicants apply online (myBenefits), by mail (call 1-800-479-6151 for a paper application), or at a DCF district office. Crisis Fuel Assistance (income up to 200% FPL) helps if you are out of fuel or facing disconnection: bulk-fuel households apply from the last Monday in November to the second Friday in April; metered (gas/electric) households through the last working day in April; apply in person at your local Community Action Agency (call first). Don't wait until the tank is empty. Furnace not working after hours: 1-877-295-7998. Utility discounts: Green Mountain Power, Vermont Gas (20% off) and some municipal electric systems offer income-based discounts at 185% FPL (call 1-800-775-0516).

entries.parent_company: Department of Vermont Health Access, Coordination of Benefits Unit
entries.mail_payment_address: Department of Vermont Health Access, Coordination of Benefits Unit, 280 State Drive, NOB 1 South, Waterbury, VT 05671-4020
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: DVHA Estate Recovery page: homestead undue-hardship exemptions (sibling/caregiver child in home; homestead under $250,000 with heir income <300% FPL or caregiving) with forms DVHA 13/14/15; paperwork to the Coordination of Benefits Unit; estate recovery contact 802-241-9343. DVHA main 802-879-5900; customer service 1-855-899-9600. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.notes: Separate portals for parents and employers; fees $5 card / $2 e-check. OCS site https://dcf.vermont.gov/ocs/.

entries.name: Vermont Public Utility Commission & Department of Public Service - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Vermont Department of Public Service / Vermont Public Utility Commission
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for regulated electric, gas and private water utilities
entries.senior_programs: Households with any member 62 or older: gas or electric service cannot be disconnected November 1 - March 31 when the temperature is forecast below 32 F during the 48 hours after the planned shutoff, if the account holder has given the utility advance written notice that the household qualifies (PUC Rule 3.300). Medical notes (Rule 3.302(B)(5)): a note from a doctor, nurse practitioner or physician assistant stating disconnection would be an immediate and serious health hazard stops disconnection for 30 days (includes a 7-day window to deliver the note); limited to two in a row and three per calendar year without Commission approval; if service is already off, a note gets it restored (within 24 hours). You still owe for usage.
entries.notes: Winter rule (PUC Rule 3.300): November 1 - March 31 gas and electric utilities may not disconnect when temperatures are forecast below 10 F during a 48-hour period starting on the disconnection date; extra protections apply for households with a member 62+. Disconnection is also not allowed if the past-due amount is $50 or less (limited use). You have the right to a reasonable payment arrangement (Rule 3.302(B)(6)). If you cannot reach a fair arrangement or have a dispute, call the Department of Public Service Consumer Affairs and Public Information (CAPI) at 1-800-622-4496 (7:45 AM-4:30 PM weekdays) first; formal complaints can also be filed with the Public Utility Commission through ePUC (Clerk 802-828-2358).

entries.name: Vermont Weatherization Assistance Program (Vermont Department for Children and Families)
entries.parent_company: Vermont Department for Children and Families, Office of Economic Opportunity
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by five regional weatherization agencies (Capstone, CVOEO, NETO, SEVCA, BROC)
entries.senior_programs: Households receiving SSI qualify automatically. Seasonal Fuel Assistance households are automatically eligible.
entries.notes: Free whole-house weatherization (energy assessment, insulation, air sealing; about $10,000 of work per home on average) for homes not weatherized by the program in the past 15 years. Eligible if income meets the program limits, or the household receives Seasonal Fuel Assistance, SSI, or Reach Up (past 12 months). To apply, find the agency serving your town (Central VT, Champlain Valley, Northeast VT, Southeast VT, Southwest VT), download its application, and send it to that agency.

entries.name: Washington LIHEAP - Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (Washington State Department of Commerce)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; applications by appointment through local LIHEAP provider agencies
entries.senior_programs: No separate senior-only LIHEAP benefit; many Washington utilities (e.g., Seattle City Light, Tacoma Public Utilities, Avista, Benton PUD) offer separate low-income senior and disability bill discounts, often enrolled through the same local agencies.
entries.notes: One-time heating grant (cooling services are also available) paid directly to the energy provider; can also help repair or replace an unsafe or broken heating/cooling system. Any fuel type (electric, gas, propane, oil, coal, wood). Income limit: 150% of the Federal Poverty Level. Apply once per program year (October 1 - September 30) by scheduling an appointment with the LIHEAP provider in your community (use the provider map; Commerce does not schedule appointments). Bring proof of identity, residence, heat costs and income. Crisis help is handled by the same local agencies. Commerce LIHEAP line: 360-725-2857 (LIHEAP@commerce.wa.gov).

entries.name: Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide for investor-owned utilities (e.g., Puget Sound Energy, Avista, Pacific Power, Cascade Natural Gas, NW Natural); PUDs and city utilities follow RCW 54.16.285 / local rules and are not handled by UTC complaints
entries.senior_programs: Medical emergency (WAC 480-100-128 electric; 480-90-128 gas): a qualified medical professional's certification that disconnection would aggravate an existing medical condition stops a shutoff; it lasts as long as certified but no more than 60 days unless renewed. Within a 5-business-day grace period the utility may require payment of 10% of the past-due balance and a plan for the rest. If the customer is known to depend on a third party (e.g., DSHS) for their affairs, the utility must notify that party and delay disconnection at least 5 business days.
entries.notes: Winter low-income payment program (WAC 480-100-143): November 15 - March 15 a utility may not shut off residential space heating if you tell the utility you can't pay, have a local energy assistance agency confirm you are income-eligible, apply for energy assistance, and agree to pay no more than 7% of household income monthly plus a share of past-due bills (past-due balance must be paid by October 15). Heat alerts (RCW 80.28.010): electric and water utilities may not disconnect residential customers on any day the National Weather Service has issued or announced a heat-related alert (heat advisory, excessive heat warning/watch) for the area, and must reconnect on request. Disconnection notices must mention the winter payment plan. For help, call the UTC consumer line 1-888-333-9882 (closed Tuesdays and Thursdays; 9 AM-12:30 PM and 1:30-4 PM), email consumer@utc.wa.gov, or file a complaint online.

entries.name: Washington Weatherization Assistance Program (Washington State Department of Commerce)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; delivered by local weatherization agencies by county
entries.senior_programs: Elderly and disabled households receive priority under federal weatherization rules; ask the local agency about wait times.
entries.notes: Free energy-efficiency and health-and-safety upgrades for homeowners and renters: insulation, air sealing, LED lighting, smoke/CO detectors, hot water and heating system checks, and fixes for combustion, mold, asbestos or lead hazards. Not a window replacement program. Income limit generally 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (see Commerce eligibility guidelines). Commerce does not accept applications; apply with your county's local weatherization agency (e.g., King County Housing Authority 206-214-1240; Kitsap Community Resources 360-473-2045; CAC of Lewis, Mason, Thurston 1-800-878-5235).

entries.name: American Financial Solutions (AFS)
entries.parent_company: American Financial Solutions of North Seattle Community College Foundation (nonprofit)
entries.service_area_detail: Seattle area (Bremerton/Seattle, WA); nationwide by phone. NFCC member; UST-approved.
entries.notes: Client Login goes to myafsaccount.com. Call for deposit changes or cancellation. Complaints/escalation: ask the agency for a supervisor first; then CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and your state attorney general (directory: https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general ); many states also license debt-management providers through the state banking/financial regulator. Background: CFPB 'What is credit counseling?' https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-credit-counseling-en-1451/. Stopping a DMP: you can usually cancel at any time, but creditors typically restore original interest rates/terms once payments stop coming through the plan - keep paying creditors directly so accounts do not go delinquent. The FAQ page shows (888) 864-8548 - either reaches AFS. FAQ does not describe draft changes or cancellation; call.

entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; county and tribal local agencies
entries.senior_programs: Wisconsin bars winter disconnection of occupied homes Nov 1-Apr 15, which protects seniors on fixed incomes.
entries.notes: Helps with heating and electric bills (regular benefit) plus crisis assistance for emergencies such as a disconnect notice or running out of fuel. Applications typically taken October 1 to May 15. Apply online, through your county/tribal local agency, or call 1-866-HEATWIS (1-866-432-8947). Income limit 60% of state median income (2026-27: $3,322/month for 1 person). Related: emergency furnace repair/replacement program.

Call the utility first; then file a complaint online, by mail (PSC, P.O. Box 7854, Madison, WI 53707-7854) or by phone 1-800-225-7729 (608-266-2001), Mon-Fri 7:45 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Rules: Wis. Code PSC 113 (electric) and PSC 134 (gas).

entries.senior_programs: Households with elderly or disabled members are a federal priority group.
entries.notes: Free insulation, air sealing and heating system work for income-eligible homeowners and renters. Households approved for WHEAP energy assistance are referred automatically; otherwise contact the local agency or call 1-866-HEATWIS.

Site offers one-on-one debt management counseling and housing counseling; call 800-350-2227. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general.

entries.name: Consumer Credit Counseling Service of the Mid-Ohio Valley, Inc.
entries.service_area_detail: HQ Parkersburg, WV; UST-approved for: Ohio, West Virginia
entries.notes: NFCC member agency. Approved by the U.S. Trustee Program to give pre-bankruptcy credit counseling. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general.

entries.name: West Virginia Bureau for Child Support Enforcement (BCSE)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide child support (and court-ordered spousal support processed through the state disbursement unit)
entries.mail_payment_address: Bureau for Child Support Enforcement, P.O. Box 247, Charleston, WV 25321
entries.payment_processor: SMART e-Pay (wv.smartchildsupport.com): one-time or recurring bank draft free; card 2.5%
entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: SMART portal (wv.smartchildsupport.com) offers one-time or recurring bank drafts with no fee; card 2.5%. Corrected pay-by-phone to 1-855-303-4094 as shown on the page.

entries.name: West Virginia Judiciary - Payments
entries.service_area_detail: State court system: traffic tickets, fines, court costs, restitution and payment plans (county/municipal courts may use their own portals)
entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.

entries.name: West Virginia LIHEAP - Low Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) (WV Department of Human Services)
entries.parent_company: West Virginia Department of Human Services, Bureau for Family Assistance
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; apply online, at county DoHS field offices, Community Action agencies or Area Agencies on Aging
entries.senior_programs: Regional Agency on Aging offices take applications. Seniors 60+ receiving SNAP, SSI or WV WORKS may also get the 20% Special Reduced Residential Rate on gas and electric bills November-March (ask the utility). Furnace repair/replacement help is limited to households with someone disabled, 60+, or a child 5 or younger.
entries.notes: Helps pay the primary heating bill. Opens for a short time each winter, usually starting with a mail-out to past recipients; online applications through WV PATH open about early February in recent years (heating component runs into September in FY2026). Emergency LIEAP (crisis) helps households facing loss of heat; its opening date is announced separately. Income limit is 60% of state median income (FY2026 about $2,454/month for 1 person). Ask for a fair hearing within 60 days if denied.

entries.name: West Virginia Medicaid Estate Recovery (WV Recovery Unit / BMS)
entries.parent_company: West Virginia Bureau for Medical Services (WV Recovery Unit run by HMS/Gainwell)
entries.mail_payment_address: WV Recovery Unit, Bureau for Medical Services, 1201 B Greenbrier St., Charleston, WV 25311
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim notice; exemptions (surviving spouse, child under 21, blind/disabled child) and undue-hardship waivers are available.
entries.notes: WV Recovery Unit site (HMS for BMS): estate claims filed in probate; Estate Recovery Brochure and Hardship Waiver Guidelines PDFs linked (hardship may waive or delay recovery). Third Party call center (877) 598-5820. Family members can request a hardship waiver so recovery is waived or delayed (Hardship Waiver Guidelines on the page). Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: West Virginia Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.parent_company: Public Service Commission of West Virginia
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; electric, gas, landline phone and most water/sewer utilities (not most municipal utility rates, cell or internet)
entries.senior_programs: Gas and electric customers 60+ who receive SSI, WV WORKS or SNAP get a 20% Special Reduced Residential Rate November-March. Utilities must make extra contact attempts before disconnecting when a medical condition is on record.
entries.notes: Call your utility first; if unresolved, file an informal complaint online or by phone with PSC Consumer Affairs (1-800-642-8544, weekdays 8 a.m.-5 p.m.); most are resolved within 30 days. Shutoff rules: no disconnection when the temperature is 32 degrees F or below; in winter months and when a medical condition is present, the utility must make 3 additional contact attempts before disconnecting. Rules are posted by the Secretary of State (PSC rules list).

entries.name: West Virginia Utility Assistance Program (Dollar Energy Fund) - gas, electric and water
entries.service_area_detail: Customers of participating West Virginia gas, electric and water utilities
entries.notes: One-time grant applied directly to a gas, electric or water bill for West Virginians, including those who do not qualify for LIEAP. Apply through a local intake agency (often the Salvation Army) found with the Agency Finder, or call 1-888-282-6816.

entries.name: West Virginia Weatherization Assistance Program (WV Community Advancement and Development)
entries.parent_company: West Virginia Department of Economic Development, Community Advancement and Development (CAD)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide through regional weatherization providers
entries.senior_programs: Elderly (60+) and people with disabilities get priority.
entries.notes: Free insulation, air sealing, heating system repair and A/C maintenance after an energy audit. Income limits from about $29,160 for 1 person to $101,120 for 8; automatically eligible with SSI or TANF. Find your county's provider on the map, then apply with that agency.

entries.name: Consumer Credit Counseling Service of Huntington (Goodwill Industries of KYOWVA Area)
entries.parent_company: Goodwill Industries of KYOWVA Area, Inc.
entries.service_area_detail: Huntington, WV tri-state area; 1102 Memorial Blvd, Huntington, WV 25701
entries.notes: NFCC member; a division of Goodwill Industries of KYOWVA. Debt Management Plan for credit card and medical debt over 3-5 years; sign in or register at cccsgoodwillhunting.fincocms.org. No public instructions for changing or stopping the monthly deposit - call 304-522-4321. Complaints: CFPB https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/ and state attorney general https://www.usa.gov/state-attorney-general.

entries.name: Wyoming Child Support Program
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide child support (and court-ordered spousal support processed through the state disbursement unit)
entries.mail_payment_address: Wyoming Department of Family Services, State of Wyoming Disbursement Unit, 2300 Capitol Avenue, Hathaway Bldg 5th Floor Suite A, Cheyenne, WY 82002
entries.payment_processor: Value Payment Systems (childsupportbillpay.com/Payment/SelectEntity/759; card 2.49% min $4.95, e-check $1); ExpertPay; PayNearMe ($1.99 at Family Dollar/CVS/ACE/7-Eleven)
entries.senior_programs: Not a senior program. Grandparents/relative caregivers raising grandchildren can apply for child support services; arrears on old cases can still be collected from Social Security retirement/SSDI via income withholding.
entries.notes: No autopay or history instructions published.

entries.name: Wyoming Judicial Branch - Payments
entries.service_area_detail: State court system: traffic tickets, fines, court costs, restitution and payment plans (county/municipal courts may use their own portals)
entries.senior_programs: Most courts allow payment plans or ability-to-pay reductions; ask the clerk. Beware text-message 'unpaid toll/court fine' scams - use only the official court site.
entries.notes: Supreme Court fees via LexisNexis; court warns of scammers demanding bond payments via payment apps - call the local court.

entries.name: Wyoming LIHEAP - Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP) (Wyoming Department of Family Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide
entries.senior_programs: Staff will take an application over the phone (1-800-246-4221), useful for seniors without internet.
entries.notes: Seasonal heating help and crisis help, October 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027. Crisis help covers shut-off notices, utility deposits, broken furnaces and running out of fuel; you must show at least one payment to the utility in the past 60 days. Income at or below 60% of state median income. Apply online (MYLIEAPWYO.ORG), by phone, or by mail to LIEAP, PO Box 827, Cheyenne, WY 82003. Email lieapinfo@wyo.gov. Energy Share of Wyoming (307-772-9100) helps people who don't qualify, Dec 1-Apr 30, up to $500 once per season.

entries.name: Wyoming Medicaid Estate Recovery
entries.mail_payment_address: Wyoming Department of Health, Division of Healthcare Financing (Program Integrity Unit), 122 W. 25th Street, 4th Floor West, Cheyenne, WY 82002
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid estate recovery claim against a deceased member's estate (age 55+ long-term care/HCBS and related costs). Heirs and estate representatives receive the claim letter; payments, hardship waivers and deferrals are handled by this unit.
entries.notes: Undue-hardship waiver reviewed only after the client dies (Chapter 35 Medicaid rules); liens must be paid before property is sold or transferred. LTC eligibility: Long Term Care Processing Unit (855) 203-2936. Estate recovery is a one-time claim against the deceased member's estate, not a monthly bill: the estate representative pays by check to the address in the claim letter, and there is no automatic or recurring payment option.

entries.name: Wyoming Public Service Commission - consumer complaints & utility shutoff protections
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; investor-owned electric, gas and water utilities and co-ops (not city-owned utilities inside city limits, cell or internet)
entries.senior_programs: Wyoming PSC rules include extra disconnection protections for elderly and handicapped customers; tell the utility if someone in the home is elderly, disabled or has a medical condition.
entries.notes: No disconnection when the temperature is forecast to be below 32 degrees F in the next 48 hours. File a complaint by online form, email wpsc_complaints@wyo.gov, phone 1-888-570-9905 (307-777-7427), or mail to WPSC Complaint Staff, 2515 Warren Ave., Suite 300, Cheyenne, WY 82002. The utility must respond and PSC staff work toward resolution; you can then request a formal hearing. Rules: PSC Chapter 3 (rules and statutes page).

entries.name: Wyoming Weatherization Assistance Program (Wyoming Department of Family Services)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide
entries.senior_programs: Elderly and disabled households are federal priority groups.
entries.notes: Free home energy improvements for income-eligible households; contact DFS for the local provider.
